title: Texans are resisting trade interest in players like Jadeveon Clowney
summary: It's the same story every year.
full_text: It's the same story every year. Teams don't make final decisions as to whether they'll be buyers, sellers, or bystanders at the trade deadline until the last bit of hay is in the barn before the clock strikes 4:00 p.m. ET on the day the window closes. As noted on Sunday morning by Mike Garafolo of NFL Network, the 2-5 Texans have received calls regarding teams that have interest in raiding the roster. The one name mentioned by Garafolo was veteran pass rusher Jadeveon Clowney. The Texans, however, are waiting to see what happens today. A win over the Chargers in L.A. would move the Texans to 3-5. With a win in hand over the Jaguars and a rematch coming in Week 15, the Texans would still have a chance to catch Jacksonville for the AFC South crown. A loss to the Chargers would change everything. Beyond falling to 2-6, the Texans will have lost to the lowly Chargers, this year's official Sixth Sense team that doesn't yet know it's dead. If the Texans lose, the calls will surely intensify — and G.M. Nick Caserio will have some decisions to make. Clowney surely would welcome the chance to land with a contender. He picked the Texans in large part because he believed they could win the Super Bowl .
author: Mike Florio

title: Mike Vick, Norfolk State lose after his order was ignored
summary: Like a growing number of former NFL players, Mike Vick has become a college football coach.
full_text: ''' Like a growing number of former NFL players, Mike Vick has become a college football coach. Unlike many college football coaches, a direct order from Vick wasn't followed on Saturday. It turned a likely win into a loss. With 1:34 to play during Saturday's game between Vick's Norfolk State and North Carolina Central, Norfolk State led, 28-23. Norfolk State had the ball, facing second and five from the 50. North Carolina Central had no timeouts remaining. While a pair of knees wouldn't have fully exhausted the remaining time, Vick told the offense to take a knee in victory formation. Two straight kneel-downs would have resulted in a punt with less than 15 seconds to play. Instead, Norfolk State lined up in shotgun formation, the quarterback ran to the left, a defender hit him, and the quarterback fumbled. North Carolina Central recovered at the Norfolk State 37. Five plays later, North Carolina scored a touchdown, on a 26-yard touchdown pass, making the score 29-28. (The two-point conversion attempt failed.) Twenty-seven seconds remained. Norfolk State drove in position to attempt a game-winning field goal. The 37-yard try missed wide left. “I don't know what happened at the end of the game," Vick told reporters after a loss that dropped Norfolk State to 4-6 on the season. "I put my headset down. I called victory formation. All we had to do was take a knee, kneel the clock out. That’s just situational football. I don’t know what happened in regards to that. I looked up and we was running the ball, and then I seen the fumble. But my final instructions was victory formation. That’s when you kneel it out. And they had, I think, zero timeouts left and the game was over practically." "Well, I put my headset down, and I took my headset off because all we had to do was just run it three times, or two times, or kneel it out. That's called victory. I don't know what happened. A run play was called. I looked up, I seen us running the ball. I don't know what happened. I really don't. I don't know what the play call was. I don't know why we even ran that play. “People will look at that, and that’ll go on as a teaching tape for a lot of teams across the country for years to come. I hate it had to be us. But I called victory formation. Just letting everybody know that. I called victory.” While the strategy wouldn't have completely exhausted the clock, it was the right move. And, even if it wasn't, the coach gave the order. The order wasn't followed. So what happened? Vick said he had taken off his headset and then later realized that a run play had been called. The fact that the offense went straight into shotgun formation suggests that it wasn't the players going rogue. Apparently, offensive coordinator Brian Sheppard decided to ignore Vick's directive. Indeed, a somewhat chaotic postgame video (posted by Vick on Twitter) includes Vick telling his players "it was supposed to have been victory ." The video of the moments before the play in question shows the offense gathered at the numbers near the Norfolk State bench, speaking to a group of coaches who were still wearing headsets. The coach without a headset (who appears to be Vick) walked to the sideline before turning around and returning to the meeting. It's clear that the coaches and players were having a discussion. From Vick's perspective, there was nothing to discuss. And while Vick claims his instruction was ignored, he seemed to be a little too nonchalant at a time when he should have realized that something more detailed than telling the quarterback to line up under center, receive the snap, and take a knee was being planned. If Vick believes Sheppard or other coaches overruled the head coach, Vick should be issuing pink slips immediately. It's possible, though, that Vick himself bears the bulk of the blame for not noticing that something other than the implementation of victory formation was coming.
author: Mike Florio

title: Hall of Fame LB Jack Ham hospitalized after medical emergency at Penn State game
summary: Hall of Fame linebacker Jack Ham, who now serves as a radio analyst for Penn State football, was hospitalized in Seattle on Saturday after experiencing a medical emergency.
full_text: Hall of Fame linebacker Jack Ham, who now serves as a radio analyst for Penn State football, was hospitalized in Seattle on Saturday after experiencing a medical emergency. Penn State coach Matt Campbell said after the 28-25 win over Washington that Ham was assisted by play-by-play announcer Steve Jones. "If it's not for Steve, what he did, I don’t know if we have as good a news as we do right now," Campbell said, via Adam Rittenberg of ESPN. Campbell added that Jones's efforts to save Ham were "heroic." Ham is in stable condition. Ham, 77, has served as the Penn State radio analyst since 2000. He won four Super Bowls, made eight straight Pro Bowls, and was named first-team All-Pro six consecutive times in a 12-year career with the Steelers. Ham was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1988, after retiring from football in 1982.
author: Mike Florio

title: Deion Sanders says Colorado deserves better after falling to 3-6
summary: Colorado lost again on Saturday night, and afterward head coach Deion Sanders said he knows his team isn't good enough.
full_text: ' Colorado lost again on Saturday night, and afterward head coach Deion Sanders said he knows his team isn't good enough. Saturday's 20-10 loss to Arizona State dropped Colorado to 3-6 this season, and dropped Sanders to 19-27 in four years as Colorado's head coach. "The season doesn't look good," Sanders said afterward. "It doesn't look good. I'm not crazy. I can see clearly. You think I'm happy? I'm not happy with the outcomes. I'm not a loser by any means, and I hate the fact that we're coming up on the short end of these games." Sanders said he feels for Colorado fans and players because he doesn't think he has done enough to put them in a position to win. "It's not a personal hurt for me, I hurt because you guys deserve better and the team deserves better. We should win. We should put our best foot forward. And I'm not seeing that," Sanders said. Sanders ran through the stats from the game and then said his team hadn't played well enough. "The fan base deserves better. They really do," Sanders said. Ultimately, Sanders says, it's on him to coach better. "We've just got to do better," Sanders said. "And that starts with me."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Report: Colts have told teams they were offered a fourth-round pick for Josh Downs
summary: A third-round pick appears to be what the Colts are trying to get to trade Downs.
full_text: '' The Colts are putting out word to the rest of the league that if you want to trade for wide receiver Josh Downs, you'll need to beat an offer of a fourth-round pick. Indianapolis has told other teams that it received an offer of a fourth for Downs, according to ESPN. Downs has asked the Colts to trade him , and the Colts would seem likely to be willing to grant that request, given that he's in the final year of his rookie contract and they have already traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner and have had trade talks about other players. Downs was a third-round pick in 2023 and leads the Colts with 330 receiving yards this season. The Colts could also try to trade wide receiver Keenan Allen, who's second on the team with 325 receiving yards this season, as they attempt to move on from a miserable 2026 season and start to focus on building for 2027 and beyond.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Cam Jordan will become third defensive player to play 250 games with same team
summary: When the Saints host the Browns on Sunday, New Orleans defensive end Cam Jordan will reach a rare milestone.
full_text: ' When the Saints host the Browns on Sunday, New Orleans defensive end Cam Jordan will reach a rare milestone. The Week 9 game will be Jordan's 250th. Via NBC Sports research, Jordan will become only the third defensive player in NFL history to play 250 or more games with the same team. The others are Darrell Green, who played 295 games for Washington from 1983 through 2002, and Jim Marshall, who played 270 games for the Vikings from 1961 through 1979. Jordan, the son of former Vikings tight end Steve Jordan, was a first-round pick in 2011. His dad played in 176 games from 1982 through 1994. Cam is an eight-time Pro Bowler, with 132.0 career sacks. He's currently 22nd on the all-time list.
author: Mike Florio

title: Player Personnel Handbook implies that the NFL can delay (or deny) Brandon Aiyuk's reinstatement
summary: The CBA is silent on the issue.
full_text: '' Until very recently, people throughout the league believed that the procedure for returning from the reserve/left squad list was administrative, and essentially automatic. The Brandon Aiyuk case shows that, in the NFL's view, it definitely is not. The Collective Bargaining Agreement is silent on the topic of the reserve/left squad list. The relevant language regarding placement (and eventual reinstatement) from the reserve/left squad list appears in the NFL's Player Personnel Handbook. In the year when the player is placed on reserve/left squad, he can't play for his current team or any other team. His season is basically over. The window for reinstatement opens the next year. Here's the key language from the Player Personnel Handbook regarding reinstatement: "A player on Reserve/Left Squad must apply to the Commissioner for reinstatement to his club's Active List. No player on Reserve/Left Squad shall be reinstated in the same season in which he is placed on Reserve. A player applying for reinstatement in a season subsequent to the season in which he is placed on Reserve/Left Squad is prohibited from being reinstated in the last 30 days of the regular season or thereafter during the postseason, and no such player will be reinstated during the period between the trading deadline of a subsequent season and the 30-day deadline unless the club initiates the reinstatement request and the Commissioner approves it." While the provision doesn't say it expressly, the language implies that the Commissioner has apparently unlimited discretion when it comes to approving the application to reinstate the player. In Aiyuk's case, the Commissioner has dragged his feet since October 27, setting the stage for an apparent effort by the 49ers to leverage Aiyuk's desire to be reinstated to his willingness to reimburse up to $13 million in previously-paid bonus money. The NFL Players Association has remained silent throughout the process, and perhaps for good reason. The absence of any provision in the CBA regarding the mechanics of the reserve/left squad list arguably means that the situation falls within the NFL's "management rights" clause, which allows the various teams "to manage and direct their operations in any manner whatsoever, except as specifically limited by the provisions of this Agreement." With no limitations in the CBA as to the operation of the reserve/left squad list (or reinstatement from it), the NFLPA may be without options. Precedent becomes relevant to the overall analysis. How has the league handled past requests for reinstatement from the reserve/left squad list? If the league has previously not delayed reinstatement (for whatever reason), there's an argument to be made that it should not be delayed as to Aiyuk. Regardless, it's becoming increasingly obvious that the NFL and the 49ers are working together to tie Aiyuk's reinstatement to his satisfaction of the debt that the 49ers believe Aiyuk has incurred through his prior default under his contract. It should be two separate issues, with the 49ers having the ability to pursue the recovery of bonus money from Aiyuk and Aiyuk having the ability to be reinstated. By tying the two together, the 49ers have found a way to condition Aiyuk's reinstatement on his willingness to wire a significant payment to the 49ers. Can the NFL and the 49ers do that? For now, they are. The question is whether Aiyuk and/or the NFLPA can come up with a legal argument against the obvious effort to block Aiyuk's return until he returns millions to the 49ers. If Aiyuk wants to be reinstated quickly, his best (and perhaps only) play will be to return millions to the 49ers, with the ensuing goal of earning it back as his career continues elsewhere.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Colts are in trade talks regarding QB Daniel Jones
summary: The list of "multiple teams" currently includes the Ravens (who pivoted elsewhere) and the Vikings.
full_text: '' The Indianapolis fire sale could indeed extend to the man who was supposed to become a franchise quarterback there. According to ESPNFL, the Colts have engaged in trade talks this week regarding Daniel Jones, speaking to "multiple teams." The precise language of the report identifies only one team as actually talking to the Colts. From the article, the Ravens "were one team to check in on Jones." The Ravens ultimately struck a deal with the Cardinals for quarterback Jacoby Brissett, whose plunge from No. 1 to No. 3 on the depth chart made it clear to the rest of the league that he was available. The only other team mentioned by name is the Vikings, and the report points only to "[s]peculation" involving Minnesota. (We've been “speculating” about it since the immediate aftermath of Sunday's loss by the Vikings in Detroit.) Past ESPNFL reporting on a potential trade for running back Jonathan Taylor ultimately listed five teams as talking to the Colts (Giants, Seahawks, Broncos, Packers, Vikings). The fact that other teams weren't mentioned as to Jones suggests that, frankly, there may not be other teams. Really, which current contender would want him? The Vikings are the only potential playoff team that checks the box as possibly needing a starter right now. And only the Vikings and Giants are contenders with which Jones has direct experience. (The Giants wouldn't want a Jones reunion, and Jones surely wouldn't want it, either.) That could change this weekend, obviously. One injury to a starter could alter the dynamics, spurring another contender to pick up the phone and make a push for Jones. The most memorable example of that came 15 years ago, when a broken collarbone to Raiders quarterback Jason Campbell prompted a quick deal for Bengals quarterback Carson Palmer, who had decided he didn't want to play for the team that had drafted him — and who had yet to report. Three years ago, Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins popped an Achilles tendon two days before the deadline, forcing the Vikings to scramble at the deadline to do a deal with the Cardinals for quarterback Josh Dobbs. Absent a multi-week injury to a starting quarterback on a contender that doesn't believe its backup can hold down the fort, the Vikings may be the only team that wants Jones at the deadline. The preferences of Daniel Jones become a factor, too. If (as we firmly believe) he's not happy that the Colts folded the tents by trading guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner after a 2-5 start that included an overtime loss to the Chiefs and a toe-to-toe battle with the then-unbeaten Vikings, Jones would have a clear interest in hopping to a contender. The Vikings wanted to keep Jones after the 2024 season. He opted to sign with the Colts in part because he saw a more realistic path to winning the job over 2023 first-rounder Anthony Richardson in Indianapolis than 2024 first-rounder J.J. McCarthy in Minneapolis. If he's told that a return to Minnesota would include being installed immediately as QB1, he'd surely prefer that to a lost season with the Colts. Andd Jones has power over this process. Beyond the basic reality that no team wants a starting quarterback who doesn't want to play for it, the 2027 roster bonus and base salary that become fully guaranteed in March ($10.51 million) are currently guaranteed for injury. The ESPNFL article mentions that Jones could waive the injury guarantee in order to expedite a deal. The reverse of that (Jones refusing to waive the injury guarantee) means that Jones could block a trade, if avoiding a potential eight-figure guarantee for 2027 is a dealbreaker for his prospective employer. Our guess? Right now, only the Vikings currently have interest in Jones. And a trade for Jones becomes a very viable possibility if the Vikings lose to the Bills on Monday with Carson Wentz playing quarterback. Given the possibility that another team will emerge as a competitor to get Jones, it's also possible that the Vikings have already decided to trade for Jones after Monday night's game — win or lose — and that the two teams have agreed to keep it under wraps until Week 9 ends. Either way, if the oft-injured Jones plays on Sunday against the Cowboys and gets injured, that would kill any chance to trade him. That makes it important to monitor Sunday's game carefully. If the Colts apply a quick hook to Jones, it could mean that he's already gone.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cowboys place OLB Malachi Lawrence on IR, activate OLB Marist Liufau from IR
summary: The Cowboys placed outside linebacker Malachi Lawrence on injured reserve, the team announced Saturday.
full_text: ' The Cowboys placed outside linebacker Malachi Lawrence on injured reserve, the team announced Saturday. Lawrence injured his ankle in Sunday's loss to the Cardinals, and coach Brian Schottenheimer had announced the rookie would miss multiple weeks. Lawrence will miss at least four games on IR. The first-round pick has 13 tackles, a sack and three quarterback hits, while playing 41 percent of the defensive snaps. In a corresponding move, the Cowboys activated outside linebacker Marist Liufau from injured reserve. Liufau broke his forearm in the preseason finale. He returned to practice Oct. 22. Cowboys defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard, who is in his 21-day return-to-practice window, will remain on injured reserve. He has a calf injury but had full practices all week. The Cowboys also announced they elevated wide receiver Jordan Hudson and tight end James Mitchell from the practice squad. Tight ends Jake Ferguson and Luke Schoonmaker are questionable to play, and at wide receiver, KaVontae Turpin is out and George Pickens is questionable.
author: Charean Williams

title: Myles Garrett: Rams' opponents will have to pick their poison, me or Aaron Donald
summary: Garrett and Donald will play together for the first time on Sunday against the Commanders.
full_text: '''' Rams defensive end Myles Garret and defensive tackle Aaron Donald will finally be on the field together Sunday in Washington, and Garrett says that's going to be bad news for opposing offenses for the rest of the season. Donald did not play in Week 1 because he was still ramping up for the season after returning from his two-year retirement, and Garret hasn't played since Week 1 because of knee surgery. Garrett said the two of them together, two multiple-time Defensive Player of the Year award winners side by side, will present a unique challenge for opposing offenses. "I think offenses really have to pick their poison. Who's going to be freed up this play? I think either of us are pretty good at winning one-on-one, so we'll have some fun," Garrett said. "Going into this season I never thought I'd have the chance, and as you all know he kept us in suspense for quite a while, so it was very exciting, and I'm looking forward to getting on the field and playing some real snaps with him." Garrett said his poor performance in Week 1 against the 49ers showed him he needed knee surgery, something he would have preferred to avoid. "I was frustrated after the game. I knew that wasn't me, and I was being hampered by something," Garrett said. "I didn't want to miss any time, but I had to be realistic about where I was physically, and I had to make the best choice for me and the team." But now Garrett is back, and he said he and Donald playing together can give the Rams an "elite defense" for the rest of the season.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Rams activate Myles Garrett, put Jaylen Watson on IR
summary: Myles Garrett is officially back on the Rams' active roster.
full_text: '''' Myles Garrett is officially back on the Rams' active roster. The Rams announced on Saturday that they have activated Garrett from injured reserve. Head coach Sean McVay had already confirmed that the linebacker will play for the first time since Week 1 and the roster move clears the way for him to take the field against the Commanders on Sunday. Running back Ronnie Rivers will also be available after being activated from injured reserve. Tight end Terrance Ferguson was expected back as well, but was scratched on Friday with a hamstring injury. Cornerback Jaylen Watson will not play as he suffered a season-ending shoulder injury. He was placed on injured reserve Saturday and the Rams also elevated long snapper Jake McQuaide and cornerback Damarion Williams from the practice squad.
author: Josh Alper

title: Philip Rivers completes high-school season, confirms interview with NC State
summary: It's looking more and more like former NFL and NC State quarterback Philip Rivers will be the next coach of the Wolfpack.
full_text: ' It's looking more and more like former NFL and NC State quarterback Philip Rivers will be the next coach of the Wolfpack. Brian Murphy of WRAL has posted video of Rivers's comments from last night, after the high-school team he coaches exited the playoffs in Alabama. Rivers confirmed that he recently interviewed for the job, which became open two weeks ago when Dan Doeren was fired in his 14th season at NC State. Rivers immediately became a candidate. By last weekend, Rivers reportedly emerged as the focus . Since then, the Wolfpack also interviewed former NFL and NC State quarterback Russell Wilson. "We'll see what the future holds," Rivers said, adding that he plans to "take it one day at a time." If he goes, it will end his tenure at St. Michael Catholic High School in Fairhope, Alabama. He became the head coach in 2021. "We didn't have a stadium a few years ago," Rivers said, turning emotional. "If it were to be the last time out here, shoot, a lot was accomplished." If it was the last time for Rivers at St. Michael, it means there will be a first time for him never year at NC State.
author: Mike Florio

title: Broncos and Bo Nix have won 16 straight one-score games
summary: The Broncos keep finding ways to win games — especially close games.
full_text: The Broncos keep finding ways to win games — especially close games. Denver has won 16 straight games decided by one score or less. Quarterback Bo Nix has been the starter in each of the games. Via NBC Sports research, the streak ties the 2023-24 Chiefs (with starting quarterback Patrick Mahomes) for the longest streak since 1950. The Broncos last lost a one-score game in Week 3 of the 2025 season, 23-20 at the Chargers. Since then, the Broncos have won every one-score game in which they have played. This year, they're doing it despite being routinely outgained. For the season, they have a yardage differential of minus-658 — third worst in the NFL. And the Broncos have won three games in 2026 despite being outgained by 100 or more yards. The record for any season is four wins, accomplished by eight different teams. With two more this year, the Broncos will have the record to themselves. The next opportunity to win a one-score game comes on Sunday, at the Panthers in a rematch of Super Bowl 50.
author: Mike Florio

title: Vikings could end up with both Daniel Jones and Jonathan Taylor
summary: With Minnesota linked to both players, why not do a package deal?
full_text: '' Before Week 8, the Vikings had been linked to Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. After Week 8, Colts quarterback Daniel Jones became a potentially more attractive target for the Vikings. With the trade deadline less than three days away, why not both? The performance of quarterback Kyler Murray in the 19-15 loss to the Lions made the passing game a front-burner issue for the Vikings. But the running game remains not good enough. In Detroit, running back Jordan Mason had eight carries for 20 yards. Running back Aaron Jones had five carries for 22 yards. A package deal could allow the Colts to get the first-round pick they won't get by trading Taylor alone. And perhaps the Colts could get another pick or two, perhaps contingent on the playing time and/or performance of either or both players. Regardless, with Minnesota previously linked to Taylor and currently linked to Jones, the Colts trading both to the same team could get Indianapolis something they won't get by trading Taylor and Jones to two different teams — a first-round pick.
author: Mike Florio

title: QB Jake Haener returns to the Giants' practice squad
summary: The Giants signed quarterback Jake Haener back to the practice squad, the team announced Saturday.
full_text: The Giants signed quarterback Jake Haener back to the practice squad, the team announced Saturday. Haener, 27, was cut from the active roster on Thursday. J.J. McCarthy and Jameis Winston remain on the 53-player roster at the position. The Giants signed wide receiver Jalin Hyatt to take the vacant spot on the active roster. His only game action this season came against the Texans when he played four offensive snaps and six on special teams. The team also elevated running back Phil Mafah and outside linebacker Dawuane Smoot from the practice squad.
author: Charean Williams

title: Mason McCormick wasn't fined for dumping Jared Verse on his head
summary: Browns defensive end Jared Verse is getting upset.
full_text: Browns defensive end Jared Verse is getting upset. Well, even more upset. Verse, who was miffed at being dumped on his head by Steelers guard Mason McCormick on an extra-point try last Sunday — and at his teammates for not rushing to his defense , will surely be unhappy to learn that the NFL didn't fine McCormick for his WWE move. McCormick was flagged for unnecessary roughness on the play. It's unclear why the league didn't fine McCormick. The league never explains the basis for not imposing a financial penalty on a given player. Regardless, the league was as unbothered by the play as the other Browns players were. And it's likely that Verse will have something to say about it after Sunday's game at the Saints.
author: Mike Florio

title: 49ers activate Demarcus Robinson, elevate KhaDarel Hodge
summary: The 49ers will have two of their Week 1 wideouts back in the lineup for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
full_text: '' The 49ers will have two of their Week 1 wideouts back in the lineup for Sunday's game against the Raiders. Demarcus Robinson has been activated from injured reserve and KhaDarel Hodge has been elevated from the practice squad. Wide receiver Christian Kirk went on injured reserve in a corresponding move. Robinson caught a touchdown in that Week 1 win over the Rams, but has been out since injuring his ankle the next week. Hodge played in the first three games of the season as a practice squad elevation, but was released in October. He returned to the team this week. Kirk injured his knee in practice this week. He opened the season on injured reserve and made his 2026 debut in the 49ers' Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
author: Josh Alper

title: Broncos activate WR Pat Bryant
summary: The Broncos have wide receiver Pat Bryant back for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
full_text: The Broncos have wide receiver Pat Bryant back for Sunday's game against the Panthers. Bryant was activated from injured reserve on Saturday afternoon. He missed four games with an ankle injury and was designated for return when he resumed practicing with the team this week. Bryant had nine catches for 133 yards and a touchdown in four games before his injury. The Broncos also signed cornerback Sean Fresch off of the practice squad and placed defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike on injured reserve. Uwazurike was ruled out for Sunday with a shoulder injury. Safety Taylor Rapp and running back Cody Schrader were elevated from the practice squad in other moves.
author: Josh Alper

title: Lions place LB Jack Campbell on injured reserve
summary: The Lions placed linebacker Jack Campbell on injured reserve, the team announced Saturday.
full_text: The Lions placed linebacker Jack Campbell on injured reserve, the team announced Saturday. Campbell injured his neck during last week's victory over the Vikings and remains hospitalized. Campbell released a statement earlier this week saying he has full movement in his lower body and continues to make progress with movement in his upper body. Trevor Nowaske is expected to start for Campbell alongside Derrick Barnes and Malcolm Rodriguez. In a corresponding move, the Lions signed cornerback Nick Whiteside from the practice squad. Whiteside has not played in 2026 but played nine games for the Lions last season. The Lions also announced the elevations of defensive end Anthony Lucas and running back Jabari Small from the practice squad.
author: Charean Williams

title: Saints activate Kelvin Banks, Jordyn Tyson
summary: The Saints offense will be getting a couple of reinforcements for Sunday's game against the Browns.
full_text: ' The Saints offense will be getting a couple of reinforcements for Sunday's game against the Browns. They announced that they have activated left tackle Kelvin Banks and wide receiver Jordyn Tyson from injured reserve. Banks has been out since suffering an ankle injury in Week 2 and Tyson has yet to play this season due to a hamstring injury. Tyson was a first-round pick this season, so Sunday's game will be his NFL debut. As previously reported, the Saints released running back Kendre Miller in a corresponding move. They also released tight end Treyton Welch. Kicker Charlie Smyth and running back Zamir White have been elevated from the practice squad on a temporary basis.
author: Josh Alper

title: Falcons activate James Pearce, Yasir Abdullah
summary: Falcons linebacker James Pearce is set to make his 2026 debut.
full_text: Falcons linebacker James Pearce is set to make his 2026 debut. Pearce was suspended for the first eight games of the season as a result of a domestic violence arrest and the team officially moved him to their active roster on Saturday. Pearce had 10.5 sacks as a rookie and he'll try to add to that total against Joe Burrow and the Bengals in Madrid on Sunday. The Falcons also activated Yasir Abdullah from injured reserve, so they'll have a couple of new options on the edge this weekend. Wide receiver Beaux Collins came off of injured reserve as well and the Falcons signed running back Khalil Herbert off of the practice squad. He's filled in for the injured Brian Robinson the last couple of weeks and will remain in that role with Robinson going on injured reserve due to a hamstring issue. Defensive lineman Drake Jackson was elevated from the practice squad to round out the day's moves.
author: Josh Alper

title: Patriots activate Mack Hollins from IR
summary: The Patriots won't have A.J.
full_text: The Patriots won't have A.J. Brown or Romeo Doubs on Sunday, but they will be getting another wide receiver back from injury against the Packers. They have activated Mack Hollins from injured reserve. Hollins returned to practice this week after missing the last four games with a calf injury. Hollins had 15 catches for 209 yards in four appearances before his injury. He had 46 catches for 550 yards and two touchdowns in his first season with the Patriots. Brown will miss his second straight game with a knee injury and Doubs remains on injured reserve. Pop Douglas, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams join Hollins as the available receivers on the 53-man roster for New England.
author: Josh Alper

title: Vikings rule Jauan Jennings out for Monday night
summary: Wide receiver Jauan Jennings passed on a possible trade back to the 49ers in order to remain with the Vikings, but he won't be in Minnesota's lineup against the Bills on Monday night.
full_text: ' Wide receiver Jauan Jennings passed on a possible trade back to the 49ers in order to remain with the Vikings, but he won't be in Minnesota's lineup against the Bills on Monday night. The Vikings ruled Jennings out due to a calf injury that kept him out of practice the last two days. Jennings has six catches for 54 yards this season, but his limited role in the offense didn't cause him to reach for the exit door last month. With Jennings out, the Vikings could elevate Odell Beckham Jr. from the practice squad to make his first appearance for the team. The Vikings have until Monday afternoon to elevate him for the game. Quarterback Kyler Murray was ruled out with a hamstring injury earlier this week. Carson Wentz will make his second start of the season on Monday night. Running back Demond Claiborne (knee) will also miss the game. Safeties Theo Jackson (quad) and Jay Ward (knee) are listed as questionable.
author: Josh Alper

title: Vikings WR Jauan Jennings declined 49ers interest because "I love where I'm at"
summary: Wide receiver Jauan Jennings has not played a major role in the Vikings offense through the first eight weeks of the season, but he wasn't interested in switching teams when the possibility presented itself last month.
full_text: ' Wide receiver Jauan Jennings has not played a major role in the Vikings offense through the first eight weeks of the season, but he wasn't interested in switching teams when the possibility presented itself last month. The 49ers and Vikings discussed a trade that would send Jennings back to the team he played for during his first five NFL seasons and talks progressed to the point that Jennings spoke to his former coach Kyle Shanahan about a return. Jennings expressed a desire to stay with the Vikings and gave a succinct reason for his decision when asked about it on Saturday, "I just thought it was best for both teams," Jennings said, via Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com. "No distractions. I love where I'm at." Jennings only has six catches on 10 targets this season, but he expressed no issues with his spot in the Vikings' offense. "I'm not the coach, so I don't call the plays," Jennings said. "I'm a player, so I just play the game. I feel like anybody who watches football, who watches sports in general, kind of understands what comes with it." Jennings won't be improving on his production Monday night as the Vikings ruled him out with a calf injury. That could open the door for Odell Beckham Jr. to make his Vikings debut.

title: Have we been thinking about franchise QBs all wrong? CJ Carr, Darian Mensah and the Brock Purdy predicament
summary: Saturday's Miami-Notre Dame showdown offered a reminder that playing quarterback is about more than looking the part.
full_text:
CJ Carr running Notre Dame's two-minute offense against Miami to end the first half is all you need to know about who he is.
It's as surgical a series of plays as you'll see this season; he's calm before the snap, unpanicked after, even when he's avoiding the rush, always has his eyes downfield, and throws with the accuracy and precision that will make you a first-rounder, even if you lack the "prototypical physical tools" NFL teams covet in their franchise QBs. When you look like you've been doing this for a decade, no one cares if you can throw the ball 80 yards or run a 4.3 forty.
Heck of a 2 Min Drive from CJ Carr! pic.twitter.com/HxMYEJksnu
That drive ended with an 18-yard laser to Micah Gilbert to give the Fighting Irish a 17-3 halftime lead. And while they didn't cruise to a blowout win – credit to Darian Mensah and the Canes for battling back – it did reinforce a question I've been thinking about as we work our way through another "can't-miss" quarterback class that has, once again, missed:
Have we been evaluating the position backward?
Every fall, NFL teams (and folks in the media too) fall in love with the big, athletic, strong-armed quarterbacks who, if you squint enough, start to look like Justin Herbert or Josh Allen. And there's a reason for that. When it all comes together, it can be special. When it doesn't … well, it can be the 2026 Los Angeles Chargers.
It's why we annually watch evaluators excuse bad decision-making, chronic inaccuracy and poor processing because a QB gets off the bus looking like Will Levis or Drew Allar or if we're talking the '27 class, names like Arch Manning and LaNorris Sellers. Meanwhile, Brock Purdy, Mr. Irrelevant in 2022, and Kirk Cousins, a fourth-rounder a decade earlier, lacked those eye-popping physical traits but proved they could play quarterback at a high level in the NFL .
I'd even throw Mac Jones into the group. He put up huge numbers at Alabama and made the Pro Bowl as a rookie in New England, but his career went sideways after the Patriots decided Matt Patricia and Joe Judge should lead the offense. Jones had a pit stop in Jacksonville before finding his way to Kyle Shanahan and San Francisco, and all he did was play so well in Purdy's absence early last season that there were questions about whether he should keep the job . The point, in part, is what a smart, accurate quarterback with average physical tools can accomplish when the system plays to his strengths.
To be clear, this is less about arm strength or athleticism than how much inconsistency evaluators are willing to put up with for the upside, no matter how unlikely that realized upside might be. Put another way: are we undervaluing quarterbacks who win with anticipation, accuracy, processing and average NFL arms?
Which brings us to CJ Carr and Darian Mensah. Both should come in 6-foot-2 or 6-foot-3, so we're not talking about Bryce Young or Kyler Murray. But neither has a Patrick Mahomes fastball in their locker, either. They see the field, throw on time and with anticipation, and consistently understand where the football needs to go. Saturday gave us two very different looks at those skills.
Carr was clinical from the start. He set protections, got the ball out quickly and accurately, and once he started feeling it, was damn-near unstoppable in the way Purdy can be when he's in his bag. Again, I'd refer you to Carr running that two-minute offense as all the evidence you need.
Mensah spent much of the first half running for his life before settling down in the third quarter and drawing the Hurricanes to within seven points after one of his bread-and-butter back-shoulder throws:
Mensah —> Barkate That 2025 Duke team… I’ll never forget pic.twitter.com/qa8pn75KKn https://t.co/rG4KgrMZZe
Notre Dame gave Miami's offensive line fits for much of the night, and on the Hurricanes' very next drive, Mensah threw just his second interception of the season.
NOTRE DAME INTERCEPTS DARIAN MENSAH! 📺 Notre Dame Football on NBC & Peacock pic.twitter.com/QA0UH9tXao
It's undoubtedly a bad pick, but this is what NFL evaluators will note – and what shows up all over Mensah's tape: he's one of the best anticipation passers in the class. And sometimes, when you throw with anticipation on a speed out and miss inside, you're playing with fire. On this play, Mensah got burned.
It also didn't help that Malachi Toney, the best player on the planet not named Jeremiah Smith, was out with an ankle injury and exactly zero of the remaining Miami receiving options scared the Fighting Irish secondary.
But excuses, as they say, are for losers.
And don't get it confused: this wasn't Caleb Williams going into South Bend in 2023 and throwing three first-half interceptions , repeatedly making bad decisions under pressure as Notre Dame dismantled USC. Mensah was under siege often, and despite that pick, he kept competing, made big-time throws down the stretch and gave Miami a chance to tie the game in the closing minutes.
But he can't catch it for them:
Mensah finds Lofton but Luke Talich knocks it out of his hands 😱 pic.twitter.com/oA1bN4io4a
He didn't win, and he wasn't perfect, but he bounced back from a slow start and an early second-half interception to give Miami a chance to tie it late, on the road against one of the best defenses he'll face all season. And he did it without abandoning the traits that made him my QB1 in the first place (and Malachi Toney).
It's worth remembering that neither Mensah nor Carr entered the season as sure-fire first-round picks. Back in August, I had both with second-round grades and a lot to prove. And while there was a lot to like, there were also some legitimate concerns.
During his 2025 season at Duke, Mensah appeared to have the bigger arm, but his footwork was all over the place, and his decision-making was at times spotty. Carr threw with anticipation, consistently knew where to go with the football and showed impressive touch on second-level throws. But he could also let pressure affect him, and an average arm raised questions about how his game would translate to the NFL.
The numbers told a different story. In August, we introduced FRED , a model that compares college quarterbacks with previous first-round picks based on their production and experience. Mensah scored a 39.4, putting him within striking distance of 50, a mark every eligible quarterback in our historical sample had reached before eventually becoming a first-round pick. Carr scored just 10.6, although he had considerably less starting experience. I liked Carr more than the model did, but Mensah's numbers suggested he might be closer to first-round territory than his 2025 tape suggested.
Fast-forward to present day, and Mensah is my QB1, Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker is QB1a , and Carr is QB3. Both Mensah and Carr have made impressive strides, and both have looked the part of future first-round picks.
Both had dominated stretches of the season, but neither had faced many opponents capable of truly testing them . The Miami-Notre Dame matchup offered a chance to change that.
For Mensah, the biggest improvement this season has been his consistency. Coming into Saturday's game, he had completed 77.4% of his passes, averaged 10.3 yards per attempt and thrown 25 touchdowns and just one interception (which is now two). But here's what really stands out: When he throws in rhythm, he's completing 83.1% of his passes and averaging 11.4 yards per attempt, both among the best marks in college football . It's a reflection of what shows up every week on tape: He sees the field, throws with anticipation and rarely passes up an easy completion to force something downfield.
Carr has made significant strides too, in part because he has addressed one of my biggest preseason concerns. A year ago, he took sacks on nearly 21% of the plays in which he was pressured. This season, that number is now 6.7%, and he's been sacked just twice. His completion percentage under pressure has also…

title: Falcons vs. Bengals prediction: Stars on display in Madrid as Cincinnati seeks first international win
summary: The NFL returns to Spain for the second straight season with a matchup that features many of the league's top offensive stars
full_text:
Following a week without an international game, the NFL heads back overseas in Week 9 when it sends the Atlanta Falcons and Cincinnati Bengals to Spain. The Bernabéu will play host to American football for the second time in as many years as two divisional contenders descend upon Madrid.
The Bengals are in search of their first win away from American soil in franchise history after going 0-1-1 in their previous two opportunities (the most recent contest dating back to 2019), while the Falcons seek to improve to .500 in games abroad. Atlanta is 2-3 away from the United States and last season lost in Berlin.
This contest pits one of the league's hottest teams against a squad that aims to reestablish positive momentum. Cincinnati rides a three-game win streak into the Madrid Game and scored no fewer than 31 points in any of those triumphs, albeit with two of the matchups coming against bottom-tier competition. Atlanta, on the other hand, lost in two of its last three outings and went scoreless in its most recent showing.
Both sides are alive and well in their respective divisions, but the context between the two differs greatly. The Falcons are just a half game back of first place in the NFC South, which may be the weakest division in football with no teams at or above .500 through the season's first two months. The Bengals' position at half a game out of the AFC North lead is the superior standing considering three teams own winning records.
Fans of American football in Spain are in for a treat, because this game has all the makings of a shootout. There is not an offense in the NFL that is clicking quite like the Bengals over the last three weeks, and between Burrow, Chase, Higgins, London and Robinson, five of the biggest names in football will be in action in a star-studded battle. Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr . should bounce back from last week's dreadful 8-for-24 showing in the rain, so Atlanta ought to have enough juice to keep pace with a team that is averaging 36.3 points per game since Oct. 11.
In a matchup where points will be aplenty, the team with the better defense holds the edge. It is not as though Atlanta is vastly superior on that side of the ball, but it is much more reliable and is about to insert one of its projected top producers into the lineup for the first time this season. There is not a more opportune time for a disruptive pass rusher like Pearce to make his first appearance than against arguably the best quarterback in the NFL. That alone could be the difference in a high-variance matchup like this one. Pick: Falcons 34, Bengals 30

title: Bears vs. Buccaneers: Chicago looks to tame Tampa's running game while staying atop the NFC North
summary: Plus, where to watch, what to know and a preview from an NFL expert
full_text:
Two of the NFL's hottest teams will clash Sunday night in the Windy City when the Chicago Bears host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .
Both teams will enter Sunday night with winning streaks. Chicago has won three straight games on the strength of an offense that has scored 95 points over that span. Tampa Bay has won consecutive games behind a running game that has churned out a staggering 582 yards during the winning streak.
Here's how you can follow the action, along with a breakdown and a prediction.
Chicago's offense has been a juggernaut since Caleb Williams returned from injury. Over that span, they've scored 31, 30 and 34 points while receiving stellar play from Williams, who has re-entered the league MVP conversation.
Over the last three games, Williams has completed a staggering 73.8% of his passes with four touchdowns and zero picks while averaging 287 yards per game.
Last Sunday was Jeffery Simmons' first game as a Bear after he was traded from Tennessee. Against the Seahawks , Simmons filled the stat sheet with six tackles (including one for loss), a sack and a pass breakup. Simmons was part of a Bears defense that held Seattle to just 17 points, 18 first downs and 252 yards.
Jeffery Simmons highlights, anyone? pic.twitter.com/AwU17TzjfC
Williams will have to rise to the challenge of facing a Buccaneer defense that is conjuring up memories of Tampa Bay's legendary "Tampa 2" unit.
Over the last two games, the Buccaneers' defense has allowed just 13 points and forced a whopping eight turnovers. They've been especially stout against the pass, allowing just 175 and 125 yards in their last two games. Tampa Bay has also held their last two opponents (the Panthers and Falcons ) to under 100 rushing yards, which is significant given the running backs ( Chuba Hubbard and Bijan Robinson ) they've faced in recent weeks.
The Buccaneers' defensive charge has been led by linebackers Josiah Trotter (68 tackles and a pick-six), Alex Anzalone (42 tackles and three interceptions) and pass rushers David Walker and YaYa Diaby .
Along with their defense, the Buccaneers' recent success has been predicated on the running game and specifically running backs Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell . Tampa Bay ran for 258 yards in its 43-13 win over Carolina and 324 in the rain during last Sunday's 16-0 win over Atlanta while becoming the first team since 1974 to win a game without completing a pass.
Irving ran for a career-high 170 yards against Atlanta while recording his third 100-yard rushing performance in Tampa Bay's last four games. Gainwell ran for a career-high 140 yards and 25 carries against the Falcons.
After a 0-4 start, Tampa Bay has proven to be a team on the rise over the past month. The Buccaneers are first in the NFL in both rushing yards gained and fewest rushing yards allowed.
Tampa Bay's passing game, however, has largely been non-existent, even with the return of Baker Mayfield . Until Tampa Bay's passing game starts to show its teeth, it's going to be hard to pick them in matchups like this.
I'm picking the Bears in a game that will likely come down to defense and Caleb Williams making a few key completions down the stretch. Score: Bears 20, Buccaneers 16

title: NFL fines Jaquan Brisker, two others for illegal Week 8 hits that placed opponents in concussion protocol
summary: Each of the players on the receiving end of those collisions will miss Week 9
full_text:
The NFL levied 31 fines in Week 8, which was the second most in a single week this season. Among the most notable punishments were those handed down to Pittsburgh Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker , Dallas Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown and Las Vegas Raiders safety Jeremy Chinn . Each fine was the result of a hit that led to the offensive player being placed in concussion protocol and ruled out for Week 9.
Brisker owes the NFL $17,911 for a blow to the head/neck on Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson . The play occurred less than a minute and a half into the Steelers' victory and drew a roughing the passer penalty, which Brisker voiced extreme displeasure with after the game.
"Babying the quarterback," Brisker said . "He's laying there crying, whatever he was doing. It is what it is. I assume I'm going to get fined because if you watch it, I'm hitting him with my chest and them I'm off to the side. But he had his binky today, so they threw it out there. It is what it is."
Watson briefly left the game , and Shedeur Sanders replaced him. The latter threw two passes before Watson returned to action and finished the game. Although Watson practiced in the days leading up to this Sunday's matchup against the New Orleans Saints and cleared the concussion protocol on Saturday, the Browns announced they will turn to Sanders as their Week 9 starter .
Brisker flagged for hit on Watson #Steelers #NFL pic.twitter.com/FCOv8QtjJA
Overshown's fine is for his use of his helmet on a hit against Arizona Cardinals running back Bam Knight. He must pay $9,528. The hit jarred the ball loose from Knight's hands, and the Cowboys recovered the fumble without a penalty. The NFL reviewed the play in the wake of the game, however, and issued the fine.
Knight will not play in the Cardinals' divisional clash with the Seattle Seahawks . He did not practice this week.
Two different angles of the hit on #AZCardinals RB Bam Knight pic.twitter.com/i2zS8LzGyF
Chinn sealed a Raiders win last week with an interception in the end zone, but just one play prior, he made forcible contact with New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson on a catch along the sideline, which resulted in a fine. Chinn owes $17,911 for a hit on a defenseless player. The two players' helmets collided on the play, and while Wilson stayed in the game for the Jets' final snap, he later entered concussion protocol.
Wilson reported concussion symptoms the next day, and by midweek the Jets placed him in the protocol. They eventually ruled him out for this week's battle with the Kansas City Chiefs .
Garrett Wilson Somehow, Someway Hangs On To This Ball. Then Jeremy Chinn Goes Helmet To Helmet And Blows Him Up. What A Dirty Play. 😡 pic.twitter.com/Og7SwQWrqZ
There have been 223 plays this season which resulted in a fine. That is 0.0113% of all plays through eight weeks. The 31 fines from Week 8 were second only to the 38 in Week 2.

title: Pick your poison: Rams' Myles Garrett anticipates matchup nightmares in first game with Aaron Donald
summary: An injured reserve stint delayed the first look at Garrett and Donald in the same lineup, but now they could dominate opposing offenses
full_text:
When Los Angeles Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett returns from injured reserve this week for his first game action since the season opener, he will line up next to defensive lineman Aaron Donald for the first time. That duo is projected to be one of the NFL's most unstoppable tandems at any position since Donald announced that he would come out of retirement for the 2026 season, and now the league will find out just how formidable it really is.
The timing of Garrett's IR stint and Donald's season debut clashed, forcing them to wait until November to suit up together. Garrett played just one game before he underwent knee surgery, and Donald entered the lineup in Week 2.
Garrett said it will be surreal to share the field with a fellow Defensive Player of the Year award winner.
"Going into this season, I never thought I'd have the chance," Garrett said ahead of Sunday's road game against the Washington Commanders . "As y'all know, he kept us in suspense for quite a while. It was very exciting to hear about that. Looking forward to the opportunity to get on the field and actually play some real snaps with him."
Garrett's arrival in Los Angeles by way of a blockbuster trade in June was a catalyst for Donald's unretirement, so it is only right that two of the most disruptive players in football history finally get the opportunity to play alongside each other. Donald has been more effective in run defense than pass rushing this season, so with Garrett (the single-season sack record holder) rejoining the fold, their skill sets should complement each other tremendously.
Both superstar defenders have commanded double teams at extreme rates throughout their careers, but opposing offensive lines might have to stay more honest with their assignments so as to prevent the other player from capitalizing on the diverted attention.
"I think offenses really have to pick their poison," Garrett said. "Who's going to be freed up this play? Either of us are pretty good at winning one-on-ones. We'll have some fun."
There is no better time than the present for Garrett to return to full strength and for this duo to join forces. The Rams are in the midst of a potential midseason turnaround after opening the year with a surprising yet immensely disappointing 2-4 record, and they need to keep the momentum rolling to fulfill their Super Bowl expectations.
At the time, it was a surprise to see Garrett held entirely in check in the season-opening blowout loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. When the news of his knee ailment came to light, though, it explained why he was held without a single tackle in the contest. Garrett said that the knee acted up on him throughout the game and limited him from making his typical impact as a first-team All-Pro-caliber force off the edge.
Now that he is healthy, the question is just how great of an impact Garrett will make for the elite Rams defense. Every year since his rookie season, the former No. 1 overall pick has logged double-digit sacks. Last season, he broke the NFL single-season record with 23. He is also a stalwart in run defense and led the league in tackles of loss each of the last two years.
There was one sign in Week 1 that suggested Garrett will deliver his usual impact and perhaps even take another step forward in his first year with the Rams. He logged five quarterback pressures on Brock Purdy in that loss to the 49ers, good for an 18.5% pressure rate on his 39 defensive snaps. That would be the third-best mark of his career if it sustained over a full season.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Saints motivated to face 'smiling' Shedeur Sanders after Browns QB offers bulletin board material
summary: The maligned New Orleans defense will have a chip on its shoulder in Sanders' first start of the season
full_text:
Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders caught himself before he explicitly gave the New Orleans Saints bulletin board material ahead of their Week 9 matchup, but it did not require much reading between the lines to decipher what he thinks of the Saints' defense.
Sanders will make his first start of the season on Sunday with Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol. As such, he conducted a media availability session ahead of the contest and made an eyebrow-raising comment about the Saints and a defense that ranks 28th in yards per game allowed and 29th in scoring.
"I've seen a lot," Sanders said with a grin when asked what he noticed on film. "When I smile, just know that means something. I'm maturing, you know what I'm saying? I'm maturing. I could have gave that a decent answer, but now I'm just going to smile whenever it's just, like, some questions, you know?"
Sanders may not have outright criticized the New Orleans defense, but by explaining his body language, he made it quite clear that he saw a unit he can pick apart when he conducted his film study. The second-year player would be far from the first quarterback to have his way against this squad, which allows 233.3 yards per game through the air, but the Saints might come out with additional motivation to stop him in the wake of those remarks.
Count edge rusher Carl Granderson among those who saw what Sanders had to say.
"We're gonna come in with a chip on our shoulder for sure," Granderson said . "They've been chirping a little bit. We see what the quarterback done said. We're finna come in hot and ready to play. We're going to pack the defense, and the offense is going to come with it. It's going to be a good game for sure. We're going to come out with the dub."
Dating back to his college career, Sanders has long been a lightning rod for attention off the field. The former fifth-round pick and son of Deion Sanders is never one to avoid speaking his mind.
For the first time this season, Sanders gets the opportunity on Sunday to back up his talk with his play on the field. He briefly entered last week's 27-6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers when Watson took a big hit in the first quarter, but he attempted only two passes and has thrown just three times this year. The Week 9 start will mark a return to the starting lineup for the first time since last season when he spent seven weeks as the Browns' No. 1 quarterback.

title: Rams' Quentin Lake apologizes to Justin Herbert for 'deli meat' remarks, Chargers not moving QB via trade
summary: Herbert leads the NFL in interceptions and holds the league's worst QBR through seven games
full_text:
Coming out of last week's win over the Los Angeles Chargers , Quentin Lake insulted quarterback Justin Herbert following his interception that helped the Los Angeles Rams clinch their second straight victory.
Lake said on Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown's podcast that Herbert was "throwing deli meat out there" during the quarterback's two-interception outing that resulted in the Chargers' seventh consecutive loss to start the season.
He apologized to Herbert via text after the comments went viral.
"I don't know if he read it," Lake said Friday, via the Los Angeles Times. "He probably says, 'I don't care about it anymore. I'm not trying to see this. It doesn't matter. You said what you said.' But at the same time I . . . felt like it was right for me to at least say,' Hey, man, I didn't mean it in any disrespectful way.'"
Lake said after the game that Herbert "was seeing ghosts out there" and that his defense was expecting him to make mistakes.
"I haven't looked into it, haven't heard anything about it, so I can't really make a comment about it," Herbert told reporters this week . "We're really just focused on what's going on in the building, playing football and doing what we can and doing our best to, you know, go put our best effort out on Sunday. And that's all that really matters. Anything outside of that is out of our control."
Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh refused to place blame on his quarterback.
"I thought he played — did his job exceptionally well," Harbaugh said after reviewing the game film. "You know, two throws he would have liked to have back."
Mike McDaniel, who's struggling in his first season as the team's offensive coordinator, dismissed Lake's opinion of Herbert on Thursday.
"People are saying whatever they want with whatever facts they have when we're not living up to expectations," McDaniel said. "Keep it moving."
Herbert has thrown an interception in every start this season, leading the NFL in the category (10) with the lowest QBR among starting quarterbacks (32.5). Despite his career-worst beginning to the campaign, Herbert is expected to be off-limits at the trade deadline, in light of a report this week that the Minnesota Vikings were interested.
ESPN's Adam Schefter reported last month that Los Angeles would not move off their franchise player.
"The person cut me off mid-sentence, stopped me in my tracks and said, 'Let me be very clear about this: we have never even discussed that idea. Should we trade Justin Herbert has never been uttered in our organization, nor will it be," Schefter said last month . "This is what the person said. … I didn't even hear a 'we will listen.' They won't discuss it, they won't think about it."
The Chargers, who haven't scored a touchdown in their last nine quarters of play, host Houston on Sunday. The Texans are 2-5 this season, with both wins coming over their last three games.
author: Brad Crawford

title: NFL trade deadline rumors: Could Giants' John Harbaugh reunite with former running back?
summary: Harbaugh brought seven players with him from the Ravens when he took the Giants job. Might an eighth be on the way?
full_text:
Although the Baltimore Ravens have not yet moved any of their players ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline, they did receive interest from other teams amid their slip to the bottom of the AFC North. One call they fielded came from their former coach's franchise.
New York Giants coach John Harbaugh would benefit from the addition of another running back to his offense, and according to ESPN , his front office inquired about a potential trade for Ravens ballcarrier Justice Hill . No deal is done, and it is unclear how receptive the Ravens were to the Giants' interest.
Hill has been the Ravens' second option behind superstar Derrick Henry for seven years and is clearly a valued member of the organization, because more than a half decade is a long time for a non-starting player to spend with one team. All but one of those years came with Harbaugh at the helm, so the coach's affinity for him is obvious.
The Giants could have made a push for a home-run trade, too, but there are no accounts of them seeking to acquire Henry. The Ravens are reportedly uninterested in trading him, anyway. Instead, Hill was and still may be the preferred target as they work to bolster a running back group that has been in flux all season.
Cam Skattebo , nursing a hamstring injury, is the primary weapon in New York but briefly fell out of favor with the coaching staff when he coughed up nearly as many fumbles as anyone else in the NFL over the first half of the season, which resulted in a one-week benching. Najee Harris , Tyrone Tracy Jr . and Devin Singletary have all pitched into the running back committee, but Harris is no longer on the roster and Tracy is on injured reserve with a hamstring issue. Considering Singletary is fourth on the team in carries, anyone who would join the roster ahead of the trade deadline would likely slot directly into the No. 2 role ahead of him.
If the Giants make a play for Hill, he would join a lengthy list of players to head to New York with experience under Harbaugh. The longtime Ravens coach brought seven players from his former job with him when he joined the Giants ahead of the 2026 season.
(only those who appeared on active roster during regular season)
Under Harbaugh's tutelage, Hill averaged 209.2 rushing yards per season and logged eight touchdowns. He was nearly just as much of a receiving threat as a rushing option and added five scores through the air during that stretch. Hill was largely a passing-down back while Henry handled the lion's share of carries.

title: NFL week 9 anytime TD best bets: Look for Jonah Coleman and Joe Milton III to find end zone

full_text:

Milton is one of those tantalizing talents where you just wonder if he could actually be a starting quarterback someday. I'm excited to watch him.

title: Chargers not interested in Khalil Mack trade, will retain top offensive players despite 0-7 record, per report
summary: The winless Chargers will stick to the status quo
full_text:
The only winless team in the NFL may stand firm at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Despite their deeply disappointing start to the season, the Los Angeles Chargers reportedly have no interest in moving their perceived top trade candidates. According to ESPN , the front office made it clear to other teams that edge rusher Khalil Mack will remain a Charger at the deadline, and any questions regarding quarterback Justin Herbert and wide receiver Ladd McConkey were met with "hard nos."
If the Chargers were to make a deal by Tuesday, Mack would be perhaps the least surprising trade piece considering he is on an expiring contract and continues to play disruptive football from the edge rusher position, which is always in demand. But Los Angeles has always been steadfast in its desire to keep the future Hall of Famer in town through the end of his deal. Mid-round draft capital would be a reasonable return for the 35-year-old , but instead the Chargers repeatedly shut down outside interest in one of their top defensive assets.
"I want Khalil Mack here," coach Jim Harbaugh said this week . "Khalil Mack wants to be here. He's one of the pillars of our team."
It is less surprising that Los Angeles put a fence around Herbert and McConkey since they could remain building blocks for whatever kind of rebuild the franchise undertakes. Herbert remains under team control through 2029, and McConkey's rookie deal runs through the end of next season. When the offense is non-dysfunctional, they are standout players.
The obvious issue, however, is that the offense is dysfunctional this season. Herbert threw more interceptions (10) than any other quarterback in the NFL over the first eight weeks, and his 69.3 passer rating is second-worst only to Daniel Jones among qualifying signal-callers. McConkey is on pace for his least productive season as a pro with only 17 catches across six games.
Moving on from those offensive weapons would likely require the Chargers to sell low, because the offense's overall woes have cast a shadow over both players. That appears to be a non-starter.
The Chargers reportedly do not like the message of giving up on this season. But at 0-7 and with more of their losses coming by more than one possession than not, the hole they dug themselves into over the first two months of the campaign is deeper than that of any other team. There is very little to play for the rest of the way.
Los Angeles is opposed to trading its most valuable tools, but by holding onto them, it is declining to cash in on the potential draft picks it would receive in return. For a team that is clearly not equipped to contend in the near future, rebuilding through the draft would be a logical step forward. Instead, it will keep intact a core that has not won a playoff game in the Harbaugh era.
Player personnel is not the only part of this operation that remains unchanged, either. Harbaugh retained offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel through the bye week, which also came as a surprise since his system is the least productive in the NFL. No team averages fewer points per game than the Chargers at 14.1. The only tangible change to the offense has come in the form of McDaniel moving from the sideline to the box for Week 9.
If the definition of insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results, then the Chargers -- by way of keeping their roster intact and declining to make changes on the coaching staff -- fit that bill.
