title: NFL trade deadline: Four Eagles, two more Colts and a starting QB included among top candidates
summary: Saquon Barkley, Jonathan Taylor, Kirk Cousins and more could fetch returns at the trade deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is less than two weeks away. That means the hot stove will heat up considerably fairly soon. We've already seen multiple high-profile deals this season, with Joey Porter Jr . heading to the Cowboys , Marvin Harrison Jr . heading to the Texans , Quenton Nelson heading to the Seahawks , DeForest Bucker landing with the 49ers and Jeffery Simmons being traded to the Bears , and we could see several more in the coming days, given how wide open the league appears to be at the moment.
With that in mind, we wanted to take a look at some of the top targets who could be on the move. We ranked the top situations that bear the most watching, but with a twist. Some of them are team-wide, meaning there are multiple targets that interested teams could pursue over the next two weeks. There are 25 targets in all. (The Nelson, Buckner and Simmons deals make us 3-for-3 on predicting players that could be dealt, from the original list below. The list has since been updated.)
So without further ado, here's the list...
Saquon Barkley's contract, with all the various option bonuses included, makes dealing with him somewhat financially complicated, but given the Eagles ' struggles, his age, and the fact that teams are looking for explosiveness at running back these days, he makes sense as a target for needy teams. His current injury situation muddies the picture a bit, but that could be cleared up in the coming days and weeks as he gets further away from the hamstring pull.
Moro Ojomo is in the final year of his rookie contract. The Eagles just paid big money to two defensive tackles ( Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis ), so they probably can't afford to keep Ojomo around. He's 25 years old and has shown production upside with 6 sacks last season.
If the Eagles want to get aggressive, they can consider dealing both him and Nolan Smith , whose fifth-year option they picked up for next season but who they probably can't afford to keep in the longer term. Smith is more of a force in the run game than as a pass rusher, but that could still be valuable for teams that need help on the edge.
Dallas Goedert , meanwhile, signed a renegotiated contract with the Eagles this past offseason and is carrying only a $1.3 million base salary. He's not the most dynamic tight end these days, but he's a reliable pass-catcher and blocker, and any team that needs an additional tight end (teams love multi-tight end sets these days) could get interested for a small price.
Nelson is already on the move, traded to the Seahawks for a pair of draft picks. Bucker is gone, too, having been sent back to the 49ers after seven years away.
Jonathan Taylor is one of the best running backs in the NFL and has been able to remain productive even while the Colts ' offense has fallen apart around him. (He's only at 4.2 yards per carry, but he's carrying a 55% rushing success rate, per Pro-Football-Reference.) He's the type of explosive back who can change an offense in the way Kenneth Walker III did for the Chiefs . The contract isn't prohibitive for trade purposes, as the Colts would incur only $10 million in dead money next year if they move him. DeForest Buckner has also been traded away .
Josh Downs has reportedly requested a trade away from Indianapolis, and with the wide receiver in the final year of his rookie contract, the Colts should seriously consider moving him if they're not going to give him a new deal this offseason. He hasn't been particularly productive this year due to Daniel Jones ' struggles, but he's been a per-route star in prior years, so he could help a team in need of receiver depth.
Simmons has already been dealt, heading to the Bears for two first-rounders and more .
Amani Hooker is a very good, very versatile safety (he's played 232 snaps in the box, 127 as a deep safety and 56 as a slot corner so far this year), and those are valuable around the NFL. He still has three years left on his contract, including 2026, so there is a team-control aspect that would be valuable to a potentially acquiring team.
Tony Pollard is in the final year of his deal with only a $6.7 million base salary. He's 29 years old, but if you look under the hood, the numbers show he's actually running pretty well so far this season. He's 10th in yards after contact per attempt among the 39 running backs with 50-plus carries, for example, according to Tru Media. He's also 12th in explosive run rate. He can still play, and help a team in need of a committee back.
Calvin Ridley has completely fallen out of favor in Tennessee and could potentially help a team in need of depth-chart wide receiver help.
Khalil Mack is on a one-year deal with an $8 million base salary. He's got three sacks in six games and has played 71% of the Chargers ' defensive snaps. He's not going to be the player he once was, but any team in need of a rotational pass rusher should give the Chargers a call to see if they can get him for a late pick.
Tuli Tuipulotu only has two sacks in the Chargers' six games, but a deeper look at the numbers reveals a player playing better than that. He's 23rd in pressure rate among 148 players with 100 or more pass-rush snaps, according to Tru Media, and 18th in havoc play rate. He's still just 24 years old and you can get out ahead of his free agency by acquiring him now.
Derwin James , like Jeffery Simmons, recently signed a contract extension, so it would be somewhat surprising to see him get dealt. But he's 31 years old, the Chargers are terrible, and he's one of their most valuable assets. His base salaries for the next three years are also pretty high ($17.5 million, $24.6 million and $21.5 million), so the return might not be as much as the Chargers would be looking for.
Quentin Johnston only has 8 catches for 165 scoreless yards this season, and he's seemingly been surpassed in the target pecking order. He also has an $18 million salary for next season after the Chargers picked up his fifth-year option. So the return is likely to be low, but it's hard to imagine that L.A. wants to keep him around.
Donte Jackson is in the final year of his deal with only a $6 million base salary. He could be of help to any team in need of a cornerback, and there are always teams that need help in the defensive backfield. If the Chargers actually decide to sell, he seems like one of the more likely candidates to move.
Budda Baker has base salaries of $14.4 million and $16.1 million this year and next, but he's a valuable enough player to make those price tags worth it. He's extremely versatile and can play both the run and the pass, whether lined up deep or in the box. He's 30 years old and still likely has several quality seasons left under his belt. The Cardinals aren't going to contend for the postseason, and Baker is their best asset for future value.
Josh Sweat is having a down year, both sack-wise (2 in 7 games) and in terms of his pressure rate (7.9%). And his contract doesn't exactly make that type of production attractive. But his track record over the long term, up to and including last year, is much more impressive, and teams could bet that he has a bounce-back in a more favorable environment. He probably wants a new contract, but that could be worked out once you see him play for your team.
Win over the Jets notwithstanding, the Dolphins look like arguably the worst team in the league this season. Zach Sieler , though, remains a quality player. He hasn't been at his best this season (nobody on the Dolphins has), but we've seen high upside as both a run defender and a pass rusher from the defensive interior. If you can tap back into that, his base salaries over the next few years are very affordable ($44.5 million from 2027 through 2029, none of which is guaranteed).
Jordyn Brooks , like Jeffery Simmons and Derwin James, recently signed an extension. But his deal actually made him easier to trade and gave the Dolphins the benefit of selling to an acquiring team, knowing they'd have Brooks…
author: Jared Dubin

title: Cowboys should consider trading George Pickens: 5 logical destinations at NFL trade deadline
summary: Pickens received only four targets in Dallas' historic collapse against Arizona, adding urgency to the Cowboys' decision before the NFL trade deadline
full_text:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Shortly after Chad Ryland 's game-winning field goal went through the uprights to seal a 33-30 comeback, Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens flew down the hallway and into the locker room by himself. No other teammate, coach, or staff member moved faster to get into the locker room and out of AT&T Stadium after Dallas made ugly history with its blown 14-point lead.
Pickens first one to the lockers, jogged down the tunnel before most media could even set up @1053thefan pic.twitter.com/RVab4T1c5M
Pickens' lack of targets was glaring. CeeDee Lamb led the way with 11 targets on Sunday while tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford was second with five targets. Pickens caught two passes for 48 yards. Four targets in a game simply isn't enough.
Pickens hasn't been bad this season: his 533 yards receiving rank as the 15th most in the NFL in 2026, just behind Trey McBride and just in front of Garrett Wilson (527) and Ja'Marr Chase (492). He is still on pace to exceed 1,100 receiving yards, but it regularly feels like the Cowboys are leaving production out on the field. Since Schottenheimer blamed Pickens' lack of vigor for run blocking for the team's struggling offense in a loss to the Green Bay Packers, he has 10 targets across the last two games.
"If I had the answer, we'd get him involved. I'm not trying to be rude or whatever it is, but he made some plays. Anytime the ball went his way, he came up with them. He had the one, unfortunately came back for a holding," quarterback Dak Prescott said. ... "I'm not sure about even how many targets he had. As I told y'all before, I go through the reads. [I] try to throw it to the open guy and stay consistent and true to that. And so, I've got to go back and look at the film and see if I missed him, see if we could have went to him more, see if we could have went to CeeDee more. I feel like it was a game that CeeDee didn't have as many catches as per usual, but we still had a chance to win and should have won it."
With the NFL trade deadline coming up in eight days on Nov. 10 and the Cowboys off to a 3-5 start and appearing to be going nowhere, it would make sense for Dallas to field trade calls for Pickens. He is playing out the franchise tag, and he will command near-top-of-the-market value on his second multi-year NFL contract. Dallas will also have to deal with balancing cornerback Joey Porter Jr. 's contract situation, since he, too, is set to be a free agent after the season.
After trading away draft capital to get Porter Jr. and Quinnen Williams, Dallas could use some additional ammunition in its 2027 NFL Draft war chest. So who could be blowing up owner/general manager Jerry Jones' phone for Pickens if word leaks out that they will listen to trade calls for their 25-year-old Pro Bowl wideout? Here is a look at five potential landing spots.
Jerry Jones has shown he doesn't care about sending a young star player to a non-divisional rival: he traded Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers . The pairing of the 49ers and Pickens makes too much sense.
San Francisco is the NFC's top seed through the first eight weeks of the season, and they have $34.98 million in cap space, the third most in the entire league, per OverTheCap.com. There are no financial barriers to this deal.
Plus, they have a glaring need for Pickens given all their wide receiver injuries. Both Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) were ruled out of their last game played in Week 7. Three wide receivers are on their injured reserve list.
Lastly, the 49ers are all in for 2026 because of their aging core. Christian McCaffrey is 30, Evans is 33, Samuel is 30, George Kittle is 33, Kyle Juszcyk is 35, Trent Williams is 38 and DeForest Buckner is 32. Both Fred Warner and Nick Bosa are healthy right now, but they're both 29 with extensive injury histories.
The Chiefs failed to score a game-winning touchdown after having a second-and-goal at the one with 15 seconds left, and Kansas City was outscored 15-0 in the fourth quarter of their narrow 28-24 road loss against the Denver Broncos on Sunday. You know who could have made a significant difference for quarterback Patrick Mahomes in the fourth quarter in Week 8? The 6-foot-3, 200-pound Pickens.
Kenneth Walker III is starting to lose a little steam after being heavily relied upon to carry the Chiefs' offense on his back. After averaging 133 rushing yards per game and 6.3 yards per carry with six rushing touchdowns in Kansas City's first five games of the season, Walker III is now averaging 52.5 rushing yards per game and 3.0 yards per carry without a touchdown in the last two games.
That's because the Chiefs' passing game requires Travis Kelce to be their No. 1 target, something that isn't a sustainable formula over the course of an 18-week season and beyond. Also, it would be incredibly foolish to waste the rest of Mahomes' glory years. The three-time Super Bowl MVP quarterback is 31, but he hasn't been the same high-flying passer that he was with a true No. 1 wide receiver like Tyreek Hill. Without Hill since 2022, Mahomes' production has taken a notable dip.
Average air yards per pass attempt
* Ranks among 37 qualified quarterbacks since 2022
The Buffalo Bills are the AFC's No. 1 seed through the first eight weeks, and they are always in win-now mode with Josh Allen . Yes, the Bills traded for DJ Moore , but he is probably best as Buffalo's No. 2 receiver on a Super Bowl team. He missed Buffalo's last two games with a shoulder injury prior to returning in Week 8, and he hyperextended his knee in the Bills' 36-10 beatdown of the Lamar Jackson-less Ravens .
Allen hasn't had a true WR1 since the 2024 Stefon Diggs trade. Pickens could help him become the league's most efficient passer. That would probably be enough for the Bills to perhaps win their first Super Bowl in franchise history.
The Las Vegas Raiders trading for Pickens would be a case of taking care of the now and the later. The Kirk Cousins-led Raiders are 4-4 and just one game out of the AFC's No. 7 seed. Giving Cousins, whose 19 passing touchdowns rank as the second most in the NFL, Pickens to pair with Brock Bowers could really make Klint Kubiak's offense pop.
Among the players officially listed as wide receivers on the Raiders' roster, Tre Tucker , a 2023 third-round pick, is the best they have. He could also help accelerate Fernando Mendoza's long-term development. Pickens is just two years older than the 23-year-old Mendoza, so the quarterback could spend the bulk of his career with a high-caliber wide receiver in addition to the 23-year-old Bowers at tight end.
Perhaps living in Las Vegas would dull the novelty of going out on The Strip that Pickens and Lamb experienced when they visited for "Monday Night Football" last season.
Despite being 6-1 and the No. 2 seed in the NFC, the Minnesota Vikings have the sixth-lowest scoring offense (20.0 points per game) in the entire NFL. Their lack of rhythm in the passing game is a major reason for that, as their Kyler Murray-quarterbacked passing attack is averaging the second-fewest passing yards per game (165.6) in the entire NFL.
Yes, Minnesota has 2022 NFL Offensive Player of the Year Justin Jefferson and former first-round pick Jordan Addison at wide receiver, but its offense could clearly use another weapon to help Murray find his groove as a Viking. They have been rumored to be in pursuit of Jonathan Taylor , but perhaps Pickens could also help fix the issues on the offensive side of the ball.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Frustrated Derrick Henry responds to trade rumors, Ravens not expected to deal him, per report
summary: Henry was not a happy camper after Baltimore's fourth straight setback
full_text:
After a 4-1 start, the Baltimore Ravens have now lost four straight following Thursday night's lopsided loss to the visiting Jacksonville Jaguars . The Ravens' current plight raised questions about Derrick Henry's future in Baltimore ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline.
A clearly frustrated Henry fielded questions after Thursday night's loss, and he gave a candid response when directly asked about his future with the Ravens.
"I'm not mentioning me going anywhere else," he said . "I'm saying let's go back to work, try to get better and turn this around."
The stance on a potential Henry trade is not exclusive to the running back himself. According to ESPN , the Ravens are not expected to trade him during the season, and the front office informed him that it has no intentions of doing so. There has reportedly never been any consideration of a deal.
The Ravens have lost four straight games and Derrick Henry is frustrated pic.twitter.com/mpkdiTIIuI
At this point, Henry remains focused on doing what he can to help the Ravens turn their season around. But while his mindset is admirable, there's not much Henry can do to help fix Baltimore's current issues.
Even if Jacoby Brissett plays well, it's going to be hard for the Ravens to make up ground in the AFC North. Baltimore is currently last in the division; they trail the first-place Steelers by 2.5 games. The Ravens are currently three spots out of the AFC's final wild-card spot.
When you add in Lamar Jackson's uncertain future with the team , it might make sense for Baltimore to begin rebuilding now rather than delay the inevitable.
There would have been no shortage of offers if the Ravens decided to trade Henry, who on Thursday night moved into seventh on the NFL's career rushing list. The Vikings , Giants , Patriots, and Packers are among the NFL's playoff-contending teams that could use help at the running back position.
Henry would have figured to command significant compensation on the trade market if the Ravens entertained any offers. While his age — he'll be 33 by the end of the regular season — is a factor that could have hurt his trade value, it would have only taken one team to drive up the price.
A championship is essentially the only thing that has eluded Henry to this point in his career, and a trade might have expedited his search for a Super Bowl. Instead, it looks as though he will have to wait at least another year as the Ravens fall out of contention.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: NFL trade deadline rumors: Colts' Daniel Jones could get dealt and there's only one team that makes sense
summary: The Vikings are 6-1 despite fielding the league's second-worst passing attack, and a reunion with Kevin O'Connell makes all the sense in the world
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have been one of the busiest teams in the NFL heading into the trade deadline and they might not be done making deals. The Colts have already traded away both Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner , and it appears that there's at least a chance that Daniel Jones could be next.
According to ESPN , the Colts have taken calls from "multiple" teams about Jones' availability and they've been willing to listen to any offer. This doesn't mean that Jones will ultimately be traded, but it does mean that he'll definitely be one of the biggest names to watch between now and Tuesday's deadline.
At one point, Jones looked like he was going to be the Colts' quarterback of the future. Last season, he helped get the Colts off to a 7-1 start before his year was derailed by injuries. He ended up tearing his Achilles in Week 13, which caused him to miss the final four games of the year. Despite the injury, the Colts still decided to sign him to a two-year $88 million extension back in March. The deal included $50 million in guaranteed money and the Colts have already paid most of that out in the form of a $44 million signing bonus .
This means that if a team acquires Jones, it wouldn't cost much from a financial standpoint. The one thing about a potential Jones trade is that there aren't very many trade candidates out there. The ESPN report mentioned that the Ravens had called about his availability, but Baltimore ended up making a deal for Jacoby Brissett .
With the Ravens out, that basically leaves one team that makes sense for Jones, and that's the Minnesota Vikings . The Vikings are off to a 6-1 start and they currently have one of the best defenses in the NFL, but that unit is essentially going to waste right now because Minnesota has an offense that can't move the ball.
The Vikings signed Kyler Murray in the offseason hoping he could spark the offense, but that hasn't happened. He's started six games this season and simply hasn't been effective. The Vikings' passing attack is averaging just 165.6 yards per game this year, which is the second-worst number in the NFL. Murray has also been dealing with multiple injuries, including a hamstring issue that will keep him on the sideline this week.
The Vikings also have Carson Wentz , who will be making his second start of the season in Week 9. Wentz started in Week 2 after Murray suffered a concussion and during that start, he completed just 55% of his passes for 143 yards and zero touchdowns. However, he did play reasonably well while filling in for Murray in Week 1 with three TD passes in a 39-22 win over the Packers .
If Wentz can lead the Vikings to a win over the 6-1 Buffalo Bills on Monday night, that might change the Vikings' mind about making a deal for Jones, but if he struggles, then it wouldn't be surprising at all to see Minnesota try to make a move for a QB before the trade deadline (The Vikings did also have J.J. McCarthy at QB, but they traded him away to the Giants in late September .
One reason Jones would make a lot of sense for Minnesota is that Kevin O'Connell is already familiar with him. Jones spent the 2024 season in Minnesota and the Vikings actually wanted him back, but he ended up signing with the Colts because he felt like he had a better chance to start with them.
The Colts will definitely be a team to watch between now and Tuesday. Besides Jones, they could also trade Jonathan Taylor , but there's no guarantee that will happen.

title: Falcons vs. Bengals: What will Week 9’s win or loss mean for Atlanta?
summary: The Atlanta Falcons traverse the great Atlantic Ocean and make their way onto the old continent, where they set their anchor down in Madrid, Spain and the historic Stantiago Bernebéu Stadium for a meeting against the Cincinnati Bengals in a standalone matchup kicking off at 9:30 a.m. eastern time. The Falcons have once again dug […]
full_text: The Atlanta Falcons traverse the great Atlantic Ocean and make their way onto the old continent, where they set their anchor down in Madrid, Spain and the historic Stantiago Bernebéu Stadium for a meeting against the Cincinnati Bengals in a standalone matchup kicking off at 9:30 a.m. eastern time. The Falcons have once again dug themselves into a hole of their own making right as they looked poised to get back into water treading territory before a loss in the elements against the Buccaneers dropped them to 3-5 at around the season’s halfway mark. Next is a matchup against Joe Burrow and AFC hopeful Cincinnati, who sit with a 5-2 record in the midst of a bounce back campaign. The clock has started to tick on the Falcons in their pursuit of ending the longest active playoff draught in the NFC, as they get ready to play the final game before the trade deadline. Here is the scenario the Falcons face if they beat the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 9, as well as if they lose. If the Falcons win They will continue with the Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde identity of beating the good teams and losing the layups, a tendency that seems ingrained within their DNA at this point. To go from beating the 49ers to losing to Tampa to beating Cincy would seem inexplicable for most teams, but that’s not the case for an Atlanta team that has been doing this for years. The Falcons, who briefly took over first place in the NFC South with Carolina’s Thursday Night Football defeat last week, could find themselves back on top with a Panthers defeat against a good Broncos team and a Buccaneers defeat against a really good Bears team. Atlanta currently sits at 1-2 in the division, having lost head to head games against both Carolina and Tampa Bay, meaning that it may be imperative for them to finish with an outright better record than both if they want to win this divsion. Atlanta is not in an advantageous spot right now according to playoffstatus.com, with just a 23% chance at making the playoffs. In a best case scenario where the Panthers and Bucs lose, those chances would increase to 30%. The Birds would also end an active three game losing streak against the Bengals, as this would be their first head to head victory since 2010. If the Falcons lose It won’t quite be panic time, but we would be getting close. The Falcons would fall to 3-6 under Kevin Stefanski, which would be the worst nine game start for a first year Falcons head coach since Bobby Petrino had the same record in 2007. The division race could get a lot worse for Atlanta, as both Carolina and Tampa could start pulling away with their own victories. If the Saints also beat the Cleveland Browns, that would relegate the Falcons down to the basement of the NFC South. Those current 23% playoff odds could crater to as low as 14% if the worst case scenario of Carolina and Tampa also winning comes to pass, which might leave the Birds to do some serious soul searching and self evaluation ahead of the Tuesday trade deadline.

title: Intriguing players to watch in Falcons vs. Bengals
summary: The Atlanta Falcons square off against the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, desperate for a win to keep their playoff hopes alive after a heartbreaking loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. They’ll need several offensive players to bounce back from last week’s loss, and others to step up in critical matchups if the Falcons want to […]
full_text: VALDEBEBAS, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 05: Michael Penix Jr. of Atlanta Falcons attends during the NFL Madrid 2026, week of game, between Atlanta Falcons and Cincinnati Bengals at Ciudad Deportiva Real Madrid on November 05, 2026, in Madrid, Spain. (Photo By Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press via Getty Images) | Europa Press via Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons square off against the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, desperate for a win to keep their playoff hopes alive after a heartbreaking loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They’ll need several offensive players to bounce back from last week’s loss, and others to step up in critical matchups if the Falcons want to be celebrating a win on the flight home. Michael Penix Quarterback Michael Penix most needs a rebound game after playing the worst game of his career, tossing an uncharacteristic four interceptions against the Bucs. Penix has generally done an excellent job protecting the football and limiting negative plays throughout his career, so last week’s performance feels like an outlier. With Penix promising he’ll “shake back” after last week’s loss , seeing how that plays out on Sunday morning in Madrid will go a long way toward showing his resiliency as a passer. His injury history has made him resilient through the physical and mental hurdles of playing quarterback, so this should be another test. Bijan Robinson Falcons star running back Bijan Robinson has also been uncharacteristically underwhelming in recent weeks, admitting as much this week . After a dominant start, Robinson still leads the NFL in rushing, but the Falcons desperately need him to return to that early-season dominance against the Bengals. A key part of the Falcons’ strategy to slow down the Bengals’ high-scoring offense will be keeping it sidelined by controlling the clock with Bijan and the run game. Robinson is still capable of dynamic, explosive runs, but the blown protections on blitz pickups and dropped passes have been some of the areas where he has missed the mark recently. Shining in front of an international audience may be the spark that gets Bijan back to his usual brilliance. Ryan Neuzil Center Ryan Neuzil will face one of the toughest assignments in Madrid when he takes on Bengals defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence, who is off to a brilliant start this season. Neuzil and the rest of the Falcons’ interior offensive line will literally have their hands full against the 350-pound nose tackle. Lawrence is too good to be completely neutralized, but the Falcons must keep him from consistently wrecking the game. That’ll be important for their success not only in establishing the run with Robinson, but also in protecting Penix. A.J. Terrell Another marquee matchup will be that between cornerback A.J. Terrell and Bengals wideout Ja’Marr Chase. It represents a rematch from the 2020 National Championship game, when both were still at Clemson and LSU, respectively. Chase finished that game with 221 receiving yards and two touchdowns, most of which came at Terrell’s expense. That game alone led many to criticize the Falcons for “reaching” on Terrell in the 2020 NFL Draft , and Terrell has worked hard to silence his doubters since. It’s unlikely Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich will make the same mistake Clemson did six years ago: leaving Terrell on an island against Chase this go-round. But Terrell will likely find himself matched up with Chase often on Sunday morning, and if the Falcons want to slow down this high-flying Bengals aerial attack, this rematch will need to be a lot less lopsided. Jessie Bates Speaking of revenge, Falcons safety Jessie Bates likely will enter Sunday’s matchup with a chip on his shoulder facing his former team. Bates spent four years in Cincinnati, and that experience could be an X-factor in the Falcons slowing down the NFL’s second-highest scoring offense. But that familiarity goes both ways, as quarterback Joe Burrow is very much aware of Bates’ propensity to take the ball away. Yet, the better the opposing quarterback, the better Bates tends to play. Three of his last four interceptions have come against MVP candidates Brock Purdy, Matthew Stafford, and Drake Maye. If Bates can add another notch to his belt, the Falcons could add another upset win to their 2026 accolades. These five Falcons could have a critical impact on Sunday’s game in Madrid and determine whether it’s time for a fiesta or siesta on the flight home as the Falcons’ 2026 season reaches the midpoint. Can you name any other Falcons that intrigue you in this matchup?

title: Falcons vs. Bengals series history: Win-loss record, matchup results
summary: The Falcons head back into play against the AFC this week, and they do so across the pond in the second ever NFL game to be played in the Spanish capital of Madrid, at the esteemed Estadio de Santiago Bernebéu. Their opponent in that game will be the Cincinnati Bengals, who have won two games […]
full_text: 24 Nov 1996: Running back Jamal Anderson #32 of the Atlanta Falcons carries the football during the Falcons 41-31 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals at Riverfront Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio. Mandatory Credit: Jed Jacobsohn /Allsport | Getty Images The Falcons head back into play against the AFC this week, and they do so across the pond in the second ever NFL game to be played in the Spanish capital of Madrid, at the esteemed Estadio de Santiago Bernebéu. Their opponent in that game will be the Cincinnati Bengals, who have won two games out of every three against the Birds, owning a very aesthetically pleasing 10-5 all time record against Atlanta. The majority of that damage came before the turn of the millennia, with the Bengals winning seven out of 10 matchups against the overmatched Falcons through the 1996 season, with games between these teams happening on averaged every three years in that time period. The Birds pulled back a little bit with three consecutive victories — in 2002, 2006 and 2010 — to pull the series close to even. That was quickly followed with three straight Bengals victories which brings us to where we are today, with two of those coming in the Matt Ryan era, which was also the most successful one in Falcons history. The Bengals caught Atlanta in a down year of that era twice in a row, in 2014 and 2018. When these teams met last The Falcons had some confidence about them in year 2 of the Arthur Smith regime, having just pulled back to .500 at 3-3, with a victory against the 49ers after some questionable reffing cost them against Tampa the week before. The Bengals sported the same record, but they proved from the start that they were on another level. It took exactly two minutes for second year man Joe Burrow to hit Tyler Boyd on a 60-yard touchdown to open the scoring. Then after a Falcon punt, the Bengals punched the ball in again following a longer drive. Then an Atlanta three and out was followed with a Burrow to rookie Ja’Marr Chase touchdown on the first play of the second quarter, before the two connected in the end zone again on the back end of the same quarter. By halftime the game was effectively over as the Falcon offense spent the second half completely one dimensional and getting terrorized by the Bengal defense, with Burrow putting the finishing touches on with a rushing score to complete his magnificent day. Up 35-17, one of the most impressive feats by the Bengal offense was getting the ball back via punt at their own 3-yard-line (why the Falcons punted it near midfield down three scores in the fourth quarter I don’t know) with 8:44 left in the game and choking away that entire clock (and all three Atlanta timeouts) with a 17-play drive which went 95 yards and ended in a kneel down.

title: The Falcoholic Reacts: Uncertainty about Michael Penix Jr.’s outlook

They were manhandled in the trenches. They couldn’t convert on third down, no matter the distance. Tackling became a persistent problem. For all […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Michael Penix Jr. #9 of the Atlanta Falcons runs against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the second half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images How the Falcons lost to Tampa Bay left scars within the fanbase. Regardless of the nasty conditions, it was a winnable game against an opponent without any semblance of a passing game. They were manhandled in the trenches. They couldn’t convert on third down, no matter the distance. Tackling became a persistent problem. For all those issues, nothing was more concerning than Michael Penix Jr.’s performance. He was making self-inflicted errors you don’t see from a starting-caliber quarterback. Although Penix Jr. can throw with anticipation well at times, it was detrimental against Todd Bowles’ defense. From failing to identify defenders dropping into coverage to throwing into passing windows that didn’t exist, his performance was alarming in how rudimentary his mistakes were. That has left fans very concerned about his ability to be a franchise quarterback. It’s worrying times for the Falcons. They play against two top contenders before the bye week. Expecting Penix Jr. to go throw for throw with Joe Burrow and Patrick Mahomes would be unfair. He needs to play significantly better to show the Falcons can compete with top offenses. That will go a long way toward rebuilding the team’s confidence after a catastrophic display in Tampa Bay. This result is brought to you by FanDuel Sportsbook.

title: Ravens film study: Zion Young stepping up after Tavius Robinson injury
summary: The Buffalo Bills handled the Baltimore Ravens 36-10 in Buffalo last Sunday, in a game that quickly went downhill after starting quarterback Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley both suffered potentially season-ending injuries. Despite the lopsided score, Baltimore’s defense showed some signs of life, with two players standing out on tape. Roquan Smith arguably put […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Zion Young #9 of the Baltimore Ravens reacts against the Buffalo Bills during an NFL football game at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills handled the Baltimore Ravens 36-10 in Buffalo last Sunday, in a game that quickly went downhill after starting quarterback Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley both suffered potentially season-ending injuries. Despite the lopsided score, Baltimore’s defense showed some signs of life, with two players standing out on tape. Roquan Smith arguably put together his best performance as a Raven, while rookie Zion Young continued to show why he could be an important piece of Baltimore’s defense moving forward. OLB Zion Young 35 snaps | 21 run defense | 14 pass rush | 1 tackle | 1 assist | 1 pressure Zion Young’s box score may not immediately stand out, but turning on the tape reveals the type of impact that makes his long-term outlook so intriguing. Young finished with 1 tackle, 1 assist and 1 pressure while recording a 100% pass-rush win rate on true pass sets. While the statistical production was limited, his ability to affect running lanes, displace blockers and maintain gap integrity was evident throughout the afternoon. Young continues to show that his value extends well beyond traditional box-score production. Decade long starter in the NFL pic.twitter.com/Kje0Z148Lh — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) November 3, 2026 One of Young’s most impressive traits throughout the season has been his ability to work down the line of scrimmage against the run, and Sunday was no different. On one rep, Young worked laterally down the line and made a key tackle to prevent Josh Allen from sneaking into the end zone. On another, he flashed his physicality and hand usage, displacing a blocker and forcing the running back to redirect into a different rushing lane. Perhaps his most impressive rep came when he engaged two blockers simultaneously and drove both into the backfield, disrupting the timing of the run and allowing the rest of Baltimore’s defense to rally to the football. With Tavius Robinson sidelined, Young is expected to assume a larger role as Baltimore’s starting outside linebacker on early downs. His ability to set a firm edge, maintain gap discipline and use his length and power at the point of attack makes him a natural fit for that responsibility. Young has consistently demonstrated the technique, physicality and effort necessary to succeed as an early-down defender. The next step in his development will be expanding his opportunities as a pass rusher, where his power profile and developing arsenal of moves offer intriguing upside. As his workload continues to increase, Young has an opportunity to establish himself as a foundational piece of Baltimore’s defensive front. LB Roquan Smith 52 snaps | 25 run defense | 3 pass rush | 24 coverage | 8 tackles | 4 assists | 1 pressure | 1 forced fumble Roquan Smith arguably had his best performance as a Raven against Buffalo, flying around the field in coverage, flowing downhill against the run and making key tackles both in the backfield and in open space. Smith finished with 8 tackles, 4 assists, 1 pressure and a forced fumble while allowing just 1 reception for 16 yards in coverage. One of the most impressive aspects of his performance was his ability to consistently put himself in position to make plays, showing the instincts, physicality and range that have made him one of the league’s premier linebackers. Probably Roquan Smiths best game as a Raven pic.twitter.com/WJqNSq19jv — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) November 3, 2026 On one rep, Smith flashed his ability as a power rusher, knocking back a Buffalo offensive guard and driving him into Josh Allen’s lap. Against the run, Smith consistently displayed excellent spatial awareness, navigating around blockers to keep himself clean and meet running backs in the hole. On a toss play to James Cook, Smith showed excellent tackling technique and body control to bring him down in open space. His biggest play of the afternoon came on a shot over the middle, where he rallied to the football and punched it loose to force a fumble that Baltimore recovered. After receiving a pregame speech from Ravens legend Ray Lewis, Smith delivered arguably his most complete performance of the season. His play over the past several weeks has been inconsistent, particularly compared to the standard he has established throughout his career. However, Sunday’s performance was an encouraging reminder of the impact he can have when playing with confidence and decisiveness. If Smith can build on this performance, it could go a long way toward helping Baltimore’s defense return to form. has an opportunity to establish himself as a foundational piece of Baltimore’s defensive front.

title: Roquan Smith fined twice by NFL for penalties in Ravens vs. Bills in Week 8
summary: Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith was hit with two fines for his play in Week 8’s loss to the Buffalo Bills. In total, Smith will pony up almost $36,000 for two penalties last Sunday. One fine was connected to unnecessary roughness for this play, where Smith not only grabbed Bills quarterback Josh Allen’s facemask, but twisted […]
full_text: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images | Getty Images Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith was hit with two fines for his play in Week 8’s loss to the Buffalo Bills. In total, Smith will pony up almost $36,000 for two penalties last Sunday. One fine was connected to unnecessary roughness for this play, where Smith not only grabbed Bills quarterback Josh Allen’s facemask, but twisted it almost 180 degrees. Is Josh Allen part owl? Roquan Smith twisted his neck nearly 180 degrees on his touchdown run. #BillsMafia @BuffaloPlus pic.twitter.com/92orE2nEeJ — Dan Fetes (@danfetes) November 2, 2026 The second fine stemmed from unnecessary roughness penalty for a hit on a defenseless player not even a full minute into the game. Week 8’s fines make three total for Smith during the 2026 season. He was also fined $11,941 for unnecessary roughness stemming from a face mask in Week 2. That’s why Week 8’s fines were almost $18,000 each — because they weren’t the first this season. No other Ravens players were fined in Week 8. No Bills players were fined for that contest. The NFL donates half the fines it collects to the NFLPA’s efforts to support retired players, and the other half to the NFL Foundation and organizations supporting youth football programs, community health and wellness, and athlete safety.

full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills runs the ball in for a touchdown as Roquan Smith #0 of the Baltimore Ravens tries to make a tackle during a game at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images Baltimore Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith had an expensive day in Orchard Park, NY last weekend. Smith received a heavy dose of fines for his on-field efforts against the Buffalo Bills in Week 8. He was fined a total of $35,822 for two infractions, one against quarterback Josh Allen, and a second against wide receiver DJ Moore. The NFL handed Smith a fine of $17,911 for a facemask grab and tug he implemented on quarterback Josh Allen during a successful touchdown sneak, per Tom Pelissero . During the play, Smith was observed grabbing Allen’s facemask while trying to pull him back, then pulling and twisting the helmet aggressively until it ended up completely backwards — and with Allen’s head and neck turning almost a complete 180 degrees. Smith wasn’t penalized following the play. Here’s a closer look via still shots available from the play: Smith was also received an additional fine of $17,911 for unsportsmanlike conduct, which the NFL levied as a hit on a defenseless player. Sal Capaccio of WGR 550 noted that the particular play involved Smith hitting Moore as he was “ going across the middle in the 1st quarter as the ball was thrown elsewhere .” Many wondered if Smith would face discipline following the now-viral play against Allen. He seems to have avoided suspension despite a pattern of concern, as evidenced by Smith’s availability for Thursday Night Football in Week 9, just a few days ago. Smith is a highly decorated defensive mercenary. This week, however, he’s the one taking a huge hit where it hurts — thanks to a decent bit less of the typical $1,176,470.59 he’s paid per game in 2026.

title: 5 Minnesota Vikings to watch vs. the Buffalo Bills
summary: The Buffalo Bills and the Minnesota Vikings are set to face off on Monday night in a battle of two 6-1 teams. The Bills are the current No. 1 seed in the AFC, and while the Vikings are the No. 2 seed, depending on the result of the San Francisco 49ers’ matchup with the Las […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills and the Minnesota Vikings are set to face off on Monday night in a battle of two 6-1 teams. The Bills are the current No. 1 seed in the AFC, and while the Vikings are the No. 2 seed, depending on the result of the San Francisco 49ers’ matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, Minnesota could be playing as the technical No. 1 seed when their game kicks off Monday night. The Bills currently have the NFL’s top scoring offense, as head coach Joe Brady’s bunch averages 33.3 points per game so far this season. Minnesota, on the other hand, has the NFL’s top scoring defense, as defensive coordinator Brian Flores’ charges allow just 13.3 points per game so far this year. Minnesota’s offense is ranked just 27th in the league; Buffalo’s defense is ranked just 24th. In a lot of ways, these two teams are polar opposites; however, they’re similar in the most important way: They win football games. And, if Buffalo wants to improve their mark to 7-1 this season, they’ll need to turn in another stellar defensive performance against a backup quarterback, albeit one with much more starting experience than their last opponent. Here are five Vikings to watch on Monday night. _____________________________________________________________________________ QB Carson Wentz In some ways, having Wentz start the game might present greater problems for Buffalo than Kyler Murray, who is Minnesota’s normal starter. Murray is out with a sore hamstring, and while he is a great scrambler, he’s not as good a pure passer as Wentz is. Wentz was once rather mobile, but injuries and age have slowed him down, and he’s not close to the player he was when he was an MVP front-runner with the Philadelphia Eagles back in 2019. I expect the Bills to take a page out of the Brian Flores playbook—or the Week Eight Jim Leonhard playbook, even—by blitzing Wentz early and often. Buffalo blitzed on nearly two-thirds of their defensive snaps last week. Doing that again while setting a solid edge will keep Wentz in the pocket and cause him to process quickly. If he has time to throw, he’ll find receivers. If he’s rushed, he’ll look to dump the ball off before taking big hits, which could lead to some turnovers for a Buffalo defense looking for a second straight week of solid play. WR Justin Jefferson Jefferson will always be a “what-if” for Buffalo, even if that characterization isn’t necessarily fair. Yes, he was drafted by the Vikings with the first-round pick Buffalo sent to Minnesota in exchange for Stefon Diggs. While some people say that the Bills just could have drafted Jefferson rather than making the trade, there was no way to tell exactly what Jefferson would become, or even if he would be available when Buffalo picked. If draft choices are lottery tickets, stud veterans are closer to sure bets, and for the better part of four seasons, Diggs was as sure a bet as there was in the NFL. With all that said, Jefferson is Buffalo’s problem this week, and I’d expect to see No. 47, Christian Benford, lined up across from him more often than not. If Jefferson is matched up against literally anyone else in Buffalo’s secondary, I’d expect Wentz to throw that way. If he’s covered by Benford, we at least know that it’s Buffalo’s best on Minnesota’s best. That matchup is one of the biggest keys of the game. OLB Andrew Van Ginkel The veteran is a Brian Flores staple, as he was teamed with Flores during his time with the Miami Dolphins. As a result, the Bills and quarterback Josh Allen are quite familiar with Van Ginkel and his flowing locks. The big edge rusher is having a great year so far, as he leads the Vikings with 6.5 sacks and seven tackles for loss. Guard Alec Anderson did not practice on Thursday with an ankle issue, and tackles Dion Dawkins (rib) and Spencer Brown (back) were out of practice and limited in it, respectively. Buffalo’s offensive line is beat up a little bit, and it’s not a great time for that to happen. No time is great for a banged-up offensive line, but a date with the league’s No. 1 defense is basically the worst time for that to be the case. Regardless of who’s at tackle, the Bills will have to account for Van Ginkel on Monday. OLB Dallas Turner They’ll also have to look out for Van Ginkel’s teammate, as Turner has six sacks and a team-high 19 quarterback hits this season. The third-year man is improving on his breakout 2025 campaign, and he’s on pace to surpass his 2025 sack total (8) by plenty this season. At the risk of sounding like I just teleported in from 1992, Buffalo’s best bet to slow the pass rush might be to establish the running game early. Play-action passes on first down can give the Vikings’ edge rushers pause, and some solid second-down runs can slow them further. Minnesota is allowing opponents to average 4.5 yards per rush, and given that the Bills average 4.8 yards per rush on the season, it’s a strength on offense and a weakness for Minneosta’s defense in what has otherwise been an outstanding unit. This might be a James Cook III day moreso than a Josh Allen day if Buffalo is going to come out on top. Cook can help keep his quarterback clean by breaking some big runs, which should hopefully make the Vikings’ stellar edge rushers hesitate before pinning their ears back and going full-force into pass-rush mode. CB Byron Murphy No name bias here, but Murphy is a stud. He’s allowing just a 57.3 quarterback rating this season when he’s the closest man in coverage, as he has three interceptions and six pass breakups while allowing zero touchdowns on 40 pass attempts his way. He’s really playing better than he has at any point in his career. Buffalo’s passing offense has been outstanding, but against the league’s No. 1 pass defense, it might be wise to avoid the guy who’s currently having a career-year. The problem, of course, is that James Pierre and Isaiah Rodgers are also playing extremely well. What if I told you that, despite the numbers listed above, Murphy is still the guy allowing the greatest percentage of completed passes on this defense, as he’s allowed a 65% completion rate for 310 yards. Compared to Pierre (47.6%, 20.2 passer rating against) and Rodgers (33.3% competion rate, 34.7 passer rating against), Murphy might actually be the one performing the worst at the moment. This is a really good defense. The Bills will have to pick their poison. Murphy might be it.

title: Buffalo Bills fan confidence makes huge rebound ahead of Week 9
summary: After watching the Buffalo Bills thrash the mostly listless Baltimore Ravens in Week 8, Bills Mafia is once again buying what Buffalo’s selling. Now 6-1 and in sole possession of first place in the AFC, the Bills currently control their playoff destiny. Hopefully that includes earning the one seed, but there’s plenty of football to […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates after a touchdown against the Baltimore Ravens during an NFL football game at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images After watching the Buffalo Bills thrash the mostly listless Baltimore Ravens in Week 8, Bills Mafia is once again buying what Buffalo’s selling. Now 6-1 and in sole possession of first place in the AFC, the Bills currently control their playoff destiny. Hopefully that includes earning the one seed, but there’s plenty of football to play before deciding that situation. As is true with most seasons since quarterback Josh Allen rose to NFL royalty, fans have the biggest expectations of Buffalo — things like AFC Championships and Super Bowl wins. Everyone understands it’s also true that time as constructed is limited, and that Allen loses opportunity with each passing season. Reading the tea leaves, that idea loomed large in co-owner Terry Pegula’s decision to fire former head coach Sean McDermott. Time is short, and much of it had been “wasted” heading into this season. Accolades, stats, and places in the sport’s history are each incredible to claim in their own right, yet they pale when considering that elusive Lombardi Trophy. Enter new head coach Joe Brady and his equally new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. Both men get their first shot at NFL stardom with arguably the NFL’s biggest and most-talented star leading the way. No pressure to be perfect, right? That’s just it. Perfection is all but guaranteed, yet that’s what so many Bills fans have demanded of the 2026 season because it seems absurd that Allen hasn’t so much as even played in a Super Bowl to this point in time. Nevermind that, yes, the team does have a first-time head coach and defensive coordinator. Nevermind that the defense underwent a huge overhaul in scheme. Nevermind that other NFL teams have the same goals. Somehow, beating a downtrodden Ravens team that filtered through to its emergency quarterback was all that some still-skeptical fans needed to express their support of the Bills this season. Our latest Reacts results reveal that 86% of voters are confident in the team’s direction under Brady and president of football operations/general manger Brandon Beane. It’s a jump of 23 percentage points from last week’s 63% confidence rating. The defense played a fantastic game, and quite honestly safety Damar Hamlin looked like the perfect fit as an emotional and schematic leader for Leonhard’s system. If nothing else, it speaks to the potential of an aggressive and tough defense lying in wait. That complementing the league’s top-scoring offense (and one in first by a large margin) should be enough to get Buffalo where is needs to be by season’s end. But they must continue playing this brand of football, and find the right amount of luck at the right time. The Bills get to play another purple-clad team in Week 9, this time hoping to put a stamp on their signature offensive attack in front of another national audience. If you’re still unsure about Buffalo this season, what has to happen to change your mind? We also asked Rumblers to weigh in with their positional wishlist ahead of the NFL trade deadline. Despite the great game Hamlin played, it’s likely unsurprising that the safety position led our poll results. We’re not talking by just a few percentage points, either. A massive 72% of votes went toward adding a safety. The next closest position was linebacker. Wide receiver garnered just 9% of the vote, and only 3% of voters saw fit to add elsewhere to the Bills’ roster. As if you needed a reminder, the results from one of this week’s national polls revealed that Josh Allen is viewed as the NFL MVP through Week 8. Buffalo’s opponent in Week 9, the Minnesota Vikings, also sport a 6-1 record. The Vikings have a championship-caliber defense that might not be getting enough attention at the moment. But the offense has been a bit inconsistent too often with either Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz at quarterback. Now, rumors suggest Minnesota could be in the market to trade for a quarterback. A lot of that will depend on how things go during Monday Night Football. However, it appears the situation on offense has the SKOL family second-guessing the team’s direction this season. Mind you, Minnesota just lost and it’s their first defeat of the season. That somehow has just 17% of Vikings fans confident in the current direction of their favorite team. Think you’ve got what it takes to make a play with the Buffalo Bills in 2026? Head over to FanDuel Sportsbook now and put it to the test !

title: 5 Buffalo Bills to watch at the Minnesota Vikings
summary: The Buffalo Bills are off to a great start, sitting at 6-1 atop the entire AFC. The Minnesota Vikings are also off to a great start, and they are second in the NFC with a a6-1 record, as they are currently tired with the San Francisco 49ers. The Vikings have the NFL’s best defense. The […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills are off to a great start, sitting at 6-1 atop the entire AFC. The Minnesota Vikings are also off to a great start, and they are second in the NFC with a a6-1 record, as they are currently tired with the San Francisco 49ers. The Vikings have the NFL’s best defense. The Bills have the NFL’s best offense. Something’s gotta give, as the move title suggests, and while I don’t expect to see Jack Nicholson in this one—or Diane Keaton, for that matter—I do expect to see a darn good football game. If the Bills are going to come out on top, they’ll need all of their top players to perform to their capability. Here are five Bills to watch on Monday night. _____________________________________________________________________________ QB Josh Allen In a game like this, Allen has to avoid trying to do too much. Just take the checkdown. Take the easy money. Take the thing the defense gives you so that you can sustain the drive. Don’t come out juiced up trying to be a hero from the jump. Just play within the system, hit your keys, focus on your reads, and throw it to the guys wearing white helmets. If you do that, you’re probably going to leave Minnesota with a win. If you hold the ball, force it downfield into double coverage, and try to make chicken salad out of a far less desireable byproduct of chicken feed? Well, this is a defense that will make you pay. Allen doesn’t need to be Superman for the Bills to win on Monday. He just needs to be Josh Allen. RB James Cook III IF this stellar Vikings defense has a weakness, it’s the running game. They’re currently allowing opposing teams to average 4.5 yards per carry. That doesn’t bode well for the Vikings against the NFL’s third-best rushing offense. Cook averages 5.1 yards per carry this season, and Buffalo’s second-leading rusher—Allen—averages 4.9 yards per rush. If those two can take off, look out. The Bills worked Ray Davis into the rotation a bit more last week, which was nice to see. I’d like to see them do that a little bit more on Monday, as well, as Davis offers a different build and different running style to Cook. If Buffalo’s top back can find his footing, though, it will go a long way towards keeping the Bills on schedule, which will lead to points. Injured Offensive Linemen Which Buffalo offensive linemen will play? Alec Anderson missed Thursday’s practice with an ankle injury—is Austin Corbett going to slot in and start? Dion Dawkins missed practice with a rib injury—is Tylan Grable going to play left tackle just one week after starting in place of Spencer Brown at right tackle? Speaking of Brown, he was limited in practice thanks to his back injury. What happens if both he and Dawkins can’t suit up? Rookie Jude Bowry was terrible in the preseason, so making his first career start against the NFL’s top defense isn’t exactly ideal. The Bills could move Anderson out to tackle in pinch, but again, if he’s hurt too…what do the Bills do? The offensive line, and who is able to play, is a huge area of concern this week. LB Terrel Bernard Minnesota’s second most frequently targets receiver is tight end T.J. Hockenson. Bernard has been playing much better of late, as he seems to be settling in a touch in new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard’s scheme. The Vikings have struggled this year on offense, averaging just 20 points and 279 yards per game. However, Buffalo’s defense has also struggled, allowing 26 points and 352 yards per game. If Bernard can combine with Buffalo’s other linebackers and slot players to limit Hockenson, it will go a long way towards stymying a mid-level Minnesota offense. If he can’t, well, it could lead to a scenario where the moveable force (Buffalo’s defense) is pushed around by the immoveable object (Minnesota’s offense). Hopefully, Bernard continues his upward trajectory this week. CB Christian Benford Minnesota’s top receiving target needs no introduction, as Justin Jefferson is one of the NFL’s elite receivers. After a poor start to the season, Benford has thrived the last two games as an eraser for the opposing team’s top target. He traveled with Raiders’ tight end Brock Bowers and largely eliminated him from the game in Buffalo’s 33-30 victory three weeks ago. Then, last week, he traveled with Baltimore Ravens’ wideout Zay Flowers and completely erased him from the game, as Flowers logged the first zero-catch game of his career. Benford is a legitimate stud corner, and Jefferson is a legitimate stud wideout. This is a premier matchup, and I expect it to be one of the biggest keys to the entire game for both teams. If Benford can limit Jefferson, it will give the Bills a huge boost in the game.

title: Report: Buffalo Bills are looking to trade for defensive back
summary: This is not exactly a shock, but now we have a report from a national insider about what the Buffalo Bills are looking for at the NFL trade deadline. That insider is Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer. I recently tweeted the lack of reports this season represents a stark contrast to recent years, when the Bills […]
full_text: This is not exactly a shock, but now we have a report from a national insider about what the Buffalo Bills are looking for at the NFL trade deadline. That insider is Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer. I recently tweeted the lack of reports this season represents a stark contrast to recent years, when the Bills were listed in essentially every trade-deadline insight article in the weeks leading up to the deadline. Now, there was one mention of the Bills’ intentions, from Breer, in late October. We wrote about here at Rumblings. It was one sentence and relatively vague compared to the rest of the mentions pertaining to other teams and trade chips. “ The Bills are looking for another piece or two on defense .” This time around, in a response to a tweet that highlighted the lack of a Bills mention in his latest trade-deadline article , Breer wrote this: I had it in my last trade column, and will add it here—The Bills are still looking in to adding a piece on the defensive side of the ball. And specifically at corner and safety. https://t.co/CkjvAiQRLa — Albert Breer (@AlbertBreer) November 7, 2026 The positions are the unexpected part. However, the Bills have recently added Tre’Davious White and Kader Kohou to the practice squad at cornerback. They just got a quality effort from Te’Cory Couch in the slot. At safety, Jordan Hancock is close to returning. Damar Hamlin is playing sound football. Geno Stone tied for the team lead in tackles with six against the Ravens on just 19 snaps, and he tipped a pass that led to Davison Igbinosun’s first career interception. According to Breer, the Bills are want to add a defensive back at the trade deadline. We’ll see if it happens.

title: Discussion: How different do you expect the Panthers defense to look today?
summary: The last discussion post I put up asked about the warmth of Ejiro Evero’s seat. He’s been fired in the meantime, so I’d say it was pretty hot. It comes after an okay performance against the Green Bay Packers, but that’s probably more a product of convenience than anything. The Panthers were on a short […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 15: Carolina Panthers defensive line coach Todd Wash looks on during the first half of the game against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium on October 15, 2023 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images The last discussion post I put up asked about the warmth of Ejiro Evero’s seat. He’s been fired in the meantime, so I’d say it was pretty hot. It comes after an okay performance against the Green Bay Packers, but that’s probably more a product of convenience than anything. The Panthers were on a short week, so if the decision was made after the Buccaneers game, it would make more sense to wait a few extra days and make the move after the Thursday night game. In Ejiro’s place is Todd Wash. Wash overlapped with Dave Canales in Seattle in 2011 and 2012. He spent time as defensive coordinator in Jacksonville and led three units that were top six in yards allowed per game before things unraveled under Doug Marrone. He’s been the defensive line coach in Carolina since 2023 and was retained when Canales was hired in 2024. Now he gets his shot at defensive coordinator. He’s talked about changing the approach a little bit, and today’s discussion questions centers around that idea. How different do you expect the defense to look in the first week under Todd Wash? MY TAKE: I think we’ll see a difference for a couple of different reasons. First, the approach is supposed to be different under Wash. Not in a 4-3 vs 3-4 way, which seems to be an obsession of reporters for some reason, but rather a proactive mentality rather than a reactive one. From everything I’ve gathered, Evero preferred his defensive line to try to read the play before making a move. This often requires the linemen to absorb blockers before attempting to make a play. Wash has said he wants the line to be more proactive, which would mean prioritizing breaking the line of scrimmage first and then making a play. In his first press conference, Wash said the latter is what a lot of the linemen here played before they got to Carolina. He avoided saying it outright, but the implication is that this more aggressive approach on the line is a better fit for the personnel. On top of that, there are few better ways to galvanize a group of players than to fire their leader. Whether they were fans of Evero or not, the boss getting fired puts everyone on notice. There is going to be an extra bit of fire coming from all the guys, be it because of a fresh approach, a new voice, or the pressure imposed by the firing of someone in one’s vicinity. A new approach doesn’t necessarily mean more success. I don’t necessarily think the defense is going to be significantly better in its first week with a new coordinator. I expect there will be missed assignments and some growing pains. But I do think we’ll see a more disruptive defensive line that will muck things up against a disjointed Broncos offense.

title: 5 questions with Mile High Report
summary: The Denver Broncos are coming to Charlotte today with a slim hope of exceeding the 11 sacks that the Carolina Panthers have surrendered in the past two weeks. To figure out how slim that chance was—or not—and if Sean Payton has already worn out his welcome in Denver, I spoke with Laurie Lattimore-Volkmann over at […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 1: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks on before the game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The Denver Broncos won 28-24. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos are coming to Charlotte today with a slim hope of exceeding the 11 sacks that the Carolina Panthers have surrendered in the past two weeks. To figure out how slim that chance was—or not—and if Sean Payton has already worn out his welcome in Denver, I spoke with Laurie Lattimore-Volkmann over at Mile High Report. Here’s what she had to say about that, Bo Nix’s struggles, and more. Bo Nix has not been having the season that many in Broncos country have been hoping for. What has held him back and how will he look to step his game up against the Panthers? A lot has been made of Bo’s offseason ankle surgery/recovery for his slow start to the season. I won’t discount that that has likely played a role, despite him and the coaches saying he was feeling “just as mobile” at the beginning of the season as he had before the injury. Anyone who has competed in sports knows there is a mental hurdle to get past when coming back from an injury. But my guess is that it was a combination of many things, beginning with a little hesitation leftover from the injury, learning new terminology when Davis Webb did the play-calling, and playing the first six games against at least five of the top defenses in the league. A much smaller factor, but still one I believe impacted his play, is that Bo became a new dad this summer. Anyone who has kids and can remember that first year knows that you don’t get anywhere near enough sleep. Some may laugh at that reason, but I believe it’s impacted him a little. Watching Bo at the press conferences, it’s clear he is exhausted and has zero f**** to give any naysayers. That’s what being a new parent does to you! Sean Payton is not a name that is greeted with respect or warmth in the Carolinas. How has his reception been so far in Denver? A winning coach is always welcomed with open arms. Payton probably had to win over a few fans initially, but given the sh*tshow that preceded him, it didn’t take much. He runs a tight ship, has great vision for the short and long-term plan for the team and has produced a winning product every season. And given that the rookie QB he chose to lead the team has worked out well, it means Payton is quite popular here. The story of the season so far for the Carolina Panthers so far has been injuries. The most impactful have been along their offensive line. Does Denver try to generate pressure from the edge, the interior, from blitzing, or all of the above? Panthers fans would like to know which weakness to be most afraid of on Sunday. Unfortunately for Bryce Young, there’s not much of a weakness for your depleted O-line to take advantage of. Vance Joseph is phenomenal at disguising looks and bringing pressure – which is a dangerous combo. He doesn’t blitz a ton, but it’s generally effective when he does. Zach Allen and Malcolm Roach will generate a lot of pressure up the middle, allowing Nik Bonitto and Jonathan Cooper a good chance at the QB. And even when they don’t get the sack, they can still rattle the quarterback enough to cause trouble for your offense. The defensive weakness to exploit is the linebackers, who are good tacklers but not particularly fast, as well as a slew of backup corners. But to do that, Young has to get to the receivers first. Similarly, the secondary has been gutted by injuries, with three of their top four corners already on injured reserve and the fourth having yet to participate in practice this week. That has allowed the Panthers to surrender some historic rushing totals. Have Denver’s rushing struggles this season come from trouble with their offensive line or from their running backs not being able to break tackles in the secondary? That is a great question and if you can figure it out, Broncos Country would be thrilled. Every offseason we buy the hype that our running backs will finally be the group to take our run game to the next level. And every season, it seems like we spend a lot of energy in post-game commentary wondering where the run game is. I believe the play-calling/scheme is the main culprit. But we also haven’t put a ton of draft or free agent capital into the position, so there is usually a lower ceiling with our RB room than we’d like to admit (which is why early rumors of Jonathan Taylor being traded to Denver had a lot of fans salivating). But there is a lot of hope for rookie Jonah Coleman and even second-year back RJ Harvey if he/they can stay healthy. If only Payton and Webb can commit to the run and create effective plays for it, there might be a chance. At 6-2, the Broncos are riding pretty high at the moment. How confident are their fans in a win in Charlotte? Do you have a score prediction? I think most fans are highly confident but also not immune to the fear of a trap game and/or the reality of how Broncos tend to play East Coast games (they haven’t played particularly well in the 1 p.m. EST slot)! But as long as the Broncos don’t beat themselves in the first half, I think the odds of a win are quite good. I’ll go with Denver 28, Carolina 17.

title: Reacts Results: Settling expectations into the gutter
summary: Go back into the comments this week on almost any article and you’ll find a number of our readers referencing “shuffling the deck chairs on the titanic.” That’s the mood across the Carolina Panthers fandom after two consecutive, demoralizing losses that have highlighted both the weaknesses of the coaching staff and the limitations of this […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 18: Luke Fortner #77 of the Carolina Panthers defends against the Philadelphia Eagles during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on October 18, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Go back into the comments this week on almost any article and you’ll find a number of our readers referencing “shuffling the deck chairs on the titanic.” That’s the mood across the Carolina Panthers fandom after two consecutive, demoralizing losses that have highlighted both the weaknesses of the coaching staff and the limitations of this heavily injured roster. Fan confidence, which was riding in the 90s for a couple of week as the Panthers built themselves up to a 3-2 record after their early bye week, has cratered. The inability of the remains of Carolina’s offensive line to do anything with much success has hamstrung the high-flying offense that began the season with hopes of an NFL-leading passer and whispers of the MVP conversation. Now, instead of an award, the team views a first down as a lofty aspiration. Staff firings aren’t surprising with these kinds of confidence numbers. Many have been out on Evero for years as his “bend but don’t break” style of defense too often broke. What is telling, however, is that most Panthers fans don’t think his removal moves the needle much. Head coach Dave Canales has a battle ahead of him to not lose the fanbase entirely. From one perspective, it is simple: start winning again. From another, it is much harder. Just as fans are right not to expect major changes for a unit devastated by injury just because their much-maligned leader has been fired, fans also shouldn’t expect a massive change in the Panthers ability to compete. They are fielding what is, at many positions, a roster with less reliable or less heralded players than they had during the preseason. Cornerback and left guard have been particularly affected. Left tackle, center, and right guard have experienced much less turmoil and yet also been somehow more disappointing as the season has worn on. Some of that blame is rightly laid at Canales’ feet. Coaching plays a part in every players performance and the buck stops with him on that front. Some if it, however, comes down to luck and the players. Injuries, regressions, and mistakes are things that happen. It takes a team effort to overcome them and, for the moment, that effort seems lacking across the board. title: Bears vs. Buccaneers: Game Picks and Predictions
summary: Sunday night at Soldier Field closes out a three-game prime-time stretch for a 6-2 Bears team that just beat the defending Super Bowl champions in Seattle.
