full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 17: Lavonte David #54 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers attempts to tackle Cole Kmet #85 of the Chicago Bears during the second quarter at Raymond James Stadium on September 17, 2023 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sunday night at Soldier Field closes out a three-game prime-time stretch for a 6-2 Bears team that just beat the defending Super Bowl champions in Seattle. Chicago’s high-powered offense and top-tier rushing attack host a 3-5 Buccaneers squad that has won two straight (despite not completing a single pass in their last game) and boasts the NFL’s top ground game led by Bucky Irving. The Bears are favored by about six points, but Tampa Bay’s physical run defense and Baker Mayfield’s ability to keep games close make this a real test before the bye. Several prominent national analysts have pointed to this game as a trap/upset in the making. What follows are our score pick, winner, and projected stat lines for a Sunday Night Football matchup that could push Chicago deeper into the NFC race. Sunday, November 8, 2026 , at Soldier Field . Kickoff: 7:20 p.m. CT (8:20 p.m. ET) TV: NBC Streaming: Peacock and NFL+ (Chicago area) Radio: ESPN Chicago (1000 AM / 100.3 FM HD2) and LATINO MIX 93.5 FM (Spanish) National broadcast team is Mike Tirico (play-by-play), Cris Collinsworth (analyst), and Melissa Stark (sideline). Local Bears radio is Jeff Joniak, Tom Thayer, and Jason McKie. Our Game Scores and Predictions Josh : I think the Bucs get their yards in the air this game, with Chicago’s depleted secondary giving up a pair of scores and the run game getting them into field goal range. By contrast, I think Chicago’s offense doesn’t miss a beat and they hang a pair through the air and a pair on the ground with a Santos field goal to round it out. 31-17 Bears. Jeff Berckes : There’s something about what this Bears team is building, where we’re at on the schedule, and the narrative that feels like there’s an outburst coming. Bucs defense is good, I’m not discounting that – I just think the offensive operation is getting to a level of inevitability. Defense, empowered by the Jeffery Simmons move, want to show out at home. Bears 41 – Bucs 13. Sam : I’m no longer scared of good defenses. But that doesn’t make this game a walk in the park. The Bears are due for a letdown. It’s a tough spot — three straight primetime games and the bye week looming. I think the Bucs’ defense keeps them in the game, but Chicago still gets theirs and Rome Odunze breaks through for a touchdown. The defense is stymied by a good Bucs OL and the run defense struggles. I just can’t trust Baker to suddenly wake up the passing game, but I can’t rule it out. His thumb has to be healing. Bears still have enough to get it done, but the Bucs cover. Bears 28, Bucs 23 Mongo Peanut : With Tristan Wirfs looking uncertain (he’ll play, but he had a DNP and a limited at practice this week with a toe injury) , I think the Bears’ new look line piles up the sacks on Baker. The Bears offense keeps humming and wins 37-14. Gary: Bears feed off an energized crowd in Jeffery Simmons’ first home game as a Bear; offense continues to do what it’s been doing, and that is being dominant. Bucs will get a score before halftime, as per tradition, to make it close at the half, but in the second half the Bears pull away. 34-20 Bears. GOOCH : I can’t speak for anyone else, but I’m offended by how many national talking heads are calling this a trap game and suggesting the Bucs defense is going to put Caleb in his place. This Bears team is for real, but so many seem to want to pick it apart, despite all the evidence to the contrary. Well, I’m predicting a signature game for Caleb: 350 yards passing, three touchdown passes, one touchdown run. Rome goes off for 125 yards and a score, Loveland and Burden add their own. Swift puts up over 100 yards on the ground and adds another score. Bears limit the Bucs’ rushing attack to its lowest output of the season, and Baker is on the run the whole game. Booker, Sweat, and Simmons all score sacks. Thineman and Malik add interceptions. Final score: 42-3. Take that, national talking heads. Now it’s your turn. Give us your picks and predictions for the game.

He was coming off an exciting first year with Ben Johnson, with a highlight reel a mile long. He was the Madden cover athlete, and as the offseason progressed, the buzz around Caleb and the Chicago Bears kept building. After they dropped a 50-burger in Week 1, the NFL shifted the hype train into high gear, and the Bears were the lead story on every NFL show. But then Week 2 and Brian Flores’ Minnesota Vikings defense came to town, and coupled with a steady downpour, Chicago’s offense never got on track. Then a fourth-quarter hamstring injury as the Bears were driving inside the Minnesota 1o yard line would sideline Williams for the next three games, seemingly ending his Most Valuable Player chances. The Bears went 2-1 in his absence, but since his return, Williams and the Bears haven’t trailed in any of their three games, and he’s completing 73.8% of his passes for 860 yards, 4 touchdowns, no turnovers, and a passer rating of 111.3. The last two weeks, he diced up the defenses of the last two Super Bowl teams, and his MVP odds have shot back up according to our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook . Right now, he’s at +800 to win MVP, trailing only the Buffalo Bills’ Josh Allen (+175), the Cincinnati Bengals’ Joe Burrow (+450), the San Fransocso 49ers’ Brock Purdy (+550 ), and the Jacksonville Jaguars’ Trevor Lawrence (+600). Earlier this week, we outlined how difficult it has been historically for a player to win the Most Valuable Player award after missing time during the season, but there is a precedent for him to do it, and another big game on Sunday Night Football could get him back in the conversation.

title: Chicago Bears Question of the Day: Which teams scare you?
summary: The Chicago Bears are hitting a fever pitch at the moment. A year and a half of Ben Johnson has produced a lot of quality football, but in consecutive weeks the Bears have confidently disposed of the two teams playing in the 2025 Super Bowl. The addition of Jeffery Simmons, improvement of Caleb Williams, and […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: George Kittle #85 of the San Francisco 49ers runs onto the field prior to the game against the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears are hitting a fever pitch at the moment. A year and a half of Ben Johnson has produced a lot of quality football, but in consecutive weeks the Bears have confidently disposed of the two teams playing in the 2025 Super Bowl. The addition of Jeffery Simmons, improvement of Caleb Williams, and a litany of talent on both sides of the ball have finally earned the Bears some serious respect across the league. As noted in Sam’s article earlier this week , the Bears are being ranked by various outlets anywhere from #7 to #2. They are being viewed as a legitimate title threat. Still, the NFL’s product is based in parity and chaos. There are still a ton of teams that can win the Super Bowl this season. However, that doesn’t mean that they are all scary to an Bears fanbase growing in confidence. Halloween has come and gone, but scary season is still upon us. Which leads me to my question. Which NFL teams still scare you? I think I can sort these teams into two different categories. Rationally scary and irrationally scary. Rationally Scary Teams This is a short list. These are the teams that I think are as good or better than the Bears right now and could beat them in a 1-on-1 matchup. San Francisco 49ers: The Niners are still the best team in football in my eyes. Shanahan remains the gold standard for head coaching, and he has morphed Brock Purdy into the perfect on-field extension of him. They are talented, fast, smart, and can beat you in a ton of ways. They are the best in the league. Buffalo Bills: The Bills are elite and will remain elite so long as they have the best QB in the league, Josh Allen, at the helm. Add in talents like Deone Walker and Gregory Rousseau making waves on defense, and the Bills are legit. Jacksonville Jaguars: I’m not overlooking you, Coach Cohen! The Jags have the 4th-best scoring offense and 2nd-best scoring defense in the league. They’re a fantastic team top to bottom that have beaten good teams like the Bengals, Patriots, and Ravens (still good even without Lamar). Irrationaly Scary Teams Detroit Lions: I think the Lions have a bottom 10 defense in the league. Outside of some talents like Aidan Hutchinson, Alim McNeil, and Brian Branch the defense is going to cost the Lions a lot of games. However, the Bears are 0-2 against the Lions since Ben Johnson has taken over, and that offense is still among the league’s best. While I think the Bears are the better team, the Lions still feel like the boogeyman. Green Bay Packers: Again, the Bears (with QB1) are the better team than the Packers. They are more complete in the trenches, and have a better QB/Coach pairing. Still, watching Jordan Love just heave bombs 40 yards downfield and assume that his WRs would beat our secondary terrifies me. A few broken coverages can change the entire shape of a season; just ask Chris Conte. Minnesota Vikings: Again…I think the Bears are far and away the more complete team. The Vikings are the inverse of the Lions. Super talented on defense and just wildly inconsistent on offense. Similarly, they have some talents on offense, namely Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, TJ Hockenson, and their two tackles, Christian Darrisaw and Brian O’Neil. But the well below average QB play from Kyler Murray has put their ceiling in doubt. As long as Brian Flores is coaching that defense, and KOC is eeking out enough offense, I will have my fears in playing the Vikings. Let’s be clear. The Bears look like they can win it all this season. Even the teams listed above are beatable if the Bears play the way we know they are capable. Stringing together wins against teams like these is another thing. Scary? Maybe a little. But we have Caleb Williams, Jeffery Simmons, and Ben Johnson, so I am sleeping well at night.

full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - SEPTEMBER 13: Tampa Bay Buccaneers linebacker Josiah Trotter (45) intercepts the ball for a touchdown during the game between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Two straight prime-time victories against the two Super Bowl representatives from a year ago lead us to one last prime-time matchup before Chicago’s BYE in Week 10. This time around, Chicago plays a feisty Buccaneers squad who just shut out a divisional rival last week without passing for a single yard. Clearly, the run game in Tampa is rolling, but don’t overlook the defense. Let’s get to the players for the Bucs that have my attention, starting with that defense. Defense: Josiah Trotter, #45 – LB The son of former Philadelphia Eagles great Jeremiah Trotter and brother of current Eagles LB Jeremiah Trotter Jr., Jeremiah is making a name for himself down in Tampa. After being drafted in the 2nd round of the 2026 NFL draft out of Missouri, Trotter wasted zero time doing just that as a pro. Against the Bengals in Week 1, the rookie notched 11 tackles with 1 sack and 1 stuff, along with 1 INT that he returned for a TD and another pass deflection. Despite having missed a game, he is currently leading all Tampa defenders in tackles by 25! At 6’2”, 237lbs, Josiah isn’t quite as stout as his dad, but he is a beast in his own right having done 27 reps of 225lb at the NFL combine and he could be the most athletically gifted of the whole crew. Caleb and Co. will have to know where #45 is so they don’t get blasted like Michael Penix Jr. did in the picture above. If Trotter can make his presence felt in the run and passing games, watch for Tampa to keep this one close. If Chicago’s offensive line can keep Caleb and the RBs clean, Tampa will need to pray that some more turnover treasure is looted to give them a chance. Offense: Tez Johnson, #15 – WR After the Jeffery Simmons trade, it would appear that Cornerback is Chicago’s last remaining weakness. Particularly against the deep ball. A few weeks ago I highlighted Falcons receiver Jahan Dotson in this piece for similar reasons and Dotson went on to post 87 yards on three catches. Three. That is a 29 yard average per catch. Tez Johnson is the deep threat for Tampa and averages 19.8 yards per catch himself. With Emeka Egbuka hobbled and Chris Godwin aging, Tez has stepped into a larger role in the offense and has played in all 8 games so far this season – though he has only been targeted 15 times. If Tampa once again is committed to run the football behind one of the most underrated offensive lines in the entire league, watch for the play-action to #15. If Tampa can move the chains on the backs of RBs Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell, I expect for veteran signal caller Baker Mayfield to take some shots downfield this week. If he can connect, Tampa’s offense has a chance to keep this one close and even secure the upset. If not, Chi-town will enter the BYE week with an elite 7-2 record. What about you? Which players will you be focused on when Tampa visits Soldier Field?!

title: Chicago Bears Week 9 Flashbacks: A Pair of Wins Against Rivals and a Defensive Masterclass
summary: Climb aboard the Gridiron Time Machine as we revisit three memorable Week 9 performances from Chicago Bears history! 1.) 1990, Bears @ Buccaneers: Testaverde throws it to everybody November 4, 1990 | Bears win 26-6 The Bears entered Week 9 of the 1990 season at 7-1 and firmly in control of the NFC Central. Tampa […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - NOVEMBER 04: Josh McCown #12 of the Chicago Bears looks for a receiver against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on November 4, 2013 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. The Bears defeated the Packers 27-20. (Photo by Jonathan Daniel/Getty Images) | Getty Images Climb aboard the Gridiron Time Machine as we revisit three memorable Week 9 performances from Chicago Bears history! 1.) 1990, Bears @ Buccaneers: Testaverde throws it to everybody November 4, 1990 | Bears win 26-6 The Bears entered Week 9 of the 1990 season at 7-1 and firmly in control of the NFC Central. Tampa Bay quarterback Vinny Testaverde probably wishes this particular Sunday had gone a little differently. After a scoreless opening quarter, Chicago finally broke through with a 12-yard touchdown run from Brad Muster. Neal Anderson added another score later in the quarter, while Kevin Butler’s 30-yard field goal sent the Bears into halftime with a 17-0 advantage. The offense did its part, but the defense completely took over the afternoon. Testaverde completed just 10-of-24 passes for 149 yards while throwing five interceptions and losing a fumble. Rookie safety Mark Carrier grabbed two of those interceptions within a two-minute span late in the second quarter, helping set up 10 Chicago points. Richard Dent, Shaun Gayle and Ron Rivera each added interceptions of their own. Jim Harbaugh quietly put together a solid afternoon on the other side, completing 14-of-23 passes for 213 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. His 19-yard scoring strike to Dennis Gentry helped extend the lead to 23-0 in the third quarter. Chicago piled up 378 yards of offense, including 187 on the ground, while controlling the football for more than 38 minutes. Tampa Bay did not finally reach the end zone until the fourth quarter, long after the game had been decided. The Bears walked out of Tampa with a 26-6 victory and an 8-1 record. Five interceptions, six total takeaways and another dominant performance from a defense loaded with familiar names. That sounds like a pretty good Sunday against Tampa Bay. 2.) 2013, Bears @ Packers: McCown gets it done at Lambeau November 4, 2013 | Bears win 27-20 Walking into Lambeau Field without your starting quarterback is generally not an ideal recipe for success. The Bears found a way anyway. With Jay Cutler sidelined, veteran backup Josh McCown made his first start since the end of the 2011 season against a Packers team sitting atop the NFC North. The complexion of the game changed almost immediately when Shea McClellin sacked Aaron Rodgers on Green Bay’s opening possession. Rodgers suffered a fractured left collarbone on the play and did not return, leaving Seneca Wallace to finish the game. That turned Monday Night Football into a battle of backup quarterbacks, and McCown was more than ready for it. He completed 22-of-41 passes for 272 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions. Brandon Marshall caught seven passes for 107 yards and a score, while Matt Forte rushed for 125 yards and another touchdown. Green Bay managed to turn a 17-10 halftime deficit into a 20-17 lead in the third quarter without Chicago’s offense touching the football, scoring a touchdown before recovering a surprise onside kick. McCown answered. He found Alshon Jeffery for a six-yard touchdown late in the third quarter to put Chicago back in front 24-20. From there, the Bears put together a clock-killing fourth-quarter drive that eventually ended with a Robbie Gould field goal and a 27-20 victory. McClellin finished with three sacks, matching his career total entering the night, while Chicago’s defensive ends combined for five sacks overall. The win snapped Green Bay’s six-game winning streak against the Bears and created a three-way tie atop the NFC North at 5-3. A backup quarterback, Lambeau Field and Monday Night Football. Not a bad time for one of the best performances of McCown’s Bears career. 3.) 2018, Bears @ Bills: The defense does the scoring November 4, 2018 | Bears win 41-9 The 2018 Bears were beginning to figure out just how dangerous their defense could be when they traveled to Buffalo in Week 9. The Bills got the full experience. Chicago’s offense managed just 190 total yards, Mitchell Trubisky threw for only 135 yards, and the Bears possessed the football for less than 26 minutes. Naturally, they scored 41 points. After a scoreless first quarter, Jordan Howard punched in a one-yard touchdown to give Chicago the lead. Then the defense decided to handle the scoring itself. Eddie Jackson stripped tight end Jason Croom, recovered the football and raced 65 yards for a touchdown. On Buffalo’s next possession, Kyle Fuller broke up a pass that Adrian Amos intercepted. Watch the full game below: One possession later, Fuller did it again. This time the deflection landed in the hands of Leonard Floyd, who returned the interception 19 yards for another touchdown. Chicago had forced turnovers on three straight Buffalo possessions, scored twice on defense and suddenly held a 21-0 lead. Howard added another touchdown before halftime to make it 28-0. The Bears defense finished with four takeaways, three interceptions and four sacks. Jackson and Floyd accounted for 14 points by themselves, while the Bills offense scored just nine. Chicago cruised to a 41-9 victory, improving to 5-3 and maintaining its lead in the NFC North. There may not be a stat that sums up the 2018 Bears better than this one: 41 points. Just 190 yards of offense. Sometimes the easiest way to fix an offense is to let the defense score instead. You can follow him on Twitter at @iamcogs .

It’s been that we’ve had a really strong group, but now he’s going to get more of an opportunity with Cashius being out, and he’s prepared himself for this moment,” Taylor told reporters this week. “I’m really excited to see him get that opportunity. He’s done everything the right way, and we’re going for him.” Cashius Howell is now on IR, and Cedric Johnson has been dealing with some injury issues, so there could be an opportunity for Stewart to see the field more. title: 3 overlooked Joe Burrow throws that helped Bengals defeat Titans

full_text: Seven players caught at least one pass from Joe Burrow in Sunday’s 43-36 overtime win for the Bengals over the Tennessee Titans. Samaje Perine and Jack Endries were both only targeted one time. Perine hauled in a nine-yard reception on the second play of overtime, and Endries hauled in a one-yard touchdown that gave the Bengals a 14-13 lead just before halftime. Coming into this season, there was a lot of conversation about the Bengals’ wide receiver depth behind Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Sunday, though, showed that depth is good heading into mid-November. Mike Gesicki has a touchdown in five straight games and six out of seven overall this season, and Dohnte Meyers has gone from a great training camp story to an integral part of the Bengals’ receiver room and special teams. Burrow has trust in a lot of receivers right now. Several players caught passes from Burrow in the fourth quarter and overtime Sunday in got-to-have-it situations. On a day where Burrow was historically good, three throws are getting overlooked, but they stand out for the growing trust he has in the Bengals deep group of pass catchers and also for how ridiculously accurate and prolific Joe Burrow is at throwing the football. 1. 10:07 4Q — 3rd&3 from the Bengals 34-yard line; Bengals trailing 28-23 Tensions were high in Paycor Stadium going into this play. The Bengals had just turned the ball over on their previous offensive possession, their fourth of the day, and Tennessee cashed in with a touchdown to take the lead. After a Chase Brown run on 2nd&4 gained just one yard, there were boo-birds coming down from the crowd. Then on 3rd&3, Burrow coolly found Mike Gesicki on the right side of the field for 18 yards and a badly needed first down. It was just Gesicki’s second catch of the game, but it would be the first of three receptions for him in the fourth quarter that accumulated 48 yards. Four plays after his third-down reception, Gesicki hauled in a 25-yard touchdown for his sixth score of the season and to give the Bengals a 29-28 lead. Gesicki is now tied for the most touchdowns he’s ever scored in a season, and that was back in 2020, when he caught six touchdowns in his third season with the Dolphins. This season, Gesicki has 17 receptions for 241 yards and six touchdowns, averaging 14.2 yards per reception. Every Mike Gesicki catch so far this season: Touchdown First down First down First down First down Six yards Touchdown Six yards Touchdown Seven yards First down Touchdown Touchdown #WhoDey — SleeperBengals (@SleeperBengals) October 31, 2026 Fourteen of Gesicki’s 17 receptions are for first downs or touchdowns. He set the tone for this season in Week 1, catching five passes for 78 yards and a touchdown, including three catches for 52 yards on the Bengals’ final first-half drive that led to a field goal. Now, Gesicki has a touchdown in five straight games, the longest streak for a tight end in Bengals’ franchise history. 2. 8:03 4Q — 3rd&10 from the Titans’ 48-yard line; Bengals trailing 28-23 Don’t let Gesicki’s emergence and Tee’s career-year overshadow the incredible connection Burrow and Chase have. They’ve been on the same page going all the way back to their first season at LSU in 2018. This play on Sunday shows the timing Burrow and Chase have on a difficult throw as Burrow is getting hit from a defensive stunt. First of all, this play was set up by a 10-yard reception by Chase Brown on 2nd&20, which the Bengals were in after Burrow was sacked on first down. So getting back into third-and-manageable is impressive in and of itself. Then on 3rd&10, the Titans ran a stunt with defensive end Jacob Martin looping around the left side of the Bengals’ offensive line. It gave him a free rush at Burrow, but he didn’t sack him. While he hit him hard, Burrow got rid of the ball just in time and layered a throw around multiple Titans’ defenders to Chase on the far side of the field. It gained 23 yards, and it set up Gesicki’s 25-yard touchdown on the next play. Burrow with the strike to Ja’Marr Chase with pressure bearing down on him pic.twitter.com/c6XAMTLjEW — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026 Chase had 11 receptions for 141 yards and a touchdown on Sunday, his first game with 100+ receiving yards and his first game with 10+ receptions. Even though Chase “only” has 492 receiving yards through seven games, he still has six touchdowns on the season, touchdowns in three straight games and five of his last six. And if Chase has 10 receptions on Sunday, he’ll tie Michael Thomas for the most games with 10+ receptions by a player in his first six seasons all-time with 18. For what it’s worth, Chase is still on pace for 148 targets, 104 receptions, 1,195 receiving yards, and 15 touchdowns this season. Even if that’s a “down” year, it’d still be a great year. But don’t worry; Chase had eight receptions for 130 yards and two touchdowns the last time the Bengals played the Falcons… and he didn’t even play in the second half of that game. 3. 3:01 4Q — 2nd&3 from the Bengals’ 26-yard line; Bengals trailing 36-29 This is my favorite play of the game. Tennessee just scored what could have been a back-breaking touchdown to take a 36-29 lead. I don’t know about you, but I didn’t know what the Bengals were going to do on their ensuing drive. It felt to me that it could go either way. But after this play, I was confident the Bengals were going to score and tie the game. Burrow was in trouble on this play, but he bounced out of the pocket and started rolling to his left. It wasn’t Chase or Higgins who caught the pass, though. It was Dohnte Meyers. The standout in training camp and the preseason, and who recently starred in the CFL, came across the field and made a diving 18-yard reception to move the chains and get the offense rolling. we not talking bout this play enough 🤦🏽‍♂️🔥🔥🔥 pic.twitter.com/JCMkluz14u — Khiicapalot (@Not_Gstreets) November 2, 2026 In that big of a spot, with Burrow escaping the pocket, it was Meyers making an incredible catch to gain the Bengals’ first down on the drive that ultimately tied the game late in the fourth quarter. Five plays later, Tee Higgins caught his second touchdown to tie the game at 36-36. Through seven games, Meyers has 16 receptions for 175 yards. Ten of those catches are for first downs, and he also has one rush for 10 yards that gained a first down against Tampa Bay. On special teams, Meyers has 11 punt returns for 103 yards and a 9.4 average, and he has 25 kick returns for 660 yards and a 26.4 average. Meyers had three receptions for 34 yards on Sunday, including two receptions in the fourth quarter for 27 yards. Joe Burrow is averaging 302.1 passing yards per game. Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins both lead the Bengals with 43 receptions. But other players are also stepping up, as evidenced by their performances on Sunday and through seven games this season. The Bengals not only have the best wide receiver duo in the NFL, but they also have one of the NFL’s overlooked but deepest groups of pass catchers. That may be what lifts Joe Burrow to the pole position of the MVP race and ultimately wins him his first MVP award.

full_text: The Cleveland Browns’ matchup against the New Orleans Saints is a significant game in the context of their season. The team is currently 5-3 and will either continue climbing toward the top of the AFC or continue to fall back into the pack . The team needs to show it can bounce back after a tough loss. The looming NFL trade deadline also could be impacted by the Week 9 outcome. With the Saints holding a 2-5 record, it is important for the Browns to take advantage of what should be a favorable matchup. They have lost four of their last five, giving the Browns a big opportunity, but New Orleans is also coming off of their bye week. Cleveland is currently sitting at third in the AFC North. The 6-2 Pittsburgh Steelers and the 5-2 Cincinnati Bengals sit above them. In order to establish themselves as contenders in the division this season, this will be a crucial win. While there is still plenty of football left to be played this season, losing this game would not be a good sign in an increasingly competitive AFC. With Shedeur Sanders starting at quarterback and some uncertainty surrounding how he will perform under center, this game could be considered a must-win. full_text: The Cleveland Browns are looking to bounce back after a tough road loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Browns’ game against the New Orleans Saints will look entirely different from the previous week, with Shedeur Sanders taking snaps under center . The offense will need to adjust to this change in preparation for the matchup. Beyond Sanders, there are several other key matchups that could help decide the outcome of this game. Chris Olave has 636 yards and two touchdowns this season, making him an important matchup for Denzel Ward . Ward has continued to prove why he is one of the best cornerbacks in the league this season, and he will face another test as he looks to limit Olave’s production. Jordyn Tyson’s return could add even more issues for the Browns defense. Cleveland’s offensive line struggled to protect Deshaun Watson last week. The offensive line will need to do a much better job of protecting Sanders if they want to give him a chance to run the offense effectively. The Browns struggled to stop the run against the Steelers and will want to improve on that part of their game against the Saints. New Orleans has struggled to stop the run this season, giving Cleveland a great opportunity to establish its dominance in that area. full_text: Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome to Week 9 of the NFL season! Today’s slate of games opens early as the Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons tangle in Madrid, Spain, at 9:30 a.m. The day closes with Tampa Bay taking on Chicago in a renewal of an old NFC Central clash on Sunday Night Football. And in between? Oh, nothing much, just what will be the most over-analyzed Cleveland Browns game of the season as they face the New Orleans Saints. If the Browns are serious about staying in the playoff race, there is no excuse to lose this game. The Saints are bad and have nothing to play for. Cleveland’s defense should be good enough to limit whatever New Orleans wants to do on offense. But all the attention will be on Cleveland’s offense, as Shedeur Sanders is making a spot start at quarterback while Deshaun Watson is still in the concussion protocol. There is already talk that if Sanders looks even remotely competent, head coach Todd Monken will bench Watson and turn Cleveland’s playoff hopes over to Sanders in an attempt to “see what the Browns have.” Never mind that Monken has never once even hinted that he would consider such lunacy. Watson has not been playing good, but in Cleveland’s wins he has been good enough. And there is no evidence to support the idea that the Browns would be in the playoff picture in November if Sanders had been the starter from Week 1. It’s the Browns and quarterbacks, so people tend to get irrational. But there isn’t a single team in the league that would bench its starter and go with a backup in this situation, so there is no reason for the Browns to be trendsetters. Sanders gets the start today, because that is what the backup quarterback does when the starter is out. Then, as soon as the starter is cleared to play, things go back to the way they were. The Browns need to win this game, and it doesn’t matter how they do it as long as they accomplish that goal. Banks was the Saints’ first-round pick last season and started all 17 games for the team as a rookie in 2025, but went on injured reserve after two games this season. Saturday afternoon, New Orleans officially activated both Tyson and Banks off injured reserve, along with four other moves: Waived RB Kendre Miller Waived TE Treyton Welch Elevated K Charlie Smyth Elevated RB Zamir White Given Tyson’s injury history in college, it will be interesting how much playing time he is allowed in Week 9 against the Browns, while Banks is likely to take back over at left tackle.

Ryan was signed to Cleveland’s active roster on Wednesday, practiced, and then was waived on Thursday . title: Shedeur Sanders’ have a shot at Deshaun Watson’s job? Talking to myself about it
summary: Channeling the long-time Cleveland sports media great Terry Pluto, I have found myself talking over whether Week 9 presents an opportunity for QB Shedeur Sanders to take QB Deshaun Watson’s job as the Cleveland Browns starting quarterback. Sanders is set to lead the Browns offense against the New Orleans Saints, but Watson has not been […]
full_text: Channeling the long-time Cleveland sports media great Terry Pluto, I have found myself talking over whether Week 9 presents an opportunity for QB Shedeur Sanders to take QB Deshaun Watson’s job as the Cleveland Browns starting quarterback. Sanders is set to lead the Browns offense against the New Orleans Saints , but Watson has not been ruled out for the game as he progresses through concussion protocol. First things first, can Sanders lead Cleveland to a victory in New Orleans ? That seems like the bare minimum for the second-year quarterback to have a shot at taking over as the team’s full-time starting quarterback. Then… well… welcome into my mind as I think about the future: Me 1: “Of course anything is possible in the NFL; it’s not like Watson was handed the job at the start of training camp, Todd Monken made the decision much later than expected.” Me 2: “Sure, but losing your job because of a one-week concussion is almost unheard of. Often, even missing weeks due to an injury isn’t enough for a quarterback to lose their starting position, unless they were already playing bad enough that a chance was likely anyway, like Kyler Murray this week with the Vikings.” Me 1: “But can we assume Monken cares about NFL norms in any way?” Me 2: “That’s fine, but what about the rest of the roster? Do they want players thinking that something outside of their control or strictly performance-based can upend their spot with the team? Does Monken have a strong enough feel for how the young locker room would be impacted by such a decision?” Me 1: “Great question, self, but what if the roster was already wondering when Sanders would take over already? We have no idea what is going on inside of the locker room.” Me 2: “Of course we don’t. We also know that the Saints defense isn’t very good, so there is a strong chance that Sanders could have a huge game in Week 9, but that Watson would have done the same or better had he been healthy.” Me 1: “Are you ignoring the more Brownsian outcome, that Sanders either struggles or gets dinged up and Watson, cleared Saturday (possibly) of concussion protocol, comes on in relief?” Me 2: “Not really; that outcome sort of closes the book on Sanders for this season, barring a major Watson injury. If that happens, it’s also possible that Dillon Gabriel is given the next shot at starting. So, that ”Browns is the Browns” option just ends this conversation (which psychologically might be best for me/us and the fanbase, but for the team????).“ Me 1: “Do you think readers are following along?” Me 2: “No clue, Jared is a strange creature.” Me 1: “So what is the benefit for the team if Monken turns to Sanders if the Browns win on Sunday and the quarterback has a great game?” Me 2: “From Jimmy Haslam, to Andrew Berry, and down to Monken, the entire Cleveland organization has made it clear that the only thing that matters is winning and producing on the field. If Sanders and Watson really were that close during the QB competition, and Sanders has a huge game in Week 9, making him the starter reinforces that principle.” Me 1: “Sure, but how in the world would one game versus a bad defense be enough to overcome Watson winning the competition to start the year, having multiple 4th-quarter comebacks, and two or three good games this season?” Me 2: “See, that is why we keep talking to ourselves about this. It isn’t that simple. Most believed that Watson would fail early in the season and Sanders would take over. Instead, through Week 7, the veteran looked like he was improving as the season went on.” Me 1: “So… are we ignoring Week 8 versus the Pittsburgh Steelers?” Me 2: “Exactly, which would be very different if his poor performance came in the Week 4 matchup in the AFC North. Instead, the last game Watson played was not good; he could miss Week 9 due to a concussion, and his job is being discussed by a somewhat sane person pretending to be two different people in this article.” Me 1: “Have we come to a conclusion?” Me 2: “Not really. Maybe our readers will be able to fill in some of their thoughts into the conversation. There may be two things both me’s will agree on, and probably most Browns fans: Browns HC Todd Monken will do whatever he wants and be unapologetic about his decisions All that matters is winning football games; if the team is winning, the QB will be supported, whoever it is Do you think there is any chance for Sanders to take over as the Browns starting QB after Week 9, or does Watson get it back no matter what when he’s cleared? title: Browns season heading into Week 9 versus the Saints: Ahead of schedule good enough?
summary: Going into the season, the expectations around the Cleveland Browns were reasonably low. New coaching staff, the youngest roster in the league, uncertainty at the quarterback position, and the team just traded one of the best defensive players of this generation to Inglewood. Fast forward to early November, the Browns are 5-3 and are still […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Going into the season, the expectations around the Cleveland Browns were reasonably low . New coaching staff, the youngest roster in the league, uncertainty at the quarterback position, and the team just traded one of the best defensive players of this generation to Inglewood . Fast forward to early November, the Browns are 5-3 and are still in the playoff hunt in the AFC . Considering how many believed that around this time Cleveland would be in “making mock drafts” territory ( Editor’s Note: I did create one recently , just one), 5-3 is better than what anyone thought. As people will question how good the Browns are, it’s a fair process to go through. However, in this day and age, context is rarely used correctly. Going into the season, Cleveland had one of the easier schedules. In the first 8 games of the season, the Browns were only favored in 1 of their 5 wins, their most recent one: Week 2 @ Buccaneers: 23-19 Week 3 vs Panthers: 21-18 Week 4 vs Steelers: 27-24 Week 6 vs Ravens: 13-10 Week 7 @ Titans: 27-24 Fans’ confidence in the team has waxed and waned throughout the season, but is higher than it was before the season. If you want to argue which win was most impressive, you can make an argument that it was the home win against the Steelers. The final score doesn’t indicate how the game actually went. If you rewatched that game, the Browns looked like the better team throughout, and it was a surprise to everyone watching that night. Winning in the NFL is hard, and it doesn’t matter how you do it. Is Cleveland a good football team? Bad football team? Neither. Average, so far, but young. Offensively, despite their issues, they are better than last year. Having better personnel helps, but the scheme is better than last season. Defensively, the unit isn’t as dominant as last season, but it’s still regarded as one of the better units in the NFL. Progress is being shown even if the results aren’t as impressive. If the team were winless or 1-7, we would argue that the Browns are making any progress at all. Instead, the team is 5-3 and exceeding expectations. It’s possible that the team goes over their win total sooner rather than later , and it’s possible that the team is playing meaningful games towards mid-November and early December. title: Cowboys vs Colts: Writer predictions for Week 9
summary: Dallas heads to Indianapolis needing an immediate response after somehow turning a 24-10 fourth-quarter lead into a 33-30 overtime defeat against Arizona. The Colts have problems of their own, losing four straight and entering Sunday at 2-6 after being demolished 42-7 by Jacksonville. This is a game where both teams desperately need something positive before […]
full_text: Photo by Richard Rodriguez/Getty Images | Getty Images Dallas heads to Indianapolis needing an immediate response after somehow turning a 24-10 fourth-quarter lead into a 33-30 overtime defeat against Arizona. The Colts have problems of their own, losing four straight and entering Sunday at 2-6 after being demolished 42-7 by Jacksonville. This is a game where both teams desperately need something positive before their seasons begin slipping away completely. When Indianapolis has the ball There should be no mystery about what Indianapolis needs to try first. Jonathan Taylor has rushed for 610 yards and eight touchdowns, while Dallas just allowed Tyler Allgeier to produce an incredible 147 rushing yards on only 11 carries. After watching Allgeier break runs of 63 and 52 yards, Indianapolis would be foolish not to test the Cowboys on the ground immediately. Taylor remains the best player on this Colts offense and can also contribute as a receiver, so Dallas has to tackle far better than it did during that disastrous second half against Arizona. The Cowboys’ goal should be to stop Taylor and put the game onto Daniel Jones. Jones has thrown only five touchdowns against nine interceptions, while Indianapolis owns the NFL’s worst turnover differential at minus-11. The Colts also traded All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson last week, leaving a less experienced offensive line in front of Jones. That gives Quinnen Williams and the Dallas pass rush a real opportunity after producing five sacks against Arizona. If Dallas can force Indianapolis into obvious passing situations, this is the type of matchup where the defense should finally create pressure without constantly needing to blitz. When Dallas has the ball Dallas should look at the Indianapolis defense and see an opportunity to rediscover its running game. The Colts are allowing 4.9 yards per carry, and their defensive front no longer includes DeForest Buckner after he was traded to San Francisco. Dallas ran the ball 39 times against Arizona but gained only 93 yards, so simply calling more runs is not enough. Brian Schottenheimer needs to find the concepts and directions that actually create space for Javonte Williams rather than repeatedly running into crowded areas. Establishing Williams would make life considerably easier for Dak Prescott. Dallas is still scoring 27 points per game, seventh in the NFL, while Prescott has 14 touchdowns against five interceptions. Indianapolis has only two interceptions all season and has just traded away its best interior pass rusher, so there should be opportunities if Dallas stays ahead of the chains. CeeDee Lamb remains the obvious focal point, although Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward give Indianapolis two experienced cornerbacks capable of making the outside matchups difficult. That makes Jake Ferguson’s ankle injury particularly important but he is questionable, while George Pickens was limited by a hamstring issue. The Cowboys cannot repeat what happened late against Arizona, when the offense had chances to put the game away but failed to finish drives. Indianapolis has conceded 23 touchdowns while scoring only 15 itself, and Jacksonville just put 42 points on this defense. Dallas should attack with balance, use play-action once Williams gets going and force a Colts defense without Buckner to defend the entire field. Now onto the predictions from your BTB writers… Tom Ryle (4-4) Maybe it’s just all getting to me, but I’m starting to worry this team is fundamentally and irreparably broken. It feels good like the collapse will continue. Colts 30 Cowboys 27 Brandon Loree (5-3) The Cowboys play the Indianapolis Colts every four years, so the last win at Lucas Oil Stadium feels like a lifetime ago. If you go back and watch that game, I think this Sunday could have a similar formula. The Colts can’t get going on offense and have multiple turnovers, but stick around until the very end. The Cowboys need to decide whether they’re a pass team or a run team and stick to that identity. Flipping back and forth is what’s causing this inconsistency. It’s close, but if this Cowboys team can’t beat this version of Indy, all hope is lost. I think the Cowboys win 33-24. Dyllan Rivers (4-4) The floundering Cowboys take on the fire sale Colts this week. As of this prediction, Jonathan Taylor is still wearing white and blue. If that holds true, he’ll be the target to eliminate on Sunday. After watching Tyler Allgeier make swiss cheese of the run defense, forgive me if I lack confidence in their ability to limit the Colts running back. Still, the pattern suggests Dallas will win this one. So with a big sigh and shrug, give me the Cowboys 31-24. Matt Holleran (4-4) I am very worried that this Cowboys team is broken upon repair. If this is the case, Sunday’s matchup against the Colts could end up being the lowest point of an already very low season. I have no confidence this team will show any fight or bounce back, even in a very winnable matchup. I hope I’m wrong, but I see this game being the culmination of the downward spiral as Dallas hits an even lower rock bottom. Give me Indy, 33-20. Mike Poland (3-5) Dallas should bounce back this weekend (well that’s what I’m hoping), and this matchup against Indianapolis gives them the perfect opportunity to do it. The Cowboys rank seventh-best in the NFL in points per game, while the Colts have the league’s worst defenses, allowing 28 points per game. The Colts have also struggled offensively, with Daniel Jones throwing nine interceptions to just five touchdowns. I’m expecting a positive outlook from Dallas and a much-needed victory to get their season moving in the right direction with the Cowboys winning 31-17. Or maybe I’m just being stupidly optimistic.

title: 2026 Week 9 rooting guide for Cowboys fans
summary: After their latest disaster against the Cardinals, the Dallas Cowboys feel more like a charity case than a contender. But as fitting as a classic Jim Mora “Playoffs?!” meme feels at this point, Dallas is still mathematically alive in both the NFC East and the Wild Card picture. If they do somehow turn things around […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images After their latest disaster against the Cardinals, the Dallas Cowboys feel more like a charity case than a contender. But as fitting as a classic Jim Mora “Playoffs?!” meme feels at this point, Dallas is still mathematically alive in both the NFC East and the Wild Card picture. If they do somehow turn things around this season, what else needs to go right to make a postseason appearance possible? Our Week 9 rooting guide is for those still hopped up on hopium. Because Dallas probably won’t have its own first-round pick in 2027, so rooting for draft position just isn’t as fun or interesting. We’ll flip over to that once it’s clearly the only path worth considering. Current 2026 NFC Playoff Standings 1. San Francisco 49ers 6-1 (4-1 vs NFC) 2. Minnesota Vikings 6-1 (4-1) 3. New York Giants 4-2-1 (2-2-1) 4. Carolina Panthers 3-4 (3-3) 5. Chicago Bears 6-2 (4-2) 6. Detroit Lions 5-2 (4-1) 7. Green Bay Packers 5-3 (4-3) _______________________________ 8. Seattle Seahawks 4-4 (1-3) 9. Los Angeles Rams 4-4 (2-2) 10. Tampa Bay Buccaneers 3-5 (3-2) 11. Atlanta Falcons 3-5 (3-3) 12. Arizona Cardinals 3-5 (2-4) 11. Dallas Cowboys 3-5 (2-4) Thanks mostly to head-to-head losses, the Cowboys are at the back of the pack of 3-5 teams. That’s quickly rectified if they can start piling up some wins, but it does make the current wild card picture look quite daunting. Thankfully, the climb in the NFC East isn’t so steep. The Giants’ lead isn’t that great, especially as their schedule is about to stiffen up. It only takes a couple of weeks for division contention to feel very possible, and the mood around here to change. Much of that hinges on this Sunday, of course. If the Cowboys can’t even put down the Colts, who’ve already started selling off assets in a clear surrender of this season, then it will be time for them to consider a similar course. With the trade deadline on Tuesday, it will be a major decision point for the front office as to how it wants to treat this current season and the future of the franchise. So, if Dallas can do its part in Indianapolis, what else can we root for from the Week 9 schedule? NFC East teams Eagles d. Giants Commanders d. Rams While we don’t want Philly or Washington suddenly becoming problems for us in the division, New York and Los Angeles are bigger fish to fry. Obviously, we want the G-Men to start taking losses and becoming easier to catch. We also don’t need the Rams suddenly finding themselves and remaining a barrier to a potential wild card spot. Plus, while Dallas probably won’t be drafting ahead of the Eagles or Commanders in the 2027 first round, we certainly wouldn’t mind seeing as far down the draft order as possible. NFC vs. NFC Cardinals d. Seahawks Bears d. Bucs Both of these matchups feature a team that Dallas has lost to this season, but we’re treating them differently. Arizona doesn’t seem like a threat to contend later this year, while Seattle could easily remain a problem in the wild card race. So the long game favors a Cardinals upset here. Tampa Bay, on the other hand, does have some staying power once Baker Mayfield returns. And with the Bears at 6-2, they’re probably not going to fall into Dallas’ range in the wild card. If anything, they’re still the arguable favorite to win the NFC North. NFC vs. AFC Bengals d. Falcons Dolphins d. Lions Broncos d. Panthers Patriots d. Packers Raiders d. 49ers Bills d. Vikings What a week for the AFC to do us some favors. These are all NFC teams currently ahead of Dallas in the standings, so a wave of AFC wins would be most welcome. Granted, even if Dallas gets its stuff together, we’re probably not touching the Niners, Vikings, or a few other frontrunners come January. But when there are zero pains from the AFC teams’ success, we’ll take any gains we can get. The Green Bay-New England game is of added interest because of 2027 draft implications. If Dallas ends up using the Packers’ first-round pick next April, which is highly likely, we certainly want it as high in the order as possible. We’ll gladly sacrifice the value of the seventh-round pick that the Patriots owe us, too. This heavy interconference slate rounds out the week in terms of Dallas’ rooting interests. The Steelers are on their bye, so we’ll check back in with them and the fourth-rounder they owe us next week. We’ll also see what happens with our own goofy team this Sunday, and how that shapes our rooting guides going forward.

title: Cowboys two keys to beating Colts and keeping playoffs hopes alive
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have very possibly not yet defined what “rock bottom” could look like on this 2026 season, but any version of sinking lower than they are right now would involve a second straight loss to a losing team this upcoming Sunday afternoon. The Cowboys are at the Colts, who have not won in […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have very possibly not yet defined what “rock bottom” could look like on this 2026 season, but any version of sinking lower than they are right now would involve a second straight loss to a losing team this upcoming Sunday afternoon. The Cowboys are at the Colts, who have not won in over a month. Many things about this matchup make it feel like it’s an opportunity sitting on a tee for Brian Schottenheimer’s team to get back in the win column, and just maybe make the run-in to Thanksgiving interesting. It’s time for our weekly look at how the Cowboys can keep alternating wins and losses by bouncing back in week nine, or how they could send this season farther down the drain with another bad loss. The Dallas Cowboys will beat the Indianapolis Colts if… …they don’t turn the ball over. Old friend Daniel Jones at QB for the Colts is the next opponent for the Cowboys to put pressure on, both with their defense (more on that later) and ideally the offense too, by possessing the ball and scoring touchdowns. Jones is 1-8 in his career against the Cowboys, from his past time with the Giants, with four touchdowns and six interceptions in these nine games. At all three levels of the Colts defense right now, they have problems. Up front, they just traded away DeForest Buckner. At linebacker, Akeem Davis-Gaither will be out on Sunday, with the team already starting rookie C.J. Allen at one of the linebacker positions. In the secondary, former Cowboy Charvarius Ward and Sauce Gardner have not played up to potential and are prone to being beat over the top, and committing costly penalties. Nickel defender Justin Walley is also ruled out against the Cowboys. The Colts also have the worst turnover differential in the league this season, and have been minus three in two of their last three games, both divisional losses. They do not have a game with a positive margin, and their only neutral game was still a 34-22 loss to Mike McCarthy’s Steelers. With CeeDee Lamb telling the media this week he views the Cowboys offense as beating themselves more than anything, there should be no excuse to not execute the basics against the Colts. Not every drive has to end in points, but not having the focus to stay on the field in short-yardage situations, not getting backed up by unforced penalties, and not finding ways to get the ball to Lamb and George Pickens in space to lean on the Colts all afternoon with this highly-paid offense would be an abject failure. The Colts defense has not taken the ball away once throughout their active four-game losing streak. If the Cowboys don’t turn the ball over and give the Colts extra life and short fields to keep the game close, the talent differential in this matchup should reveal itself and allow the Cowboys to get out of Indy with a win. The Dallas Cowboys will lose to the Indianapolis Colts if… …they don’t get to Daniel Jones. Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor might be the obvious choice as the potential game-wrecker against the Cowboys defense in this matchup, especially considering the Colts main objective may actually be getting Taylor’s trade value up with a big game against a Dallas defense torched by Tyler Allgeier last week. Allgeier was certainly a big factor in how the Cardinals made their comeback in Arlington last Sunday, but when the game clearly came down to Gardner Minshew needing to make a throw, he did so as well for the real backbreaking plays against Christian Parker’s defense. The Cowboys also sacked Jacoby Brissett four times last week, but only got to Minshew once with Quinnen Williams doing so in overtime. Daniel Jones was sacked three times last Sunday against the Jags. He was sacked four times against a Vikings defense that blitzed him at a relentless rate that literally broke records for how often a defense could blitz. The week before that, he was sacked six times against the Titans. The Steelers defense only got to Jones once, but still swung the game in their favor by forcing Jones to drop back 44 times compared to 24 total rushing attempts for the Colts in week five. In Jones’ last four starts against the Cowboys, all losses, he’s been sacked 16 times. Narrow this down to the last two games, and the Cowboys have won by a combined score of 60-15 with eight sacks, and also three interceptions. Whether it’s with the blitz or trusting Williams, Rashan Gary, and Donovan Ezeiruaku up front, Parker’s defense needs to make pressure the priority against this Colts offense. The coverage is not good enough to hold up for long enough periods of time to be trusted more than the Cowboys should trust their ability to get to Jones before he can even throw the ball, and the same goes for run defense. Sacks to get the Colts behind the chains is what this defense should be after more than anything. If the Cowboys continue to struggle finishing around the quarterback and allow Jones to extend plays, it will equally keep Jonathan Taylor as a threat in this game, and could make for a longer than anticipated afternoon trying to beat a team that’s already waved a white flag.
author: Sean Martin

title: Cowboys fans assign blame for last week’s debacle
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are as frustrating a team as there is in the NFL. Not good enough to win games they should and make their case as a contender, not bad enough that they extinguish all hope of a comeback playoff run. The state of the NFC East keeps them just on the edge of […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys are as frustrating a team as there is in the NFL. Not good enough to win games they should and make their case as a contender, not bad enough that they extinguish all hope of a comeback playoff run. The state of the NFC East keeps them just on the edge of a possible comeback this season, but the obvious warts and debacle’s like the Arizona Cardinals game keep showing up. Earlier this week we asked you who was most to blame for the loss to the Cardinals between two choices – the offense that couldn’t finish, and the defense that totally collapsed. What we got back was sort of an even split, but the majority of respondents (58%) blamed the Cowboys offense. The offense is the more talented group of the two, so there is an expectation that they will have to carry the team. They didn’t when it mattered and were unable to finish off the Cardinals when they had chances. The defense got 42% of the vote after the put together an outstanding effort until late in the third quarter, then totally fell apart after Gardner Minshew and Tyler Allgeier took over. Both units have a chance to respond this week as they are favored by 5.5 points against an Indianapolis Colts team that has given up on 2026. But it doesn’t look like they inspire much confidence as only 8% of fans think things are heading in the right direction. Bonus question: Will the Cowboys win on Sunday? Hit the comments and let us know your take.

title: College football draft targets for the Cowboys: Week 10
summary: We are taking a quick peek ahead to the upcoming offseason to scout out a few potential draft picks in the college ranks. Miami vs. Notre Dame Miami takes the highest-scoring offense in the country to South Bend, but the Hurricanes will be without explosive receiver Malachi Toney following ankle surgery. That increases the pressure […]
full_text: Photo by Aaron Baker/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We are taking a quick peek ahead to the upcoming offseason to scout out a few potential draft picks in the college ranks. Miami vs. Notre Dame Miami takes the highest-scoring offense in the country to South Bend, but the Hurricanes will be without explosive receiver Malachi Toney following ankle surgery. That increases the pressure on Miami’s defense and gives Notre Dame receiver Jordan Faison an even more important role. In the middle of that battle will be Hurricanes defensive tackle Ahmad Moten Sr, one of the better interior defenders expected to enter the 2027 draft. Miami: Ahmad Moten Sr, defensive tackle Moten is the prototypical sized defensive tackle who wins with his first step. He fires off the ball before offensive linemen can settle into their stance and forces the blocking scheme to react immediately. That burst allows him to create pressure from the three-technique position and disrupt running plays before the back reaches the line of scrimmage. He became a full-time starter in 2025 and produced 4.5 sacks and nine tackles for loss. His 12.9% pressure rate showed that the production was not based only on a handful of big plays. Moten repeatedly found his way into the backfield while playing beside first-round talents Rueben Bain Jr. and Akheem Mesidor. With those players now in the NFL, he has taken on a larger role as the experienced leader of Miami’s defensive front. Why The Cowboys Care Dallas needs to add young legs to their veteran rotation on the inside and prepare for the future adding another interior disruptor would help protect the investment Dallas has already made in Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark. Moten could begin as a rotational three-technique and a pass-rushing option on obvious throwing downs. His ability to penetrate would complement the power of Williams and Clark, while Christian Parker could move him across different alignments in the pressure package. He currently carries a second-round projection, placing him in the exact area of the draft Dallas must maximise. The Cowboys would need to improve his pad level and consistency against double teams, but his explosive first step is a trait that cannot easily be taught. Notre Dame: Jordan Faison, wide receiver Faison has developed from a walk-on and two-sport athlete into Notre Dame’s leading receiver. He enters this game with 38 catches for 497 yards and four touchdowns. He led the Irish in both receptions and receiving yards last season, recording 49 catches for 640 yards and four scores, while also contributing as a punt returner. His route running is the foundation of his game. Faison changes speed during the route to create separation without relying on elite size. He is especially effective from the slot. Why The Cowboys Care We say it every week when bringing g up wide receiver, this is all about George Pickens’ future. His long-term contract and possible trade value will remain major offseason questions, and although Ryan Flournoy has provided useful depth, the Cowboys still need another receiver who can separate quickly and keep the offense on schedule. Faison could compete for the third-receiver role, work from the slot and give Dak Prescott a reliable answer when the defense sends pressure. His punt-return experience adds another route onto the active roster. He is currently viewed as a third-round prospect, which makes him a realistic Dallas target rather than a player the Cowboys would need to chase at the top of the draft. BYU vs. Utah The Holy War will feature two top-10 teams for the first time. Utah enters at 8-0, while BYU is 7-1 and attempting to hand its rival a second consecutive defeat in the series. BYU running back L.J. Martin is doubtful, placing more responsibility on the Cougars’ defense. That makes linebacker Isaiah Glasker a key figure against a Utah offense protected by rising left tackle Zereoue Williams. BYU: Isaiah Glasker, linebacker Glasker looks like an NFL linebacker in every way. A former high school receiver and safety, he has the athletic background to turn and run in coverage and match tight ends without immediately creating a size disadvantage. That versatility has been central to his role at BYU. The Cougars can align him as an off-ball linebacker, walk him onto the edge or send him through an interior gap. He recorded 67 tackles, 8.5 tackles for loss and two interceptions in 2025 after a 2024 season in which he produced 70 tackles, 14.5 tackles for loss, 3.5 sacks and three interceptions. Those numbers reflect a defender capable of making plays in several areas rather than simply collecting tackles in the box. Why The Cowboys Care DeMarvion Overshown’s injury history remains a concern, while Dee Winters may or may not be part of a future roster. Glasker could give this defense a long, athletic defender who can play in space, blitz from different angles and contribute on special teams. His current draft stock has fallen into the late-round, which makes the rest of the season important. Dallas would not need to spend a premium selection to bet on his physical tools. A strong performance against unbeaten Utah could move him back into full Day 3 consideration. The Cowboys would be drafting the coverage range and versatility while trusting their coaches to improve his processing and ability to defeat blocks. Utah: Zereoue Williams, offensive tackle Williams is one of the fastest-rising offensive tackles in this draft class. The 6-foot-8, 305-pound senior spent most of his college career as a reserve before earning Utah’s starting left-tackle job this season. His size immediately creates problems for edge rushers. Williams has the length to make first contact and guide speed rushers beyond the quarterback. He moves well for a player of his height and has enough balance to stay connected rather than lunging at defenders. His basketball background appears in the way he mirrors movement and uses his reach without losing control of his base. Why The Cowboys Care Offensive tackle remains one of the most important positions for Dallas to evaluate. Williams has the physical tools to compete on the left side, or he can play on the right and potentially take over for Terence Steele. His draft range is wide because of the small sample, but most projections place him around the second or third round, but it really does range with him. That makes him especially relevant to a Cowboys team with limited draft capital. Dallas could allow him to develop behind its starters before asking him to take over a full-time job, or he could win it straight away.

title: Cowboys key matchup: Quinnen Williams vs the Colts interior OL
summary: We have been saying the same thing for almost a month now, but the Dallas Cowboys are heading into a must win game in week nine with the Indianapolis Colts. This is a unique matchup for the Cowboys due to the Colts practically punting on their season and moving on to 2027. In recent weeks, […]
full_text: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images We have been saying the same thing for almost a month now, but the Dallas Cowboys are heading into a must win game in week nine with the Indianapolis Colts. This is a unique matchup for the Cowboys due to the Colts practically punting on their season and moving on to 2027. In recent weeks, the Colts have traded away two of the best players on their roster in DeForest Buckner and Queneton Nelson, and their star running back Jonathan Taylor has dominated trade rumors over the last two weeks. With the Colts not focusing on winning football games right now, and the Cowboys desperately needing a win, one of the biggest matchups in this game should be a massive mismatch favoring the Cowboys. Early on in the season, it was fair to say Quinnen Williams was a bit disappointing. But over the last month or so, Williams has really turned it on and has been showing the dominant player we all expected to see in 2026. Since week five, Williams has recorded four sacks, three run stuffs, and 14 tackles. Williams has an intriguing matchup coming up in week nine against a depleted Colts offensive line. The interior of the Colts offensive line took a big blow when Quenton Nelson was traded to the Seattle Seahawks. Taking his place at left guard was rookie fourth-round pick Jalen Farmer, who struggled mightily in his first start of the season in week eight. Farmer allowed three pressures, one hurry, and two QB hits against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Colts center has struggled this season too. Tanor Bortolini has allowed multiple pressures in every game this season except for two and has drawn six flags in the last four games. The Colts right guard, Matt Goncalves, has had a solid season so far for the Colts, but he is also a player Williams should be able to take advantage of as well in the running and passing game. Goncalves has allowed multiple pressures in the last two weeks. This is an ideal matchup for Quinnen Williams who has been heating up here lately. Williams has registered 15 pressures and four sacks in the last three weeks, and this matchup should be one of the more favorable matchups he will see this season. Williams will need help from Kenny Clark and Otito Ogbonnia to keep some of the focus off of him, but this should be a matchup the Cowboys should win, and can be one of the biggest factors in them winning a much needed football game on Sunday.

title: Cowboys news: Jerry Jones tries to walk back ‘paying coaches’ comments
summary: Jerry Jones has been criticized for not being willing to write a huge check for a championship type of coach, but he doesn’t feel that it’s an issue whatsoever. full_text: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images | Getty Images Jerry Jones has been criticized for not being willing to write a huge check for a championship type of coach, but he doesn’t feel that it’s an issue whatsoever. The NFL trade deadline is rapidly approaching. If Dallas was to indulge, there’s one area that’s likely to get the most attention. The Cowboys have a talented offense that more than capable of being productive, but hiccups at the wrong times have caused some confusion. Cowboys’ Jerry Jones says paying coaches has never been an issue – Todd Archer, ESPN Jerry Jones got ridiculed after he mentioned that there was no connection between the highest-paid coaches to winning championships. Now, he’s saying spend top dollar for a coach hasn’t been a problem in Dallas. “The facts are I have been out there, and I have been trying to lure very successful coaches away from the teams they were on and knew full well that I was going to pay them for their success,” he said. “So that has been done. No one knows that, but I do. And so it is absolutely ridiculous. And I actually grin when somebody says, ‘Jerry’s not willing to pay the money for what it would take to get the right kind of coach out there.'” Cowboys to be without two starters, four more questionable vs. Colts – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram The Cowboys are facing a huge game against the Colts as they try to stay within striking distance in the NFC East. They’ll have to do so with multiple starters out. On Friday, the Cowboys hit the practice field for the last time before boarding the flight to Indianapolis on Saturday, and they did so without two starters. Wide receiver and kick returner KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and rookie outside linebacker Malachi Lawrence (ankle) did not practice this week and have been ruled out for Sunday’s game. Which position group could Cowboys add to at trade deadline? Stephen Jones answers – SportsDay Staff, Dallas Morning News The NFL deadline is next Tuesday, and the Cowboys have been talked about as a team that could make a move. The specific position that they could make a play for was revealed. Q: Which position or positions do you think could help the team the most right now? Jones: “Yeah I think it’s one everybody talks [about], obviously a pressure player could help us. After that, we took care of business earlier in the year with [Joey Porter Jr.]. It’s unfortunate he’s been missing some time. No excuses, because everybody has injuries, but no question it hurt us not having him or Caleb [Downs] in the game there in that quarter as well.” Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Here We Goooo: Cowboys defense must turn pressure into turnovers vs. Colts -Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Dallas is starting to pick up defensively when it comes to getting to the quarterback. However, taking the ball away needs to improve more also. Pressure is nice, but it doesn’t mean anything if the defense not affecting the quarterback. Bringing quarterbacks down more recently has helped, but Dallas needs to be able to throw Colts QB Daniel Jones off his game with their pressure on Sunday, as it’s affected him throughout the season. Quinnen Williams has been the best defender in terms of getting into the backfield and affecting the quarterback this season, so expect him to be let loose again in this game. Cowboys disconnect grows as CeeDee Lamb unloads on underachieving offense – Jerry Trotta, The Landry Hat The Cowboys look pedestrian offensively in situational football last week against the Cardinals. It’s caused tensions to boil over. Lamb is a veteran. He may wear his emotions on his sleeve on the field, but he’s not the type to publicly throw his head coach under the bus. What good would that accomplish? That leaves us to speculate about the root of his frustration. His comments could just as easily be interpreted as criticism of the players’ execution, but it’s hard to imagine Schottenheimer’s conservative play-calling and predictable offense aren’t at least part of the equation.

title: Mike Shanahan and Dan Reeves among Hall of Fame finalists
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Dan Reeves and Mike Shanahan are one step closer to the Pro Football Hall of Fame. But that’s likely where the journey will end, at least this year. The Hall of Fame announced on Thursday that both former Denver Broncos head coaches were among the five former head coaches advanced by […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY - SEPTEMBER 28: Mike Shanahan of the Denver Broncos motions on the field during the game against the Kansas City Chiefs on September 28, 2008 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri. The Chiefs defeated the Broncos 33-19. (Photo by: Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Dan Reeves and Mike Shanahan are one step closer to the Pro Football Hall of Fame. But that’s likely where the journey will end, at least this year. The Hall of Fame announced on Thursday that both former Denver Broncos head coaches were among the five former head coaches advanced by the Coach Subcommittee. Bill Belichick, Tom Coughlin, and Mike Holmgren were the other head coaches to advance. The next step in the process comes on Nov. 17, when the subcommittee will select one finalist to advance to the selection committee and present him for possible induction. After the presentation, the committee votes on whether to induct the former head coach. Since only one head coach will be included in the 2027 enshrinement class, Belichick is the best bet. The fact that it’s taken this long for Shanahan in particular to get inducted is absurd. Shanahan’s resume speaks for itself. He’s the winningest coach in Broncos history, and the Broncos are one of the most successful franchises in NFL history. Shanahan is one of seven coaches to win back-to-back Super Bowls (Chuck Knoll did it twice with the Pittsburgh Steelers). Of those seven, four are in the Hall of Fame, with two as locks when the time comes for Bill Belichick (maybe?) and Andy Reid. Including his time as a Broncos assistant, Shanahan is one of just six head coaches to earn at least 200 wins and multiple titles with a single franchise. From 1996-98, Shanahan oversaw one of the most successful periods in NFL history. Denver won 46 games and two Super Bowls. The Shanahan coaching tree and his offensive mind continue to influence the league in major ways. His time as offensive coordinator with the San Francisco 49ers helped Steve Young win his first Super Bowl as a starting quarterback. If that wasn’t enough, here are some more tidbits to prove how incredible Shanahan was, especially in Denver. The Broncos led the league in both 1,000-yard rushing seasons (11) and 1,000-yard receiving seasons (18) during Shanahan’s 14 years as Denver’s head coach. As for Reeves, what he did with the Broncos is just as impressive as what former Buffalo Bills head coach and Hall of Famer Marv Levy did, yet Reeves’ accomplishments are overlooked and underappreciated. Remember, Reeves was head coach for a team that went to three Super Bowls in four years. Reeves won more than 60 percent of his games during his 12 seasons in Denver. But as the Broncos website points out, Reeves’ candidacy extends beyond just the Mile High City. Reeves participated in nine Super Bowls as a player or coach, and he was a two-time AP Coach of the Year. Shanahan should already be in the Hall of Fame, so hopefully it happens sooner rather than later. For Reeves, it’ll take some time, but here’s hoping he eventually gets his rightful place. Unfortunately, it’ll be posthumously. Broncos Country takeover of Charlotte It’s becoming clear that Broncos fans travel. We saw it a few weeks ago in Arizona against the Cardinals. But what I’ve seen the last few days in the Queen City is freaking impressive. Everywhere you look, there are Denver fans. I won’t predict what Bank of America Stadium will look like today, but there will be a lot of orange. Broncos links
