title: Ultimate Fan: It’s a good time to open up the offense, keep the defensive pressure coming
summary: Ultimate Fans, life could not get better in Broncos Country right now. Denver is coming off an incredible victory over KC, currently holding court at the top of the AFC West, before a short trip out East to play the Panthers in spectacular weather just in front of a much-needed bye week. AND on top […]
full_text: Ultimate Fans, life could not get better in Broncos Country right now. Denver is coming off an incredible victory over KC, currently holding court at the top of the AFC West, before a short trip out East to play the Panthers in spectacular weather just in front of a much-needed bye week. AND on top of that, we have a fabulous UFG from another younger fan and newbie to the series who knocked it out the park just like his predecessors. While Ky Broncos Fan wasn’t even alive during the John Elway Era, his momma raised him right and turned him on to the GOAT and early Broncos’ Lombardis. Watching the Tebow-to-DT thriller turned him into a fan for life and his Broncos’ Mount Rushmore is testament to his appreciation for Denver’s incredible history. So that gives you a hint of the treat you are in for! I’m going to be at this game, and my track record is pretty good, so let’s assume it’s going to continue! Is @BoNix10 the King of the Fourth? 😏 DENvsCAR – Sunday 1pm ET on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/vONU45jlfO — NFL (@NFL) November 7, 2026 Week 9: Broncos at Panthers MHR – First, we have to talk about that KC game. What in the world happened? How excited/nervous were you for those final 15 seconds? Ky Broncos Fan: What happened was some Mile High Magic! I was standing in front of the TV pacing like a coach, and when that obvious false start was called (no matter what Brittany Mahomes thinks), I knew fate was on our side. The defining play of that sequence in my mind was JL Skinner stuffing Walker at the line of scrimmage after being forced into the game due to injuries; that kind of grit and determination is emblematic of the whole team. Last Sunday was my birthday, and the KC game was the perfect gift! MHR – We used to do a post-game story at Mile High Report asking, “what did you learn about the Broncos this week?” It’s a great question, so have YOU learned about the Broncos the last few weeks ? Ky Broncos Fan: I’ve learned that the Broncos are still elite in late game situations. Over and over against some of the best teams in the league (besides the drubbing of the Cardinals), they’ve proved they still know how to win with their backs against the wall. The Arizona win was a nice reminder that fans can expect the Broncos to beat the teams they’re supposed to beat instead of every week feeling like a coin flip. MHR – The Broncos sit atop the AFC West at 6-2, but they rank 30th in total offense. Bo Nix has looked much better in the wins over Arizona and Kansas City. Has he turned a corner, or is this offense still living on late comebacks? As I’ve asked many before, is a constant comeback-style game, Ky Broncos Fan: The offense is improving, but the late comebacks are still hiding deeper issues. Establishing the run early will go a long way for more offensive consistency, and luckily for Broncos fans, Jonah Coleman seems more than ready to take that on. As for Bo, we all fell in love with his fire and gunslinging mentality last season when it mattered most. As he continues to regain confidence following the ankle injury, Denver needs him to trust his eyes and take the shots when they’re there. His aversion to negative plays is one of his best traits, but Denver is at its best when he’s balancing that with more risk-taking. MHR – Carolina has been without starting corners Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, and Akayleb Evans is also on injured reserve. How aggressive should Sean Payton/Davis Webb be with telling Bo Nix to throw downfield on Sunday? Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle have been key to moving the chains but not super explosive…any chance we get a big day from either/both? Ky Broncos Fan: This game is the perfect opportunity to unleash the passing game. Utilize the running backs to get ahead of the chains, and then open up the playbook and test their secondary. Rushing success will open up some play-action opportunities, and overall, I think pushing the ball downfield in this game is necessary to gaining confidence and setting the passing game up for more success later in the season. Waddle’s speed and elusiveness are nightmares for opposing defenders, and I think he’s overdue for turning a quick slant up field for a long touchdown. I also think we’re overdue for a Sutton long bomb TD. When Bo puts it in the right place, Sutton turns 50/50 balls into 80/20 balls, and I want to see him get some chances to convert big plays and gain confidence this week. Huge news for the Broncos: Pat Bryant has been activated off IR and will play against the Panthers on Sunday. Bryant has quickly become one of Bo Nix’s favorite targets. He’s back. pic.twitter.com/VVHooNMGhg — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) November 7, 2026 MHR – On the other hand, the Panthers’ run defense is atrocious (ranked 30th)…is this a game for Jonah Coleman to really break out? After that 51-yard catch-and-run + 5-yard TD last week…maybe he’s poised for a big second half finish to the season? How would you suggest using him and JK Dobbins this week? Ky Broncos Fan: I’m starting Jonah Coleman in fantasy again this week. I spent a decent portion of my free agency budget to get him, and the Panthers’ defense is the perfect chance for him to show the front office we don’t need to spend draft capital on Jonathan Taylor. Dobbins can still be a very effective runner when healthy, and the priority has to be keeping Dobbins healthy for a playoff run. I’d make Coleman the true bellcow and spell him with Dobbins occasionally. MHR – Nix dismissed the “trap game” talk. But it’s a 1 p.m EST kickoff (11 a.m. Mile High time) right after an emotional comeback. Are you concerned the offense comes out flat? How does Nix avoid the offense getting in its own way? Ky Broncos Fan: I’m concerned. As someone who lives in eastern time, the Broncos always seem to start flat when they come to my time zone. Nix can avoid the offense getting in its own way with one word: handoff. Let Coleman and Dobbins do their jobs, and use their success to test the secondary in favorable situations. There are times when the playcalling should favor some early down aggressiveness to put Carolina on their heels too, but those playcalls have to be high-completion percentage opportunities that Payton trusts the offense to execute. MHR – The Broncos defense has been mostly outstanding, coming up big when it needs to, even if it gives up some plays. How should Vance Joseph plan for Bryce Young, who has been having a decent season getting the ball in the hands of reigning Offensive Rookie of the Year Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker, an equally dangerous receiver? Ky Broncos Fan: The secondary can trust the front line to get home. Young is easily overwhelmed by pressure and possibly dealing with an undisclosed knee injury that is altering his mobility. Joseph doesn’t need to blitz more; just changing up coverage looks enough to keep Young guessing will buy the front line the time it needs to make game-changing plays. McMillan and Coker are great young receivers, but Denver’s secondary has stymied greater, more experienced players already this season. Broncos are putting QBs UNDER PRESSURE pic.twitter.com/s2AKm6fiq3 — PFF (@PFF) November 5, 2026 MHR – How should Vance Joseph take advantage of a depleted offensive line standing in front of Bryce Young…does the QB even have a chance with Zach Allen, Nik Bonitto, Jonathan Cooper, Malcolm Roach coming at him? With 23 sacks as a team this season, how worried should Young be on Sunday? Ky Broncos Fan: Young should be terrified. Carolina’s path to success is a quick short passing game to get the ball out and mitigate the pass rush, but as long as the secondary and linebackers stay disciplined, they should face 3rd and longs routinely that let Allen, Bonitto and the others feast. Young has issues with the ball getting batted down at the line of scrimmage too, and the defense should be able to exploit him and create some chaos. They’ve made better quarterbacks than Young look worse…

His third elevation. — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) November 7, 2026 With Brandon Jones ruled out and Talanoa Hufanga questionable, the Broncos will elevate safety Taylor Rapp to provide depth and potentially start Sunday’s game vs. the Panthers. It remains to be seen if Hufanga will play or not, but either way, Rapp should see significant playing time once again this Sunday. Special teams star Devon Key has also seen some playing time at safety and could get the start opposite Rapp if both Jones and Hufanga are sidelined. I also wouldn’t be surprised if reserve safety JL Skinner gets some added playing time after his big-time hit on Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker at the goal line during last Sunday’s thrilling victory over the Kansas City Chiefs. Either way, the Broncos will need to rely on their safety depth for at least one more week. As for Cody Schrader, he will serve as the Broncos RB3 for the second straight week. Look for another heavy dose of JK Dobbins and rookie Jonah Coleman at running back, with Schrader serving as depth and playing special teams. With both RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie on the injured reserve, Schrader is getting the call at running back. The Broncos have been calling around about running backs prior to the upcoming trade deadline, so this might be the final week we see Schrader elevated, but time will tell. The team also announced that they have activated wide receiver Pat Bryant from the injured reserve while also placing defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike on the injured reserve . They also signed reserve cornerback/returner Sam Fresch Jr. from the practice squad to the active roster. So, it was an active Saturday for the Broncos when it came to roster transactions.

title: 5 questions with Cat Scratch Reader
summary: This week I had a chance to exchange questions with Walker Clement of SBNation’s Cat Scratch Reader about our upcoming matchup. full_text: This week I had a chance to exchange questions with Walker Clement of SBNation’s Cat Scratch Reader about our upcoming matchup. This is no SB50 rematch but there are a lot of good storylines to tackle (see what I did there?) And so we did! The irony is that Walker now lives in Colorado and I’m in the Carolinas…what are the odds? He had fantastic answers to my questions so enjoy this extra insight into the 2026 Panthers (and thank him in the comments while convincing him to become at least a secondary Broncos fan!) Heading to the Queen City. 🏙️ pic.twitter.com/aOs1yE2JXO — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) November 6, 2026 MHR – Carolina has swung wildly this year with wins of 34-3 at Atlanta and 25-14 at Philadelphia, then a 43-13 loss to Tampa Bay. Which version of the Panthers can Denver expect Sunday? WC: Smart money is on the “vs Tampa Bay” version of the Panthers for a number of reasons, but the only real important one is the health of their current roster. The Carolina Panthers are currently without their RT1, LT1, LG1, CB1, CB2, CB3, CB4, DT3, OLB 1, OLB 2, ILB 2, RB2, RB3, and WR3. Two of those guys missed last week’s game against the Packers, the rest have been missing since sometime between September and January. The depth chart is rough right now. Of the guys who are playing, their current starting left tackle (Rasheed Walker), center (Luke Fortner), and right guard (Robert Hunt) are each leading the league in individual pressures allowed from their respective positions. It is no accident that Bryce Young was sacked 11 times in five days last week. Fixing the protection is a priority for them right now. The progress they have made since last Thursday could well decide the game this week. MHR – Bryce Young has completed 59-percent of his passes, thrown for 1,921 yards, 13 touchdowns, and just 5 interceptions on the season. He is doing well on first down and is moving the chains early and often, spreading the ball around. As Denver can be known for giving up big plays, which receiving threats should scare Denver’s DBs the most? WC: Reigning Offensive Rookie of the Year Tetairoa McMillan is your obvious first threat. Opposite him at wide receiver is Jalen Coker, an equally dangerous receiver whose precise routes and excellent hands make him a threat all over the field. After that is tight end Darren Waller. Each of them get a first down on over 50% of their receptions and nearly 30% of their targets. They have accounted for eight of Young’s 13 touchdowns and have season long receptions of 32 (McMIllan), 51 (Coker), and 50 (Waller) yards. You’ll hear their names often if Young can get more than two seconds between snap and pressure on the average down. Such was not the case in the team’s last two consecutive losses. MHR – The Panthers’ third-down efficiency has been less than optimal, mostly due to O-line play. In just seven games, Young has been sacked almost as many times as he was in 2025. How will the Panthers try to remedy that against a stout Broncos’ defensive line that puts a lot of pressure on the QB, both up the middle and from the edge? Which defender worries you the most? WC: You could line up anyone of your readers opposite the Panthers offensive line and I’d be worried for Young right now. 11 sacks in two games in five days has been completely demoralizing. Injuries have played a huge part, dating back to a torn bicep in 2025 for guard Robert Hunt that he has clearly not recovered fully from. That is an excuse that can explain recent games, but it doesn’t threaten to win any future ones. The one bright spot is that the Panthers longtime utility lineman, Brady Christensen, is expected to return this week from injured reserve. He can plug in at any of the five spots on the offensive line and would be expected to be an instant upgrade at all of them. Of course, we also got RT1 Taylor Moton back from injured reserve in the Buccaneers game to much the same expectation, only for Walker to get tackled into his leg and break his femur–potentially ending his career as a Carolina Panther. Bear with us if we are not brimming with optimism at the moment. Can the Panthers make the right adjustments to their offensive line in preparation to face a strong Broncos defense? @Jfowlerespn and @JudyBattista weigh in on how Carolina can help protect Bryce Young and what to expect from Denver 😤 pic.twitter.com/oPrGXR78Dj — NFL Network (@nflnetwork) November 7, 2026 MHR – Speaking of QB pressure, Devin Lloyd has been your X-factor on defense, especially for a unit suffering so many injuries. The fifth-year pro already has 69 tackles, 2 interceptions, and 2 sacks on the season. How will he and the defense rattle Bo Nix and our fragile offense the most? WC: Lloyd has been excellent in everything asked of him. He can blitz, he can cover, he can stuff the run. Former defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero’s scheme was often described as overly complex and Lloyd stepped in and mastered it this offseason as a marquee free agent signing. This is the Panthers’ first week without Evero and the theme has apparently been to simplify the defense so that players can play faster. Will that accelerate Lloyd or nerf the benefit his previous acumen provided? I’m anxious to find out but, unfortunately, I do not have an educated guess as to which will prove true. MHR – The Broncos’ running game has been really hit or miss, with a few splash plays mixed in with a lot of short gains. But the Panthers’ run defense has surrendered over 140 rushing yards per game. Which team’s weak spot wins out on Sunday – our run game or your run defense? WC: 140 rushing yards per game looks bad, but it is misleading. The Panthers held Bijan Robinson to 72 yards and Jahmyr Gibbs to 46 yards. They just also gave up 291 yards to the Chicago Bears and 258 yards to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. When it rains, it pours in the Carolinas. Not all of those totals, good or bad, can be explained away by injuries. There are a lot of question marks to be addressed by interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash and I struggle to believe that he is going to answer all of them perfectly. I do think, however, that he is going to start by focusing on the obvious problems and selling out to stop the run. This game will be a sloppy shoot out, if the Panthers have their way, and Brady Christensen will help the team shore up Young’s protection long enough to give a desperate team a chance. Who wins that? I change my mind every hour, but I do believe the Panthers, on their best day, are capable of beating the Broncos on theirs. My worry is that the Panthers best days may be behind them given the current state of their roster. Bonus Question: What did you think of the firing of Ejiro Evero? Were the problems on defense his fault? Do you agree it was the right move? WC: I think the Evero firing was both the right call and likely to have little effect on the season. On the one hand, he was responsible for most of the worst rushing performances surrendered in the history of our young franchise. On the other hand, they’re not installing a new scheme in Week 9 and they’re not set to return any of the nine defensive players set to miss the game against the Broncos who have started multiple games for them this season. When you lean on a preseason caliber roster you get preseason caliber results.The remaining eight weeks in the 2026 season could be fascinating for Panthers fans. We could watch head coach Dave Canales do anything from winning coach of the year to getting fired depending on what he does with what is left of his roster. It’s such an exciting time to be us again.

title: Broncos activate WR Pat Bryant from the IR and place DL Eyioma Uwazurike on the IR
summary: The Denver Broncos announced today that they have activated wide receiver Pat Bryant from the injured reserve to the active roster and also placed defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike on the injured reserve with a shoulder injury. The team also announced it signed reserve cornerback Sam Fresch Jr. from the practice squad to the active roster. […]

(Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos announced today that they have activated wide receiver Pat Bryant from the injured reserve to the active roster and also placed defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike on the injured reserve with a shoulder injury. The team also announced it signed reserve cornerback Sam Fresch Jr. from the practice squad to the active roster. We've made a series of roster moves ahead of #DENvsCAR . 📰 » https://t.co/HywPGP19s1 pic.twitter.com/M4sGSNtS7i — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) November 7, 2026 Bryant returning to the offense will give the Broncos’ passing offense a big boost moving forward. The second-year wide receiver was the star of training camp and was establishing himself as a key member of the offense prior to his injury. Now, he will join Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton as the Broncos’ starting wide receivers moving forward. As for Uwazurike, this is a bit of a loss for the Broncos’ defense. He has been a key rotational piece who has played significant snaps thus far this season. With him sidelined, I wonder if we will see rookie defensive lineman Tyler Onyedim make his debut for the team tomorrow vs. the Panthers? He was the Broncos’ first pick in April’s 2026 NFL Draft, but has been a weekly inactive thus far this season. With Uwazurike now sidelined for at least four games, Onyedim may get a shot to prove himself. The team also has veteran Jordan Jackson on the roster, whom they could use as well. We could also see second-year defensive lineman Sai’vion Jones get some added snaps as well. Former UFL player Sam Fresch Jr. has spent the season on the Broncos’ practice squad and has been elevated a handful of times while Pat Surtain II and Riley Moss were sidelined. Now, with reserve cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine ruled out for Sunday’s game, the team decided to add Fresch Jr. to the 53-man roster. He’ll serve as the Broncos 5th corner while also giving the team another player with return ability in the kicking game. So, the Broncos received some good news of the offensive side of the ball with the return of Pat Bryant, but also received some bad news with the loss of Uwazurike.

title: Broncos checked in on TE Trey McBride, but the Cardinals refused to trade him
summary: Well, that would have been fun. According to ESPN’s NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport, the Denver Broncos have been checking in around the league for tight end help, and even checked in on Cardinals star tight end Trey McBride. The Cardinals made it clear to the Broncos that they have zero intention of […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 25: Trey McBride #85 of the Arizona Cardinals reacts to Brandon Jones #22 of the Denver Broncos during the third quarter of the game at State Farm Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, that would have been fun. According to ESPN’s NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport, the Denver Broncos have been checking in around the league for tight end help, and even checked in on Cardinals star tight end Trey McBride . The Cardinals made it clear to the Broncos that they have zero intention of trading the face of their franchise, and the Broncos have turned their attention elsewhere. The Denver Broncos have checked in around the league on tight ends, going so far as to ambitiously — and some would say outrageously — check on Cardinals star Trey McBride, who is from Fort Morgan, Colorado, and played at Colorado State. The Cardinals made it very clear they… https://t.co/fz5M8XuzSF pic.twitter.com/7M5uZb4uKo — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 7, 2026 Schefter and Rapoport added that the Broncos have checked in around the league for tight ends, including Cardinals star tight end Trey McBride, who is from Fort Morgan, Colorado, and played at Colorado State. Unfortunately for the Broncos, the Cardinals made it known they have no intention of trading away the face of their franchise. The Denver Broncos have checked in around the league on tight ends, going so far as to ambitiously — and some would say outrageously — check on Arizona Cardinals star Trey McBride, who is from Fort Morgan, Colorado, and played at Colorado State. The Cardinals made it very clear they have zero intention of trading McBride, and Denver turned its attention elsewhere. This has been a move many Broncos fans have been wanting them to make, and despite being in the basement of the NFC West once again, the Cardinals do not seem keen on the idea of trading away their star tight end. Still, it appears the Broncos are big fish hunting ahead of the trade deadline and would like to add a playmaker to their offense prior to the deadline this coming Tuesday. As we know, they have been connected to Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor, but their level of interest seems to have lowered recently, with the New York Giants being the main interested team there. McBride would have been a huge and unexpected splash, so now we have to ask: what do GM George Paton and HC Sean Payton have cooking? It’s clear they want to add a weapon to their offense and are willing to make a big splash if they can. The Colts are seeking a pricey package for Jonathan Taylor, and Trey McBride would have cost at least multiple 1st-round picks. So, what other running backs, tight ends, or, hell, even wide receivers are they looking to acquire? One tight end to potentially keep an eye on is Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert. The pass-catching tight end market is not very good, but Goedert does seem like a player who could be available. With that said, he was a free agent this past offseason, and the Broncos did not show much interest at all; he ended up re-signing with the Eagles on a one-year deal. A move at running back or tight end would make sense for the Broncos. The emergence of Jonah Coleman helps the Broncos’ backfield, but they still need more. Veteran JK Dobbins has really taken a step back this season and has struggled badly. Also, second-year back RJ Harvey and reserve/third down specialist Tyler Badie are currently on the IR. So, you could make a case that they need to add some depth to their running back room, even with Jonah Coleman playing well. As for tight end, they have veteran tight end Evan Engram who simply isn’t really used. He gets snaps but isn’t really targeted and feels like an afterthought in the offense. Adam Trautman is your blocking specialist and reserve/blocking tight end Nate Adkins leads the team in touchdown receptions (3), but only has 6 total receptions on the year. The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10th at 2 p.m. MT, and our Denver Broncos appear to be a team that will be very active ahead of the Deadline.

title: Broncos vs. Panthers: 3 Players to Watch
summary: The Denver Broncos take on the Carolina Panthers on Sunday for their Week 9 matchup. If they can achieve a victory, they will be 7-2 before their bye week. In order to win and keep their spot atop the AFC West, the Broncos need these three players to play at a high level. Nik Bonitto […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - OCTOBER 15: Linebacker Nik Bonitto (15) and defensive end Zach Allen (99) of the Denver Broncos celebrate a shared sack of quarterback Sam Darnold (14) of the Seattle Seahawks during second half of a 17-14 overtime Broncos win on Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026, at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colo. (Photo by Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Denver Broncos take on the Carolina Panthers on Sunday for their Week 9 matchup. If they can achieve a victory, they will be 7-2 before their bye week. In order to win and keep their spot atop the AFC West, the Broncos need these three players to play at a high level. Nik Bonitto — Edge Rusher Finding a way to rattle Bryce Young is one of my big keys to the game. So far this season, the Panthers’ offensive line has struggled to protect him. He has already been sacked 23 times—almost as many as last season—and he is getting pressured on over 40-percent of his drop backs. Edge rusher Nik Bonitto is one of the players who needs to show up big on Sunday. After posting back-to-back seasons with double-digit sacks, the fifth-year pro is having a slower start to the 2026 season. Compared to 2025, Bonitto is experiencing a dropoff across the board relative to sacks, hurries, quarterback hits, and pressures. Left tackle Rasheed Walker has been a liability for Carolina thus far. More often than not, Bonitto will be tasked with going up against him on Sunday. If he can have a big day and win his one-on-one opportunities versus Walker, that should definitely help slow down the Panthers’ offense which ranks Top 10 in many respects. Malcolm Roach — Defensive Lineman The Broncos boast a deep rotation along their defensive line. That has kept their line fresh and taken a big burden off of All-Pro Zach Allen’s shoulders. However, their depth will be tested on Sunday with Eyioma Uwazurike being ruled out. That means someone else is going to have to step up and be a dominant force in the trenches. I’ve got a feeling Malcolm Roach will be that player. In eight games , the seventh-year pro has 24 tackles, 3.5 sacks, 5 tackles for loss, and 12 quarterback hits. Roach has always been a quality run defender, but his ascent as a pass rusher has been a great development for the team. Being able to put pressure on Young (as mentioned above) will be critical. Though limiting running back Chuba Hubbard’s impact will be important too. Hubbard is on pace for a career season. He sports a great 4.6 yard per carry average and has 540 rushing yards with 5 rushing touchdowns on the season. Denver will need Roach to be quick off the snap and make some plays in Carolina’s backfield to slow him down. J.K. Dobbins — Running Back In a few articles this week, I’ve advocated for rookie running back Jonah Coleman to be the focal point of the Broncos’ rushing attack against the Panthers. Carolina’s defense has been awful stopping opposing rushing attacks in the first half of the season. That’s why it makes sense to pound the rock on the road. Even if I’m bullish on Coleman deserving a majority of the reps, that doesn’t negate this being a big game for Dobbins. It absolutely is. He has struggled this season and is sporting a career low 3.3 yard per carry average. If he can’t find a way to improve going up against one of the NFL’s worst run defenses, when can we reasonably assume he will get on track? Denver needs a strong running game to be legitimate Super Bowl contenders. Earlier in the week, Head Coach Sean Payton mentioned he was pleased with what he had seen from Dobbins thus far. However, rumors have swirled for weeks that the Broncos may be in the market to add to their stable of backs prior to the November 10th. How Denver’s run game looks, in particular Dobbins, against the Panthers might have an impact on whether or not they are buyers at the position before the deadline.

title: Lions elevate 2 practice squad players for Dolphins game
summary: The Detroit Lions ruled out five starters on Friday and made a series of roster moves on Saturday to adapt their roster. In addition to moving Jack Campbell to injured reserve and signing Nick Whiteside to the active roster, the Lions also elevated two practice squad members to the game-day roster: EDGE Anthony Lucas and […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive end Anthony Lucas (61) walks off the field after practice during OTAs at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, June 11, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions ruled out five starters on Friday and made a series of roster moves on Saturday to adapt their roster. In addition to moving Jack Campbell to injured reserve and signing Nick Whiteside to the active roster , the Lions also elevated two practice squad members to the game-day roster: EDGE Anthony Lucas and RB Jabari Small. All three roster additions are direct injury replacements. Whiteside will give the Lions depth at corner while D.J. Reed recovers from a hip injury; Lucas will help soften the absence of DJ Wonnum, who is in the NFL’s concussion protocol, and Small gives the Lions depth at running back with both Sione Vaki (ankle) and Jacob Saylors (neck) being listed as questionable. On Friday, when coach Dan Campbell was asked about potential replacements for Wonnum in this game, noting that Derrick Moore, Ahmed Hassanein, and Eric O’Neill were already on the roster, Campbell also made sure to mention Lucas as a player firmly in the mix: “Well, I think another guy is Anthony Lucas is somebody we’ve been repping a little bit here for whoever that defensive line, that extra spot there for Wonnum. So I mentioned this before, Brad (Holmes) has done a good job with the depth that we’ve got. And so we’ll be able to weather the storm, and those guys are going to get an opportunity, and adversity hits with injuries.” Small’s addition gives the Lions backfield depth and raises questions about either Vaki or Saylors’ status. Vaki was a late addition to Friday’s injury report, and mid-week additions typically signal bad news for players’ chances of playing Sunday, though listing him as questionable gives him a chance to play. Saylors has been dealing with a neck injury for the last two weeks and couldn’t finish the game against the Vikings in Week 8, but with him also getting a questionable designation keeps him in play to contribute against the Dolphins. It’s worth noting that neither Vaki nor Saylors have been downgraded to OUT so far, which is typically an indication that they’ve traveled with the team to Miami. We are most likely headed to a game-time decision on both running backs.

Campbell was transferred to a nearby hospital and offered the following update on his condition Wednesday via an official statement . “I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body,” Campbell said. “I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.” Since then, Lions coach Dan Campbell has said Campbell continues to improve. At this point, it’s unclear what Campbell’s injury means for the rest of the season or his career, but his placement on injured reserve guarantees he must miss the next four games. The first game he’d be eligible to return is Week 13 vs. the Atlanta Falcons on December 6. In Campbell’s place, the Lions are expected to start Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez, and Trevor Nowaske at linebacker vs. the Miami Dolphins. Detroit will also have Joe Bachie, K.J. Britt, and Amen Ogbongbemiga available among their reserves. To take Campbell’s spot on the 53-man roster, the Lions signed cornerback Nick Whiteside from the practice squad. Whiteside made a strong impression during training camp, even earning some reps with the first-team defense during early practices. Now, with top cornerback D.J. Reed out this week with a hip injury , Whiteside has an opportunity to be part of the Lions’ cornerback rotation, which will likely include Roger McCreary, Ennis Rakestraw, Rock Ya-Sin, and Khalil Dorsey. In addition to those two moves, the Lions also elevated defensive end Anthony Lucas and running back Jabari Small from the practice squad. We have more information on those moves in a separate news article .

title: Detroit Lions vs. Miami Dolphins preview: 3 key stats
summary: As the Detroit Lions approach the midway point of their season, it’s been a weird and challenging week to care as deeply about football or celebrate the Vikings win. Most Lions fans, media members, and those within the franchise have been clinging to the progress reports and updates on team captain Jack Campbell, who remains […]
full_text: Oct 30, 2022; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez (44) sacks Miami Dolphins quarterback Tua Tagovailoa (1) during the first quarter at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-USA TODAY Sports As the Detroit Lions approach the midway point of their season, it’s been a weird and challenging week to care as deeply about football or celebrate the Vikings win. Most Lions fans, media members, and those within the franchise have been clinging to the progress reports and updates on team captain Jack Campbell, who remains hospitalized with a neck injury suffered in Week 8. The player who was awarded last season’s media Good Guy of the Year award had just welcomed his first child with his wife, Megan, a son named Cooper, in July. And here was the new dad laid up in a hospital bed, still without full movement of his upper body. It was tough to harness that same giddy, football-frenzied feeling for the upcoming game until fans were reminded why this is such a likable team, as Campbell, the player who perfectly embodies this city and this franchise, remained at the forefront of players’ and coaches’ minds throughout the week. They spoke about how they’re playing for 46. Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard said, “Let’s play and prepare like 46. The way you honor him is to wipe those tears from your eyes and make sure you prepare and play like him.” That’ll get you on board to root for the boys quickly. And suddenly, just like the countless games down the stretch in 2024 that were continually billed as “trap games,” you feel reassured that the Lions won’t let the 1-6 Miami Dolphins sneak up on them. They’ll be looking to fight and take care of business against the team that once called Dan Campbell its head coach and had Sheppard as one of its defensive anchors. The Dolphins are going through a rebuilding period, but head coach Jeff Hafley and general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan both come from Green Bay and are all too familiar with the Lions. They have their talent-deficient unit losing but competing, with a number of young players who could become foundational pieces, much like the early Dan Campbell Lions. This week’s preview will examine three key stats and matchups Detroit needs to control to keep its three-game winning streak alive, avoid giving the Dolphins life, and make 46 proud. Note: Unless otherwise indicated, all statistics are sourced from NFL Pro, FTN Fantasy, Pro Football Reference, SumerSports, or Pro Football Focus. Good Golly, Miss Ollie This week’s preview will focus entirely on how the Lions’ defense will coalesce to cover for the absence of Jack Campbell, and how the Dolphins’ offense will understandably try to attack a defense without its green dot. Linebackers Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez, and Trevor Nowaske are expected to handle the primary linebacker snaps, all with expanded roles and added responsibilities. That becomes particularly important given Miami’s recent success pounding the rock with Ollie Gordon since the De’Von Achane injury. The Dolphins comparisons to the early Dan Campbell-era Lions have been prevalent this week, and one reason for that is Miami’s reliable and developing offensive line. From left to right, Patrick Paul, Kadyn Proctor, Aaron Brewer, Jonah Savaiinaea, and Austin Jackson form an above-average unit with a good mix of proven, reliable veterans and young, ascending players. They’ve started to give the Dolphins a fighting chance by being imposing and winning at the line of scrimmage. Since Week 4, the Dolphins have shifted their rushing approach, leaning into their offensive line and Gordon’s preferred running schemes by utilizing power concepts on 13.8% of runs (5th) and man/duo concepts on 20.7% of rushing attempts (15th), with considerable success. With power, which features a backside pulling guard attacking the frontside like a runaway freight train, Miami has averaged 5.7 yards per carry (7th), +0.219 EPA/rush (6th), a 56.3% rushing success rate (5th), and a 25.0% explosive run rate (4th) since Week 4. Power runs will require Detroit’s linebackers to not only process and flow quickly, but also meet the pulling guard in the hole without giving up ground and scrape from the backside. The linebackers need to be firing on all cylinders to match Miami’s physical, downhill approach. The same goes for defending man/duo concepts, where the Dolphins’ offense has churned out 5.1 yards per carry (5th), +0.122 EPA/rush (5th), a 50.0% rushing success rate (5th), and an 8.3% explosive run rate (15th) since Week 4. Interestingly, teams haven’t really tested the Lions’ defense with power runs this season, with only 3.1% of rushing attempts (31st) coming on power concepts. Detroit has faced just one such rush since Week 4, which went for minus-4 yards. The Lions have fared well in the small sample size, allowing only 3.4 yards per carry (t-11th) and no explosive plays on their limited snaps defending power. Teams have, however, tested the Lions’ defense up the gut with man/duo concepts, running them on 31.3% of rushing attempts (5th). Detroit has countered that volume by cleaning up those physical runs, allowing just a 33.3% rushing success rate (4th) and 0.6 yards after contact per rush (2nd). An underrated key to preventing the Dolphins from outmuscling Detroit up the middle with power and man/duo concepts will be whether Tyleik Williams can play with his hair on fire against All-Pro center Aaron Brewer. Brewer understands leverage and angles better than most centers in the league, but he’s also a pivot player who stands just 6-foot-1 and 290 pounds. If the 6-foot-3 Williams, who notably lost a ton of weight this spring to get down to just 325 pounds, can win at the point of attack, overpower Brewer into the backfield, disrupt rushing lanes and timing, and congest the flow of the run play, it’ll go a long way toward making the linebackers’ jobs much easier. God Forbid a Willis Gets a Little Motion While the Dolphins’ offense under second-year holdover offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik, formerly of the Houston Texans, doesn’t do much well outside of some aspects of its run designs, it does one thing often enough that it might challenge the Detroit Lions’ defense. The Dolphins’ offense uses pre-snap motion on 74.1% of its snaps, the second-highest rate of any team in the NFL. The league average is only 59.2%, while the Lions’ offense, for comparison’s sake, sits at just 54.5% (24th). What’s interesting is that the Dolphins aren’t particularly better at rushing or passing the football with or without pre-snap motion, remaining bottom 10 in most metrics. The prevalence of the pre-snap motion itself is what’s important here. The Lions’ defense hasn’t been tested as frequently against pre-snap motion this season, and when it has, there have been some struggles. Detroit has faced pre-snap motion on only 52.1% of its defensive snaps, the second-lowest rate in the NFL. The Lions have actually excelled at defending the run against pre-snap motion, restricting opponents to -0.16 EPA/rush (4th) and just a 36.7% rushing success rate (4th). Detroit has managed to shut down offenses trying to gain an advantage in the numbers game, manipulate gap assignments, or use motion to stretch the defense geometrically, get defenders out of position, and create rushing lanes. However, issues arise in pass defense against pre-snap motion. Even if the Dolphins haven’t been particularly successful using it, there are still some concerns for Detroit. Opponents have passed on 63.6% of plays featuring pre-snap motion against the Lions’ defense, the highest pass-to-run ratio in the NFL on such plays. Against pre-snap motion, Detroit’s pass defense has allowed +0.22 EPA/dropback (29th), a 54.1% passing success rate (26th), and an 11.6% explosive pass rate (27th). The Lions’ coverage unit will need to communicate effectively and trust one another, particularly with a new green dot in either Derrick Barnes or…

title: What the Packers’ roster could look like vs. the Patriots
summary: The Green Bay Packers only made one roster move on Saturday, bringing up practice squad tight end Drake Dabney to the game-day roster for action against the New England Patriots. As always, the moves that the Packers make, and don’t make, give us hints at what the roster is expected to look like on Sunday. […]
full_text: (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers only made one roster move on Saturday, bringing up practice squad tight end Drake Dabney to the game-day roster for action against the New England Patriots. As always, the moves that the Packers make, and don’t make, give us hints at what the roster is expected to look like on Sunday. Let’s get into the information we have now. Out with injury Four players have already been ruled out with injuries, bringing the Packers’ 53-man active roster to 49. The players out are tight end Josh Whyle (concussion), offensive lineman Travis Glover (knee), offensive lineman Sean Rhyan (ankle) and linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin). The Packers lost Whyle in-game against the Carolina Panthers, carrying only three tight ends on game day and scratching Jonnu Smith for the first time this season, while Glover, Rhyan and Franklin did not play. Expected scratches This season, the Packers have seemingly had no interest in carrying four running backs on the game-day roster. The same can be said about a ninth offensive lineman, despite the team consistently keeping 11 on the active roster. If you add in those scratches, Green Bay’s active roster drops down to 47 players. With the addition of Dabney, who is expected to replace the special teams snaps of Whyle (the only real special teams contributor on offense who isn’t a receiver), that gets us to a 48-man gameday roster. It’s pretty tidy. Questionable players The players listed as questionable going into the weekend were running back MarShawn Lloyd (knee), cornerback Keisean Nixon (groin) and running back Chris Brooks (ankle). Brooks isn’t on the active roster yet, as he’s going through his practice window after spending time on the injured reserve. If he were going to play on Sunday, you would have seen an activation today. Nixon is highly likely to play, as the Packers don’t really have a replacement for him on the roster, as it stands currently. If he were going to miss this game, we probably would have seen a second call-up from the practice squad on Saturday. Lloyd may or may not play. If he can’t go, the team will displace him with Kaleb Johnson, Green Bay’s fourth running back, who has been a healthy scratch since Josh Jacobs’ return to the team. Roster breakdown Here’s what the team will probably look like on Sunday (with the biggest questions being which offensive lineman gets healthy-scratched and if Lloyd can go): QB: Jordan Love and Tyrod Taylor RB: Josh Jacobs and Pierre Strong Jr. One of: MarShawn Lloyd or Kaleb Johnson WR: Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, Savion Williams, Bo Melton, J. Michael Sturdivant and Coleman Owen TE: Tucker Kraft, Mark Redman, Jonnu Smith and Drake Dabney OL: 8 players up, 3 scratched (two for sure being Sean Rhyan and Travis Glover) Most likely: Jordan Morgan, Aaron Banks, John Williams, Laken Tomlinson, Anthony Belton, Kevin Zeitler, Mekhi Becton Sr. and Jager Burton active; Donnovan Jennings a healthy scratch, along with Rhyan and Glover being out with injury. DL: Karl Brooks, Devonte Wyatt, Chris McClellan, Jordon Riley and Anthony Campbell ED: Lukas Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell, Brenton Cox Jr. and Dani Dennis-Sutton LB: Isaiah McDuffie, Ty’Ron Hopper, Nick Niemann and Kristian Welch CB: Keisean Nixon, Brandon Cisse, Carrington Valentine, Benjamin St-Juste and Kamal Hadden S: Xavier McKinney, Evan Williams, Javon Bullard, Kitan Oladapo K: Trey Smack P: Daniel Whelan LS: Matt Orzech That’s your 48-man roster against the Patriots.

title: Colts reportedly ‘not interested’ in moving QB Daniel Jones ahead of trade deadline
summary: According to NFL Insider Tom Pelissero, while they’ve received inquiries from other teams, the Indianapolis Colts are not considering trading starting quarterback Daniel Jones ahead of next Tuesday’s trade deadline: In particular, the Minnesota Vikings, who have also been connected as a suitor for star Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, have been linked to a […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts and Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings shake hands after the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The Vikings defeated the Colts 16-10. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to NFL Insider Tom Pelissero, while they’ve received inquiries from other teams, the Indianapolis Colts are not considering trading starting quarterback Daniel Jones ahead of next Tuesday’s trade deadline: The Colts have received calls on QB Daniel Jones ahead of Tuesday’s deadline, but they’ve told interested teams they aren’t trading him. More in The Sweep: https://t.co/2WjDotrPhy pic.twitter.com/LYOgpVd3gL — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 7, 2026 In particular, the Minnesota Vikings, who have also been connected as a suitor for star Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, have been linked to a potential reunion with Jones ahead of the league’s trade deadline. Incumbent starter Kyler Murray has been battling a ‘Grade 2’ hamstring strain that will keep him out at least a few weeks and hasn’t been all that effective during his debut campaign in Minnesota regardless. After being previously benched and released by the New York Giants in November of 2024, Jones was initially signed to the Vikings practice squad before being elevated to their active 53-man roster later that same season as one of the team’s backups behind entrenched starter Sam Darnold. Even though his stint in Minnesota was brief, Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell was impressed enough with Jones that they were the Colts’ primary competition to sign him during his ensuing 2025 free agency. With Darnold having signed with the Seattle Seahawks in free agency, but former 2024 10th overall J.J. McCarthy in the fold in Minnesota, Jones elected to join Shane Steichen in Indianapolis and battle Anthony Richardson Sr. for the Colts QB1 job instead. Jones would ultimately beat out Richardson for Indy’s starting quarterback job two offseasons ago, and the rest remains history in Indianapolis. That being said coming off a 2025 season-ending torn Achilles, Jones has clearly struggled during his second season with the Colts in 2026. He’s completed 162 of 268 pass attempts (60.4% completion rate), 1,542 total passing yards, 5 passing touchdowns, and 9 interceptions during all 8 starts. He hasn’t been nearly as explosive running the football, and his ability to plant and drive on his throws have both significantly declined from the quarterback that led the Colts to an 8-2 record near midseason of last year. His pocket presence isn’t as confident either, and he’s not handling blitzes well,so there’s also a mental side of it too. With Steichen looking increasing unlikely to be retained at year-end, and Jones likely joining him in NFL unemployment as a cap cut this upcoming offseason, it doesn’t make sense to me as to why the Colts wouldn’t look to clear some of his salary cap off the books, as Jones has a $10.51M injury guarantee for next year (that becomes fully guaranteed on March 15th if he remains on the Colts roster), while also potentially acquiring a ‘Day 3’ draft pick in the process.

title: There is a lot for the Colts to consider as they move forward this season.
summary: I have to admit that I have started and stopped writing this two or three times. I don’t think that I have anything new to add in this stomach churning segment of the season. Much has been discussed about our desire to see both the offensive and defensive leaders of the team relieved of their […]
full_text: I have to admit that I have started and stopped writing this two or three times. I don’t think that I have anything new to add in this stomach churning segment of the season. Much has been discussed about our desire to see both the offensive and defensive leaders of the team relieved of their duties. Not for the purpose of seeing a drastic improvement and unlikely playoff run, but simply a “We have seen enough” feeling. We’ve ran the cycle of every player that we’d like to trade or keep, and how much we’d expect to get in return. I’d throw my hat in the ring, but the honest truth is that it would be a guess. I really struggle understanding firing CB, then putting Dodds in charge of the who stays and who goes decisions. Maybe CB refused to make decisions for the next regime and that was his last act. I know that someone has to do it and maybe Carlie is keeping plausible deniability, by allowing the current admin to make these calls. I will say that I would bench Jones, but intend to keep him next year. He can’t do what he needs to do with his physical limitations. He will be past those limitations by the start of next season. A new GM could find Jones a better option than others who might be available and not as expensive as many suggest. At minimum, that GM gets a year to form his own opinion. If a rookie is brought in, I can’t see it being one that you are ready to throw to the wolves immediately, especially with the AR wounds still pretty fresh. As far as team building, I do not know who has Carlie’s ear right now? She has a very important decision regarding who is tasked with getting the Colts off the mat and back in the fight. She has had to have made some contacts with a person or persons that she feels that she can trust, but I do not know who that might be? I also do not quite understand her desire to continue to be on the sidelines and tuned in. What can she pick up by listening to Shane and Lou? If she did decide to meddle, she could get away with it pretty easily this season. I don’t think her presence is necessarily inspiring the players to give their best effort. The information that she needs to be gathering right now, is who will be the next eyes, ears, and voice of the franchise. I think she has picked up enough to have her expectations as to what she wants to hear from a GM, during the interview process. I think a view from the suite, might give her a different perspective. She can listen if she wants, it is her business to run. This is the time of the season when the “lay down” banter begins. I’ve never been a proponent and even less this year, when it doesn’t affect the first round pick. It appears that Shane and Lou will be allowed to keep doing things that don’t work, so the best you can do is protect players from getting hurt during a season that essentially means nothing. There are lots of lame ducks that are not going to get off of the ground. Honestly, I do not think we need to avoid winning, as it is going to occur naturally. It is time to see who has some pride in their craft. Do not reward lack of effort with playing time. You can live with some mistakes, if they are mistakes of aggression and excitement. I’m not proposing cutting players, but there are lots of incentives that players can’t reach, if they are not on the field. Maybe someone on the bench, or a practice squader emerges as a player? It is hard for bench players to show anything after camp is over. The NFL barely lets you have contact in practice, so how can you show what you have learned in the film room? Give them their shot. So, while we are not considering what has to be done to make the playoffs, there are still many considerations, far more than I have mentioned, which will shape the path forward. I’m normally not one to punt, but if you realize that punting can be a strategic play, maybe it is more palatable this season. We as fans might be a little more patient during this time. Many recently blasted the organization for the return they got for Q. As we find out that he had an injury, prior to the trade, maybe we should consider that we don’t know the whole story on nearly anything.

title: Chiefs elevate practice squad DT Marcus Harris for Week 9
summary: According to the NFL’s official transactions report form Saturday, the Kansas City Chiefs have elevated defensive tackle Marcus Harris from the practice squad for their Week 9 game against the New York Jets. Harris notably made the Chiefs’ initial roster coming out of training camp only to find himself cut the next day as defensive […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 20: Marcus Harris #96 of the Kansas City Chiefs rushes the quarterback during an NFL football game against the Indianapolis Colts at Arrowhead Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to the NFL’s official transactions report form Saturday, the Kansas City Chiefs have elevated defensive tackle Marcus Harris from the practice squad for their Week 9 game against the New York Jets . Harris notably made the Chiefs’ initial roster coming out of training camp only to find himself cut the next day as defensive lineman Bryson Eason and defensive end Jack Pyburn were added off waivers. Harris immediately signed to Kansas City’s practice squad. The Chiefs elevated Harris for their first two games while Eason worked into the system, and the former Kansas Jayhawk played a total of seven defensive snaps. With rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods ruled out on this week’s final injury report, Harris seemingly has a path to bigger role in his third appearance of 2026. Having exhausted the three permitted practice squad elevations on the season, the Chiefs would have to add Harris back onto the active roster for him to play again before the process resets for hypothetical postseason games. However, second-year defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott appears to be nearing a return from a torn ACL suffered in 2025. Norman-Lott is nearing the end of his 21-day practice window to the activated from the Reserve/Physically-Unable-to-Perform list. As an elevated player, Harris will immediately return to the practice squad after Sunday’s game. Kansas City did not use their other permitted practice squad elevation for Week 9. This would imply that punt returner Nikko Remigio will play after being listed as questionable with a hip injury. The Chiefs added rookie return man Jacob De Jesus — who atteded training camp with the team — to the practice squad on Wednesday, seemingly as insurance in case Remigio could not go.

title: AP readers’ 2026 Midseason Hot Seat watch for NFL coaches
summary: A month ago, we asked our readers to give us a list of head coaches who should be on the hot seat. At the time, you guys told us that the person who should have the hottest tushy was the head coach of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Todd Bowles. In second place was Green Bay […]
full_text: (Robert Gauthier/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) A month ago , we asked our readers to give us a list of head coaches who should be on the hot seat. At the time, you guys told us that the person who should have the hottest tushy was the head coach of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , Todd Bowles. In second place was Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur, and rounding out the list was Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh. The NFL is a wild place, and a lot can happen in a month. Since our last edition of this series, two of the three coaches who were previously predicted to be on their way out have found a way to right their ship enough for the time being to at least work their way off this list. But one coach has not disappointed and has lived up to our expectations of sub-par performance. Heck, some might even say his team has exceeded expectations of just how truly awful they can be. When it comes to sucking, this guy is the gold standard. Here is what you said. 1. Jim Harbaugh – Los Angeles Chargers Previous Ranking: 3 Heat Rating: Like every fart he has ever had in his entire life is coming out all at once Harbaugh (seen in the image above showing one of his players what his pet turtle looks like when it’s trying to eat lettuce) has been hard at work moving up the charts. Jumping from third place to first, Captain Khaki Pants has continued to be haunted by the angry spirits of the San Diego faithful, who are still angry that the team left their lovely city in favor of being Los Angeles’ unwanted stepchild. The Chargers have lost their last two games by double digits, with their most recent loss coming to their big brothers, the Los Angeles Rams , who held Harbaugh’s team to just nine points. Quarterback Justin Herbert continues to have the worst season of his career — with a season QBR of just 32.5, he’s currently sporting an uninspiring 5/10 interception-to-touchdown ratio. The Chargers are by far the worst team in the league. The only question is: can Harbaugh buy himself one more year by throwing his coordinators under the bus to save his own skin? What if every fart you have ever done come out once? We did the math. pic.twitter.com/A8cA0UESDQ — Way Of Discipline (@wayofdiscipline) November 6, 2026 Here is what you had to say: “Andy Reid /s But seriously, Dave Toub should be. Not quite sure why he’s still a Chief. head coaches? Dan Quinn, Jim Harbaugh, Dave Canales” – Phoenix_Chief 2. Nick Sirianni- Philadelphia Eagles Previous Ranking: N/A Heat Rating: On the toilet after appearing on the YouTube series “Hot Ones.” Sirianni (seen here looking down at his shoes and trying to remember if he put them on the right feet) is the only coach on this list to have won a Super Bowl. At first glance, it might seem a little unfair to have Sirianni on this list, especially when you consider he lost his starting quarterback for the season, and his best offensive lineman (Lane Johnson) decided to retire mid-year. But the Eagles have dropped six in a row, and this isn’t the first time a Sirianni-coached team has folded under pressure. In 2021, the Eagles were 10-1, heading into Week 13, and proceeded to go 1-5 the rest of the way to close out the season, squeaking into the playoffs as a wildcard, where they promptly got bounced by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 32-9. Also, it’s a little hard to feel bad for anyone in the Eagles organization this season, when the Eagles’ starting quarterback, Jalen Hurts, had a serious medical emergency due to his diagnosis of blood clots in his lungs being mishandled by the team. bill murray's reaction to every wing on hot ones 💪 (and pete davidson's reaction to the last dab 🫠 ) pic.twitter.com/x5ezxTUgZC — First We Feast (@firstwefeast) March 6, 2025 Here is what you had to say: “Siriani has got to be sitting on a cast iron skillet at the very least” – Andyreidsmustache_ 3. Dan Quinn- Washington Commanders Previous Ranking: N/A Heat Rating: Sitting too close to the campfire so that the soles on your shoes start to melt Since making a surprise appearance in the NFC Championship game in 2024, Dan Quinn (pictured above thinking he just had to toot, but realizing a little bit more came out) and the Commanders have gone 7-16 combined. That’s a .304 winning percentage over the last two seasons. Some may give Quinn a pass because his franchise quarterback, Jayden Daniels, has been a regular on the injured list. But let’s be real: the NFL is a results-driven industry, and fair or not, the output just hasn’t been there. Quinn made his name in the NFL as a defensive coordinator with the Seattle Seahawks , so it’s a tough look when the only team you’ve held to under 20 points on the season is the aforementioned Eagles. Especially when three teams have dropped 30+ points on you so far this year. Here is what you had to say: “Harbaugh, Schottenheimer, Siriani, and quinn all will be gone” – chiefhawk Guys who should be monitoring the temperature of their cheeks: Shane Steichen ( Indianapolis Colts ), Dave Canales ( Carolina Panthers ), and Brian Schottenheimer ( Dallas Cowboys )

title: Chiefs-Jets: 5 questions with Gang Green Nation ahead of Week 9
summary: On Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs face the New York Jets in the early afternoon slot of Week 9 games. We welcome MacGregor Wells of Gang Green Nation— our sister SBNation site covering the Jets— for Five Questions with the Enemy. Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device and join the Gang Green […]
full_text: Credit: Denny Medley-USA TODAY Sports | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect On Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs face the New York Jets in the early afternoon slot of Week 9 games. We welcome MacGregor Wells of Gang Green Nation— our sister SBNation site covering the Jets— for Five Questions with the Enemy . Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Join fellow Chiefs fans to react to every explosive play and game-changing moment in real time. Chat live throughout the game Browse with fewer ads Easily jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device and join the Gang Green Nation community through Sunday’s game to get perspectives from both sides of the Week 9 matchup! 1. The Jets are 2-6, but five of their six losses have been decided by one score, including last week’s 38-33 loss after they led Las Vegas 30-21. What has prevented this team from closing out games it has been in position to win? Part of this is always luck. Which team wins a one-score game often comes down to an untimely turnover, a costly penalty, an unlucky bounce, whatever. Things that are going to happen to any team, but happen at the wrong time to losing teams. However, the element that isn’t just bad luck for the Jets is bad coaching. The Jets have blown fairly big second-half leads. They have had comebacks come up just short. They have outplayed better teams only to lose late, and they have come out flat against lesser teams they should have beaten. The one stat that people keep on bringing up is a 100 – 6 deficit in the last two minutes of halves under Aaron Glenn’s “leadership.” I think the numbers have changed slightly since that stat came out, but you get the picture. That kind of absurd imbalance in two-minute situations is the direct result of poor coaching. The Jets look completely lost in two-minute drills. How can an NFL team be that clueless and that ineffective in crunch time? It’s nuts. There are plenty of other coaching issues I could mention, but that one stat kind of encapsulates the general incompetence of the Jets coaching. It’s frustrating because for so many years the Jets simply didn’t have the talent to be competitive. This year they have the talent. Oh, don’t get me wrong, this is no juggernaut roster. But unlike recent years, the Jets at least have the talent to be competitive in almost every game. They have been competitive. But they continue to lose. Thank you, Aaron Glenn. 2. Geno Smith has completed 69% of his passes for 1,913 yards, 12 touchdowns and only three interceptions during his return to New York. What has allowed Smith to play some of the most efficient football of his career during his second stint with the Jets? Part of this is probably just good luck. Smith has always been a turnover-prone quarterback. He began this season with five straight interception-free games, but it seemed like a mirage. His judgment and field vision haven’t suddenly taken a quantum leap in the twilight of his career. Sure enough, Smith has thrown an interception in each of his last three games. Reversion to the mean is a powerful thing. The other part is the talent that surrounds Smith on offense. The Jets have a good offensive line. They have multiple talented backs. They have solid tight ends, and they have three good receivers in Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, and rookie Omar Cooper. The defense is a mess, but the offensive talent is the best group the Jets have had in at least a decade. Geno Smith has benefited from the talent around him. Even so, the Jets have scored more than 25 points in a game just once all year, so for all the somewhat gaudy Geno stats, the bottom line is the Jets haven’t exactly lit up the scoreboard. 3. Garrett Wilson is currently in concussion protocol after catching six passes for 83 yards against the Raiders. If Wilson cannot play Sunday, which Jets playmaker will need to become the focal point of the offense? Third-year running back Braelon Allen has been impressive since Breece Hall exited game three with a leg injury, thrusting Allen into the starting role. In the last five games, Allen has been one of the best running backs in the NFL. Hall is likely to finally be back in the lineup for the Jets on Sunday, but I’m hoping, probably in vain, that the Jets have seen that Allen is the better back. Regardless of which back gets the bulk of the work, the Chiefs have been one of the best teams in the NFL in stopping the run, so if the Jets are to have any chance in this game, I would guess Geno Smith and the Jets receivers will need to have a big game. Omar Cooper might be the guy to look out for, as well as fellow rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq. If Garrett Wilson doesn’t play, those two are the most talented weapons the Jets have in the passing game. 4. The Jets rank 11th in total defense, but they surrendered 38 points and allowed the Raiders to score touchdowns on all four of their red-zone possessions last week. What is the biggest vulnerability Kansas City should attempt to exploit in New York’s defense? The Jets’ 11th ranking in total defense is a sham. The Jets defense stinks. They have one good pass rusher, rookie David Bailey. The interior defensive line is a shambles with both David Onyemata and T’Vondre Sweat out injured. The linebackers are slow and mostly ineffective. The same can be said about the cornerbacks. Safety Dane Belton has been a revelation in his first year with the Jets after spending his early career with the Giants. He’s been really good, especially against the run. The other safety, Minkah Fitzpatrick, is in steep decline, living on reputation after a stellar career. This is an untalented Jets defense that had the good fortune to face some bad offenses, some backup quarterbacks and some teams with injury problems early in the year. Lately, the results have deteriorated badly. The Jets have allowed 26+ points on defense in each of the last three games. I expect that to be more of what we can expect from the Jets defense going forward. This shouldn’t be a challenging game for the Kansas City offense. I expect Kenneth Walker to run wild against a porous Jets run defense, and I expect Patrick Mahomes to pick apart a mediocre Jets secondary. If the Jets have any chance for an unlikely upset on Sunday, it will probably have to be in a shootout. I just don’t see the Jets defense shutting down Mahomes, Walker, Rice and company. 5. The Jets have lost three consecutive games, while the Chiefs return home after dropping two straight and falling out of first place in the AFC West. How do you see Sunday’s game unfolding, including your final score prediction? The Jets have one chance against the Chiefs: a Chiefs letdown. It isn’t always easy getting up for the dregs of the league. Sometimes you look past a lesser opponent. If the Chiefs come out flat, maybe the Jets can steal a win if the Jets offense plays up to its talent level. However, Kansas City is a very difficult venue for Chiefs opponents. Even if the Chiefs come out flat, it’s likely the Jets’ bad coaching will blow the opportunity for an upset. The gap between future Hall of Fame coach Andy Reid and future out-of-work coach Aaron Glenn is enormous. It will be difficult for the Jets to overcome that. If the Chiefs don’t come out flat, this game shouldn’t be close. I am terrible at score predictions, but let’s go with Chiefs 27, Jets 16.
author: Maurice Elston

title: Kingdom Keys: 3 Keys to a Chiefs victory over the Jets in Week 9
summary: After opening the season with five consecutive victories, the Kansas City Chiefs return to Arrowhead Stadium riding a two-game losing streak. The 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks was a poor performance in all three phases. Kansas City’s offense responded with 399 total yards and 24 points against the Denver Broncos, but the defense surrendered […]
full_text: East Rutherford, NJ October 1, 2023 | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co After opening the season with five consecutive victories, the Kansas City Chiefs return to Arrowhead Stadium riding a two-game losing streak. The 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks was a poor performance in all three phases. Kansas City’s offense responded with 399 total yards and 24 points against the Denver Broncos , but the defense surrendered a late touchdown in a 28-24 loss. The Chiefs remain in the AFC West race and in contention for the AFC’s No. 1 seed, but they can no longer afford to lose games they are expected to win. The New York Jets are only 2-6 and have lost three consecutive games, but they have remained competitive. Quarterback Geno Smith is coming off a 290-yard, two-touchdown performance in which the Jets scored a season-high 33 points. Kansas City should win this game. To do so convincingly, it must accomplish these three things. Offensive key: Restore the vertical passing game Kansas City’s declining rushing production over the past two weeks has drawn plenty of discussion. After averaging 6.3 yards per carry and rushing for 665 yards over his first five games, Kenneth Walker III has been held to 105 rushing yards on 35 carries over the last two. That is an average of only 3.0 yards per attempt. Some of that decline can be attributed to offensive-line execution and opposing defenses adjusting to Kansas City’s running concepts. However, wide receiver Tyquan Thornton’s absence has also changed how defenses can play the Chiefs. Thornton was Kansas City’s primary field-stretching receiver. Before dislocating his ankle against the Las Vegas Raiders , he caught 11 passes for 219 yards — nearly 20 yards per reception. His final catch was a 55-yard gain against Cover 0 that demonstrated exactly what he provided: a receiver capable of making defenses pay for crowding the line of scrimmage. Walker still rushed for 128 yards against the Los Angeles Chargers after Thornton’s injury, so the receiver’s absence is not the only explanation for the recent struggles. But as teams have gained more film of the Thornton-less offense, they have become increasingly comfortable bringing safeties closer to the line and challenging Kansas City’s remaining receivers to win downfield. Through seven games, approximately 90% of Patrick Mahomes’ throws have traveled fewer than 20 yards beyond the line of scrimmage. Only 24 of his 232 attempts were directed 20 or more yards downfield, per statchasers.com . Kansas City does not need to throw deep on every possession. It must, however, prove that the threat exists. Head coach Andy Reid should create opportunities through play-action, max protection and pre-snap motion. Xavier Worthy is the most obvious candidate to assume more of that vertical responsibility, but Rashee Rice, Jalen Royals and Cyrus Allen must also contribute. The objective is not simply to complete one long pass. Kansas City needs to make New York’s safeties respect the possibility. If the Chiefs can connect on multiple passes of at least 20 yards, the Jets will be forced to defend more of the field. That should create additional running room for Walker and restore the balance that powered Kansas City’s 5-0 start. Defensive key: Sack Nation must return Kansas City’s pass rush has not lived up to its nickname. The Chiefs enter Week 9 with nine sacks, ranking 30th in the NFL. Their 3.6% defensive sack rate is among the league’s worst. No player better represents those struggles than defensive tackle Chris Jones. The self-proclaimed CEO of “Sack Nation” has recorded only half a sack, three quarterback hits and one tackle for loss through seven games. During the losses to Seattle and Denver, Jones failed to register a tackle, quarterback hit or pass breakup across 87 combined snaps. Jones continues to command double teams, and his presence can create opportunities for teammates. But those opportunities only matter if someone capitalizes on them. Defensive end George Karlaftis has been Kansas City’s most consistent pass rusher, but Felix Anudike-Uzomah, Ashton Gillotte, R. Mason Thomas, and the rest of the defensive front must win more one-on-one matchups. Against Denver, the Chiefs pressured Bo Nix on only two of his 34 dropbacks—a 6% pressure rate, the lowest recorded by any NFL defense in a game this season. The Jets present an ideal opportunity for the pass rush to get healthy. Smith has already been sacked 23 times, and New York ranks 26th in sack rate allowed at 9.62%. Smith has otherwise played well, throwing 12 touchdowns against only three interceptions with a 104.5 passer rating. Kansas City cannot let him operate comfortably and push the ball downfield. The defensive benchmark should be at least three sacks, with Jones directly contributing to one of them —either by recording it himself or forcing Smith into another defender. This is the matchup in which Sack Nation needs to reappear. X-factor: Win on third down Third down will connect everything Kansas City wants to accomplish on Sunday. Offensively, the Chiefs have converted 34 of their 85 third downs, exactly 40%. The Jets’ defense has allowed opponents to convert 41 of 100 attempts. That presents Kansas City with an opportunity to extend drives and wear down an injury-affected New York defensive front. Mahomes cannot be asked to repeatedly rescue the offense on third-and-long. The Chiefs must use early-down runs, play-action passes, and quick completions to create manageable situations. The goal should be to convert at least 45% of their third downs. Defensively, Kansas City must get off the field. The season-long numbers are respectable, with opponents converting 39.2% of their third-down attempts. But Seattle converted 11 of 16 third downs, including five situations requiring at least 9 yards. Those conversions let the Seahawks control the ball for nearly 36 minutes and limit Kansas City to only eight possessions. New York’s offense has converted 37.6% of its third downs this season. That is below the league’s better offenses, but Smith’s experience and willingness to push the football vertically make him dangerous if Kansas City cannot generate pressure. Third down is where Jones and the defensive line can change the game. A sack ends a possession, improves field position, and gives Mahomes another opportunity to attack a Jets defense allowing 23.5 points per game. Kansas City needs to win third down on both sides by extending its own possessions and quickly ending New York’s. The bottom line The Chiefs should not need Patrick Mahomes to carry them through another four-quarter fight against a 2-6 opponent. Kansas City must restore the deep-ball threat and force New York’s safeties away from the line of scrimmage. That will create more space for Kenneth Walker and prevent the offense from becoming predictable. Defensively, Chris Jones and Sack Nation must take advantage of an offensive line that has already allowed 23 sacks. On third down, the Chiefs must sustain their own drives while refusing to let the Jets control the clock. If Kansas City can produce multiple explosive passes, record at least three sacks and win the third-down battle, it should not merely end its losing streak — it should do so convincingly.
