summary: Well, Kyler is out and Wentz is in and the team is still home dogs. I guess it makes sense. I suppose Wentz is going to make everything better and get Jefferson a few more catches so everyone is happy eh? I think there is a ton of overreaction and jump to conclusion stories, etc […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-NOVEMBER 1: Head coach Kevin O'Connell of the Minnesota Vikings follows the play during the first half of an NFL football game between the Minnesota Vikings and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, November 1, 2026 (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Well, Kyler is out and Wentz is in and the team is still home dogs. I guess it makes sense. I suppose Wentz is going to make everything better and get Jefferson a few more catches so everyone is happy eh? I think there is a ton of overreaction and jump to conclusion stories, etc being thrown out there because that is just the nature of the sports media landscape. Kyler had a hamstring (which is now revealed to be a grade 2 strain) and played 3 more snaps afterwards. When Jefferson hurt his hammy he also played a few more snaps before he had to shut it down. KOC seems like he is leaning towards putting Kyler back out there when he is healthy. I suppose it depends on Wentz as well. I could be the right move because players like Hockenson have said, “they are not far off”. It seems to me that Kyler is not trusting what he sees or still might be swimming in the offense a bit. He has been careful with the ball and has provided some very timely runs which I was hoping for more of them. We wont get those runs from Wentz. Those will be sacks and then the complaints will be about the offense line. I do not see KOC giving up just yet. I know some feel he gave up on JJ but that is complete hogwash. The dude had two years plus another offseason to grab the job and make it his own. Injury was the main reason he could not do it. The trade was fair and it aligns with past recent trades. Trey Lance with for a 4th from the Cowboys. Mac Jones went for a 6th. Justin Fields went for a conditional 6th. Here were their stats before the trade … Quarterback | Team | Games (Starts) | Comp / Att (Pct) | Passing Yards | Passing TDs | Interceptions | Rushing Yards / TDs J.J. McCarthy | Vikings | 10 (10) | 140 / 243 (57.6%) | 1,632 | 11 | 12 | 181 / 4 Trey Lance | 49ers | 8 (4) | 56 / 102 (54.9%) | 797 | 5 | 3 | 235 / 1 Justin Fields | Bears | 40 (38) | 578 / 958 (60.3%) | 6,674 | 40 | 30 | 2,220 / 14 Mac Jones | Patriots | 42 (42) | 864 / 1,308 (66.1%) | 8,918 | 46 | 36 | 327 / 2 … if Mac Jones who had 42 starts and 8918 yards passing goes for a 6th then JJ going for a 5th was a good deal. I know that some feel the team should have kept him and that is a fair argument. They do save about 3.8M in cap space in 2027 but that is about the number for a backup QB. This has led folks to believe it was to remove any distraction which is hard to dispute or prove as well. I do not know what happened to be honest. My gut and tin foil hat suspicions make me want to believe that when he did not play in that last preseason game, it bothered the coaches and GM. Imagine if he did play and they did make him the #2 QB. He would have played those two weeks and could be starting now. I am not saying he did anything wrong but it is kind if funny how things work out eh? I wish him good luck and I hope he simply can stay healthy. He probably will have some not so good games but that still is to be expected because the young man still does not even have a full season of starts. But that is over now and the jump to conclusion and sports media dweebs (like myself I guess – I prefer doofus) are speculating about all kinds of trades. Figures like Schefter are saying things like he “is watching the Vikings QB situation”. I do not know what QB would actually be available though. Justin Herbert appears to be the dream target and if the Chargers decided they were going to move him they would eat 50.5M in dead money next year but since his cap hit is already 58.3M they would actually save $7.9M in cap space. But their only other healthy QB is DJ Iiagalelei. They also have Trey Lance who is on IR but eligible to return on Nov 16th. The problem which could be rectified with a restructure is that his salary is 24M this year of which 12M is what the Vikings would need to pay. What would be an offer? Vikings send 2027, 2028, and 2029 first round picks, plus 2027 second and fifth round picks for Herbert and a 2027 fourth. Vikings can throw in Murray or Wentz. Odds? Zero. Only if the Vikings still had JJ McCarthy they could have sent him to the Chargers for Herbert straight up right? Just kidding. But he could have been included and it may have made Hairball (aka Booger Eater) seriously consider it. Sam Darnold is being taked about too. If the Seahawks moved him they would have 19.2M in dead money for 2027 but would save 25.7M. Darnold has a 12.3M salary this year of which the Vikings would be responsible for about half which they can immediately restructure to fit him in the cap space they have available. From a cap perspective, it can work easier. Darnold has completed 127 out of 211 passes (60.2%) for 1,478 yards with 10 TDs and 9 INTs and has taken 17 sacks while rushing 11 times for 72 yards. His passer rating is 79.5. From AI … The advanced metrics reveal that his performance drops off a cliff when things get messy around him, directly deciding the outcome of those close losses: The Duress Analytics Breakdown When the offensive line leaks pressure, Darnold’s composure and efficiency completely disappear. NFL Next Gen Stats map out a stark contrast between his clean-pocket efficiency and his numbers under duress this season: Completion Percentage: He is completing only 31.3% of his passes when under pressure. The In-Duress Ratio: He has thrown 5 interceptions to just 2 touchdowns while facing a collapsing pocket. Under Pressure QBR: His total Quarterback Rating under duress is a microscopic 3.9 out of 100. How it Caused the 4 Losses This pressure problem directly manifested as the losing variable in all four defeats: The Overtime Heartbreak (vs. Denver): The most clear-cut example was the 17-14 loss to the Broncos. Facing a relentless Denver front, Darnold was sacked 5 times and tossed 2 critical interceptions—including a turnover in overtime that set up Denver’s game-winning field goal. The 49ers Meltdown: The San Francisco pass rush completely rattled him. He took 5 sacks again and gave away 2 costly interceptions, preventing the offense from ever establishing a rhythm. The Bears Disaster: In the 34-17 loss to Chicago where he suffered the injuries, he dropped back under heavy pressure. He completed just 1 of 11 attempts for 13 yards and an interception while under duress. His average time to throw ballooned to 2.89 seconds because he held onto the ball too long, trying to force explosive plays instead of checking it down … I do not know what kind of offer it would take but I think we have seen this move before no? Last year, the Seahawks had a great running fame and defense to insulate against Darnold’s turnovers. 14 interceptions and 11 fumbles (6 lost). Maybe last year was Darnold’s Nick Foles or Trent Dilfer type moment? What would be an offer? Nothing. Geno Smith is another name that has recently popped up in the trade deadline chatter. The Jets are 2-6 and may want to give Cade Klubnik some game action. Geno is completing 69% of his passes for 1,913 yards with 12 TDs and 3 INTs. Smith is 36 years old and a free agent next year so this might only be a rental. They also would need to get back Murray or Wentz What would be an offer? Vikings send a 2027 5th and Kyler Murray Jets send a 2027 6th and Geno Smith Odds? Very slim mainly due to each player having to pick up the playbook quickly. Daniel Jones is another QB being speculated upon. If the Colts traded him now they would take on a 35.2M dead money cap hit in 2027 but save 11.6M. Jones has completed 60.4% of his passes for 1,542 yards with 5 TDs and 9 INTs while rushing 25 times for 75 yards. He has 4 fumbles and lost 3. They have Anothny Richardson and Sam Ehlinger as the other QBs on the roster so they might take back a QB.…

title: What activating Mack Hollins means for the Patriots
summary: The writing was on the wall, and on Saturday the New England Patriots made it official. Mack Hollins has returned to the team’s 53-man roster after spending the previous four weeks on its injured reserve list; the veteran wide receiver was sent there after sustaining a calf injury in Week 4 versus the Buffalo Bills. […]
full_text: The writing was on the wall, and on Saturday the New England Patriots made it official. Mack Hollins has returned to the team’s 53-man roster after spending the previous four weeks on its injured reserve list; the veteran wide receiver was sent there after sustaining a calf injury in Week 4 versus the Buffalo Bills. Let’s assess what Hollins’ activation means for the Patriots ahead of their Week 9 contest versus the Green Bay Packers. Better depth Despite returning to practice earlier this week to open his 21-day window to return from injured reserve, Hollins initially remained on the list. While this is standard procedure — teams want to take a look at players at practice first before making any decisions regarding activation — it did leave the Patriots potentially three top-level wide receivers short heading into the weekend. Romeo Doubs remains on IR with a shoulder injury, while A.J. Brown was ruled out for a second straight game due to a knee issue. Had Hollins missed Sunday’s game as well, Drake Maye’s supporting cast would again have looked suspect, particularly considering running back TreVeyon Henderson’s medical status and tight end Hunter Henry being questionable for the contest as well. Hollins cannot patch all of those holes by himself, but having him available does upgrade New England’s overall defensive depth. Roster shakeup With Hollins back on the 53-man team, the Patriots now have five wide receivers rostered . In addition, their practice squad features three wideouts — one of whom, Ryan Miller, was elevated to the game day roster against the Miami Dolphins last week. 53-man roster (5): A.J. Brown (1), Mack Hollins (13), DeMario Douglas (3), Kyle Williams (18 | KR), Efton Chism III (86) Practice squad: Kyle Dixon (83), Chandler Brayboy (81), Ryan Miller (11) Injured reserve: Romeo Doubs (87) On paper, the Patriots are nearing full strength at the position again. That is particularly true given that Doubs will be eligible to come off IR himself after New England’s trip to Germany next week. The expectation is that he too will rejoin the active roster sooner rather than later, giving the club a full complement of wideouts again. That said, A.J. Brown’s status remains a question mark. While the team is optimistic that he will return before the end of the month, his participation in the upcoming international game against the Detroit Lions is uncertain. Trickle-down effect After Hollins exited the game against the Bills, one player in particular took on a bigger role: second-year man Efton Chism. A fringe game-day contributor since joining the team as a rookie free agent in 2025, Chism was on the field for 72.4% of offensive snaps during Hollins’ four-game absence. He caught 11 passes for 110 yards along the way (after already hauling in two passes, including the game-winning touchdown, down the stretch in Buffalo). While Chism’s production was solid, it would not be a surprise to see Hollins’ return seriously eat into his playing time share. More than any other player, he might feel the trickle-down effect of the activation. Leadership impact Hollins has been a solid contributor on the field so far this season, playing 63% of offensive snaps and catching 15 passes for 209 yards before going to injured reserve. However, his impact goes beyond his statistics: he is a well-respected voice in the locker room and tone-setter both on and off the field, in the pass and the run game. Getting him back especially under the current circumstances, is a positive development for New England beyond just his projected role and abilities as a pass catcher. Full roster The Patriots entered the weekend with 52 players on their active roster, meaning that activating Hollins now put the team at a full 53 again. This also means that a follow-up will be necessary in case any other additions are planned, either ahead of the upcoming NFL trade deadline or if fellow IR-return candidate Greg Van Roten — whose 21-day window also opened this week — will be ready to rejoin the active team.

title: Sunday Patriots Notes: Christian Elliss continues to impress
summary: It’s a busy time in New England as the Patriots enshrined Rob Gronkowski in the team’s Hall of Fame Saturday and will honor the 2016 Patriots team during halftime of Sunday’s game against the Packers. It has then been a busy week here on Pats Pulpit covering it all. So for anything that fell through […]
full_text: It’s a busy time in New England as the Patriots enshrined Rob Gronkowski in the team’s Hall of Fame Saturday and will honor the 2016 Patriots team during halftime of Sunday’s game against the Packers. It has then been a busy week here on Pats Pulpit covering it all. So for anything that fell through the cracks, let’s clean out the notebook from the week. Welcome to the latest edition of our Sunday Patriots Notes. Elliss attention As defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr takes the podium in front of the media every Thursday afternoon, the routine is usually typical. Questions fly about the previous game or upcoming opponent. Schematic talk is usually brushed to the side. Questions about players usually revolve around blue chip talents like Christian Gonzalez or Milton Williams. But Kuhr feels like one player in that group doesn’t get enough attention. “You didn’t mention Christian Elliss,” he said. An undrafted free agent out of Idaho in 2021, Elliss began his career as a special teams player. That remained his role when he first joined the Patriots as a waiver claim late in the 2023 season, logging zero defensive snaps over the final four games. Sticking in New England, Elliss went on to earn a consistent defensive role in 2024. His playing time has increased in each of the last three seasons, culminating in a full-time starting role this year. He has played 97% of the Patriots’ defensive snaps in 2026 while starting 21 of their last 23 games. “I think his consistency, and with him, I’d say even last year, starting off the first game, he’d admit to you, it was probably one of his worst games he’s played,” Kuhr said. “But his consistency has been his consistent improvement, and whether that be learning multiple roles now, being multiple packages, and yeah, I think he’s just a great example to those younger guys.” The production has followed. The hard hitting Elliss has made an impact in every aspect on defense, recording 60 tackles, 1.5 sacks, four tackles for loss, six quarterback hits, a pass breakup and a forced fumble this season. His 11 pressures and 26 run stops are already career highs. His play reached another level during the second half of last season, and that momentum has carried into 2026. Elliss credits a change in mindset for that development. “I’m going to play free. I’m going to play with joy. That’s the mentality I finally came to the conclusion of I need to have,” he said last season. “I was slower in my play because I’m trying to make everything perfect. [Now], I’ve just kind of been like, screw that. I don’t need it perfect. I’d rather have it be fast, physical, and, if I make a mistake, I’ll do that going 100%.” After signing a two-year, $13.5 million contract extension with the Patriots in 2025, Elliss is set to become a free agent following the season. Given his role and his production this year, he has made a strong case to be a priority for another extension in New England. Gronk jersey Rob Gronkowski received his red jacket on Saturday as he was inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame. Gronkowski and the 2016 Patriots will then be honored during Sunday’s game to celebrate the 10-year anniversary of Super Bowl LI. Drake Maye shared this week that he owned a Gronk jersey as a kid and was looking forward to reconnecting with the former tight end this weekend. The two have crossed paths a handful of times since Maye arrived in New England, with their first meeting coming at the 2024 Pro Bowl. Security blanket Maye has developed a strong connection with his own tight end during his Patriots career as Hunter Henry has climbed up the franchise ranks at the position. With Henry (foot) questionable for Sunday, it could mark Maye’s first full game he’s played as a Patriot without the veteran at his side. “I think he’s been someone for me that I can count on since my first snap in there my rookie year. He’s been a security blanket and a great guy in the huddle,” Maye said. Going long Sunday’s game will be one for fans of the deep ball. Packers quarterback Jordan Love and Drake Maye are tied for the league lead in deep completions with 17 apiece. Love ranks first in deep passing yards (591), while Maye is second (586). Maye, meanwhile, leads the league in big-time throws targeting the deep area of the field (15), with Love ranking second (12). Vrabel said the deep passing game starts with wide receivers who can get downfield and an offensive line that can hold up in protection. From there, it’s up to the quarterback to deliver. “Certainly, touch is involved, right? If you have to drive the ball, and arm strength,” Vrabel said. “But I think probably just having a good feel of, ‘Do I need a 35-yard pass that’s in the air, or do I need a 50-yard ball?’ and being able to judge that differently.” Love insight Patriots outside linebackers coach Mike Smith was on Green Bay’s defensive staff when the Packers selected Jordan Love in the first-round of the 2020 NFL Draft. Smith noted how Love was a quiet rookie — a “pretty smart” move as he soaked up knowledge behind Aaron Rodgers. Both Smith and Kuhr noted you see some resemblance of Rodgers in Love’s game now as he has developed into one of the league’s top quarterbacks. Special player “He’s a really special player when he’s at a full speed coming at you — at defenders. He’s tough to guard, tough to handle. He’s got great releases and just try to give him a chance to give him a ball to go catch,” said Drake Maye about wide receiver Kyle Williams. Assistant head coach Patriots players and coaches have enjoyed having Terrell Williams back in the building and on the sideline during game days this season. Kuhr called Williams a positive influence on his psyche as he instills confidence in the coordinator, while the assistant head coach’s impact has reached all levels of the team. “He touches all the players on both sides of the ball to get a feel for them and help them grow,” Kuhr said. “And especially with these rookies, what they have to go through, he’s just a great sounding board, great resource, advice, helps with the game-planning, but also does a good job of saying, like, ‘This is your show.’ ” Touchbacks The Patriots are one of the top special teams units in football when it comes to limiting touchbacks. On the year, just 7.7% of their kickoffs result in touchbacks while they’re 0.4 touchbacks per game ranks fourth best in the league. Head coach Mike Vrabel credited kicker Andy Borregales for his work in that aspect, while coordinator Jeremy Springer highlighted the need to cover kicks with the new rules. “You got to be able to cover kicks in the NFL. That’s the way it is now,” Springer said. “I don’t want them to start to drive at the 35 yard line. Every time you hit touchbacks, it’s the 35 yard line. “So, if we can get them inside the 30, inside the 25, or get a penalty, now they’re on the 15, the 10, those are the hidden yards throughout the game that are going to help you win football games. The last thing you want to do is kick touchbacks.” Week ahead The Patriots will change up the schedule this week with Sunday’s game against the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany. This means Mike Vrabel media availability on Monday and an off-day on Tuesday will be regularly scheduled, before the team holds a normal Wednesday before departing to Germany that night. That’s where they will practice on Thursday and Friday before kickoff on Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET.

title: 6 moments that defined Rob Gronkowski’s Patriots career
summary: Rob Gronkowski is a New England Patriots Hall of Famer, and it is not hard to see why. Not only was he an integral part of the organization’s Dynasty 2.0 in the 2010s, he also performed at the highest level throughout his nine seasons with the team. When he left the Patriots after the 2018 […]
full_text: Rob Gronkowski is a New England Patriots Hall of Famer , and it is not hard to see why. Not only was he an integral part of the organization’s Dynasty 2.0 in the 2010s, he also performed at the highest level throughout his nine seasons with the team. When he left the Patriots after the 2018 season — one capped by his third championship — he did so as the owner of 15 NFL records . While some of those have been broken over the last seven years, his impact on the Patriots and the NFL as a whole is undeniable. Breaking it down to a handful of moments is therefore a challenging task. This collection is therefore more of a “greatest hits” than a comprehensive journey through his oeuvre. No. 1: Draft-day shenanigans 15 years ago we drafted @RobGronkowski … and his reaction was PRICELESS 😂 pic.twitter.com/J8UHC3sdHm — New England Patriots (@Patriots) April 23, 2025 Despite questions about a back injury and even though he fell asleep during his pre-draft visit to Gillette Stadium, the Patriots forced their luck in the second round of the 2010 NFL Draft. Trading up two spots to leap-frog the Baltimore Ravens, they secured Gronkowski with the 42nd overall selection. That moment, which saw him celebrate on stage with his entire immediate family, already set the tone for what was about to come. No. 2: Raw power pic.twitter.com/WosAyRGnb4 — VIDEO (@pahrduve) November 6, 2026 Coming off a solid rookie season, Gronkowski fully broke out in Year 2 to establish himself as the best tight end in the NFL and a player with sky-high potential. There were multiple plays during his impressive 2011 campaign that can be picked as examples, but one stands out above the rest: a 49-yard catch-and-run against Washington that showed his rare blend of speed, power and elusiveness. It was one of the first times in his career that he showed that he was a different animal. No. 3: Runaway truck @RobGronkowski ’s brutal TD vs the Colts in 2014 will always be one of my favourites. Happy Retirement Gronk. #NFL pic.twitter.com/JbUu6rXowA — Lewis Allen (@lallen125) March 25, 2019 Even with Peyton Manning gone, Patriots vs. Colts was still one of the NFL’s best rivalries in the mid-2010s. And one particular matchup stands out in regards to Gronkowski: Week 11 of the 2014 season. He finished the game with a non-conspicuous stat-line of four catches, 71 yards and a touchdown. That score, however, was arguably the most spectacular one of his nine-year career: like a “runaway track,” as Al Michaels said on the broadcast, he ran over defenders on his way to turning a short third-down conversion into a 26-yard score. Of course, his performance that day was also remembered for something else. No. 4: Out of the club When Gronk threw Sergio Brown out of the club vs the Colts #NEPats pic.twitter.com/NdBXwzAEsw — Back Then Football (@BackThenFB) August 15, 2026 A true tight end, Gronkowski was a dual-impact player both due to his immense receiving prowess and his abilities as a blocker. His contributions in the second area oftentimes go undervalued, but they also define who he was as a player: a powerful and physical presence at the point of attack. Him blocking standout edge Terrell Suggs 1-on-1 in the 2011 AFC Championship Game is a prime example of that, and so is one of the most re-watched moments of his career, when he threw Colts safety Sergio Brown “out of the club” in 2014. No. 5: Immaculate connection A Random Dynasty Highlight: Brady to Gronk 40 yards on 4th down vs Broncos in 2015 AFC Conference Championship https://t.co/MVmmmJOIw4 #Patriots #Dynasty pic.twitter.com/ZuwpDibUbl — Patriots Dynasty (@PatsDynastyInfo) September 24, 2022 A large part of Gronkowski’s success as a Patriots was not just his physical superiority over his opponents, but also his ability to be on the same page as his quarterback; it is why Tom Brady made sure to recruit him to Tampa Bay to close out both players’ careers. The chemistry between the two was on constant display for nine years, but if we had to choose one moment as an example — despite the eventual unsatisfactory outcome — it would be the 2015 AFC Championship Game in Denver. Going against a generational defense, Gronkowski converted two massive fourth downs in the late fourth quarter. No. 6: Perfect send-off From one 🐐 to another. @RobGronkowski | #EverythingWeGot pic.twitter.com/9lCLlfxxBO — New England Patriots (@Patriots) February 4, 2019 Gronkowski’s Patriots story cannot be told without also mentioning the injuries he had to overcome, and his Super Bowl history reflects that. He was severely limited against the Giants in 2012 and unable to play against the Falcons in 2017; he also did have a profound impact on the game in his three other appearances, including, in Super Bowl LIII. That particular game put a perfect bow on his career with the team. Slowed by years of physical challenges, he still managed one last hurrah against the Rams: going up the seam as part of the New England’s famous Hoss-Y-Juke concept, he hauled in the biggest catch of the game — one that helped set up the only touchdown in the Patriots’ eventual 13-3 victory. It was Gronkowski’s final catch as a Patriot, and a worthy send-off. What additional moments do you think defined Gronkowski’s career with the Patriots? Please head down to the comment section to share your choices with the community.

A calf injury had sent Hollins to injured reserve a week into October. After missing the NFL minimum of four games, he saw his […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - OCTOBER 04: Mack Hollins #13 of the New England Patriots warms up before the game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images Mack Hollins will get the green light against the Green Bay Packers. The New England Patriots officially activated the veteran wide receiver on the eve of Sunday’s game at Gillette Stadium. A calf injury had sent Hollins to injured reserve a week into October. After missing the NFL minimum of four games, he saw his 21-day practice window open as the calendar turned to November. Three limited sessions and a questionable game designation followed. Hollins, 33, now returns as the eldest statesman on an active depth chart of four. With A.J. Brown ruled out for a second consecutive matchup due to a knee injury and Romeo Doubs still residing on injured reserve due to a shoulder injury , DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III will make up the rest of the wideout room for the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. At the time of his non-contact exit last month at Highmark Stadium, Hollins stood atop the offense with 20 targets, 15 catches and 209 yards through four appearances. The 6-foot-4, 221-pound North Carolina product finds himself 131 games, 56 starts, 223 catches, 2,828 yards and 17 touchdowns into a career that began with the Philadelphia Eagles in the fourth round of the 2017 NFL draft at No. 118 overall. A Super Bowl LII champion, Hollins made subsequent stops with the Miami Dolphins, Las Vegas Raiders, Atlanta Falcons and Buffalo Bills before arriving in Foxborough on a two-year deal in 2025. New England carried an open spot on the 53-man roster after releasing and retaining veteran cornerback Kindle Vildor on the practice squad ahead of the Green Bay visit. No standard elevations were made for Sunday afternoon. Tight end Hunter Henry, offensive tackle Morgan Moses, cornerback Carlton Davis III and safeties Kevin Byard III and Brenden Schooler move forward with questionable game statuses, while guard Greg Van Roten will remain on injured reserve after also having his practice window open at the start of the week.

title: Rob Gronkowski becomes 38th inductee into Patriots Hall of Fame
summary: Rob Gronkowski’s New England Patriots journey has reached its logical conclusion. Seven years after playing his last snap for the franchise, and four years after calling it a career, he was enshrined into the team’s Hall of Fame on Saturday afternoon. It was a worthy ceremony for one of the best and most recognizable players […]
full_text: Rob Gronkowski’s New England Patriots journey has reached its logical conclusion. Seven years after playing his last snap for the franchise, and four years after calling it a career, he was enshrined into the team’s Hall of Fame on Saturday afternoon. It was a worthy ceremony for one of the best and most recognizable players in Patriots, and NFL, history. From a star-studded group of attendees, including the likes of Tom Brady, Ty Law, Matthew Slater and current head coach Mike Vrabel, to a journey through his illustrious career in New England, it was a celebration of Gronkowski as a player and a person. Of course, it also was peak Gronk. Before he even started his speech, fellow Hall of Famer Matt Light gifted him a “Yo Soy Hall of Famer” shirt in reference to Gronkowski’s famous “Yo Soy Fiesta” quote from 2011. Then, once he was at the podium, Gronkowski gave a greatest hits compilation of anecdotes — and a reminder of what made him a unique player during the famously work-oriented Patriots dynasty. Welcome to the Patriots Hall of Fame @RobGronkowski ! pic.twitter.com/ER3D2SAvyh — New England Patriots (@Patriots) November 7, 2026 There was him congratulating longtime head coach Bill Belichick for “finally growing some balls” to select him in the second round of the NFL Draft. There was his perspective on the famous pre-draft visit that included him falling asleep at Gillette Stadium. There was a shoutout to his former and current Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels in the form of a, “You wish you still had me, buddy.” More than anything, though, there was a shared sense of appreciation of his nine years in Foxborough. “There’s one thing we all know: we know that Rob was larger than life as a talent and as a personality when he played the game,” said Patriots co-owner Jonathan Kraft. “He led with this really big heart. His play on the field was extraordinary, it was otherworldly. But it was his infectious energy and it was his consistent positive present that truly set him apart from anybody else that played here.” "I fell to the Patriots for a reason. I came to the Patriots for a cause. It's where I belonged. It's where I was meant to be." pic.twitter.com/S6mF6UhtKL — New England Patriots (@Patriots) November 7, 2026 Gronkowski himself summed up his Patriots experience as one going beyond his three Super Bowl rings, four All-Pro honors and an inclusion into the NFL’s 100th Anniversary Team. For him, being a Patriot meant. “being a part of something bigger than yourself.” “It means more than just playing football,” the self-proclaimed “Patriot for life” said in his speech. “It’s about doing what’s best for the team, being loyal, sacrificing, giving everything you have, leaving a legacy, giving back to the community, and most importantly: doing your job.”

title: 3-Point Stance: Patriots’ trade deadline isn’t time for a youth movement
summary: Are the New England Patriots sellers at the NFL trade deadline? Last week, Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer highlighted defensive tackle Christian Barmore and cornerback Carlton Davis as potential Patriots trade candidates ahead of the deadline on Tuesday, Nov. 10. According to Breer, if a deal is struck, New England’s motivation would be centered around adding […]
full_text: Are the New England Patriots sellers at the NFL trade deadline? Last week, Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer highlighted defensive tackle Christian Barmore and cornerback Carlton Davis as potential Patriots trade candidates ahead of the deadline on Tuesday, Nov. 10. According to Breer, if a deal is struck, New England’s motivation would be centered around adding draft capital and transitioning into a younger roster. Though based on his response when speaking with the media on Wednesday, head coach Mike Vrabel appears to disagree with that approach. “I think sometimes national reports have the tendency to do that. I have not shared that information with anybody,” Vrabel said. “This time of year, I think that all these things kind of get drummed up. So, we’re focused on trying to prepare for [the Green Bay Packers on Sunday] and make the corrections from [last week]. “This is business as normal here, so I don’t know where a lot of these things come from. Certainly not from any conversations with me.” Regardless of whether or not the Patriots strike a deal involving either player, trading almost any impact contributor on the roster while sitting at a 5-3 record at the regular season’s midway point is certainly questionable. At the least, a deal of that stature calls for a corresponding “buying” move. Sure, New England’s depth in multiple areas will be a largely discussed topic throughout the offseason regarding the team’s roster-building process. And rightfully so. Vrabel said it himself after a preseason victory over the Philadelphia Eagles, stating at the time that he doesn’t think his team is “very deep.” But sending away either Barmore or Davis simply doesn’t make sense at this time. Especially for a franchise still in contention for the AFC East title. Trading Barmore creates another need In 2023, Barmore posted his best season as a pro, recording 8.5 sacks, 16 quarterback hits and pressuring those passers 49 times. He also consistently disrupted opposing run offenses, forcing 13 tackles for a loss and totaling 64 combined takedowns. That season-long performance earned the Patriots’ 2021 second-round draft selection a four-year, $84 million contract extension the following offseason. Currently in year two of that new deal, Barmore’s production hasn’t entirely matched the monetary value of his contract, especially in run defense. From just last season, the 27-year-old has seen his involvement in that facet of the defense drop from 62.8% to just 36%. Still, New England evidently continues to view Barmore as a producer when rushing the quarterback, heavily using the defensive tackle during pass-rush downs and critical third-down plays. Barmore’s overall reduced role also doesn’t mean he’s expendable. Trading him shuffles the defensive line, forcing Cory Durden into a new, pass-rush-heavy role and 34-year-old DaQuan Jones, who has contributed as a relief piece for the primary starters, into a heavier workload. Davis’ departure would leave a hole in the secondary As for Davis, the cornerback hasn’t shown signs of regression. But the soon-to-be 30-year-old, entering the final year of his contract with a mighty injury history and owed $22 million in 2027, plays directly into the youth-movement argument. Nonetheless, shipping him off to another franchise creates a glaring hole in the cornerback room. That decision then forces Vrabel and the defensive coaching staff to decide between starting substitute Charles Woods opposite Christian Gonzalez or pulling Marcus Jones away from his natural nickel-cornerback position. With several offenses in the Patriots’ remaining schedule currently ranking top 10 in passing yards per game, that potential decision seems counterproductive. Davis, who recently returned to the starting lineup last week after missing four games, played a significant role in New England’s divisional round victory against the Houston Texans in the playoffs last season, intercepting C.J. Stroud twice. The offseason offers a better time to make a move It’s true that the Patriots’ defense has struggled to deliver on the expectations surrounding their offseason additions of Dre’Mont Jones, All-Pro safety Kevin Byard and second-round pick Gabe Jacas. But much like the rest of the roster, that group has dealt with injuries. Last week’s matchup against the Miami Dolphins marked the first game the starting cornerback trio of Gonzalez, Davis and Jones all played together since Week Three. While the healthy defense didn’t put together a flawless performance, the unit signaled improvement, sacking Malik Willis on five occasions, logging an interception and forcing the Miami offense into four three-and-out possessions. Teams can afford slow starts, and while there’s no guarantee New England will find its stride later in the season, the ability to play its best football down the stretch is what ultimately matters the most. In Barmore’s case, as the Boston Herald’s Andrew Callahan put it , the Patriots seemingly want “out of the Barmore business.” An offseason deal, rather than a midseason trade, allows New England greater flexibility to reallocate resources and explore replacements to replicate or improve upon Barmore’s production while spending less. Even though eventually moving Barmore or another established contributor makes sense for the team’s long-term roster construction, the Patriots’ timing of a potential trade should account for the franchise’s current position in the AFC playoff picture.

Through his four-year career, Miller has logged 656 rushing yards and 5 touchdowns while adding another 217 yards as a receiver. The former third-round draft pick is also the team’s current leading rusher, logging 159 rushing yards this season. The Saints picked up running back Audric Estime off waivers heading into the bye, and it appears he will have a major role in the team’s game plan on Sunday against the Cleveland Browns. Miller’s release also signifies a potential return for veteran running back Travis Etienne. The decision to move on from Miller mid-season is shocking, but the writing has been on the wall. Despite his very obvious talent, the former TCU running back has struggled to stay healthy and has made plenty of mistakes throughout the 2026 season. There’s always the chance New Orleans looks to bring Miller back to the roster or through the practice squad, but with his talent, it’s unlikely he doesn’t find his way on to another team’s roster.

title: Saints Hall of Fame Honors Mark Ingram, Terron Armstead and Sal La Rock
summary: On Friday, November 6, 2026, former New Orleans Saints left tackle Terron Armstead and running back Mark Ingram were inducted into the Saints Hall of Fame during a luncheon held at Chateau Country Club in Kenner. Sal La Rock, the Superdome’s press box security supervisor, received the Joe Gemelli “Fleur de Lis” Award, which recognizes […]
full_text: On Friday, November 6, 2026, former New Orleans Saints left tackle Terron Armstead and running back Mark Ingram were inducted into the Saints Hall of Fame during a luncheon held at Chateau Country Club in Kenner. Sal La Rock, the Superdome’s press box security supervisor, received the Joe Gemelli “Fleur de Lis” Award, which recognizes individuals who have made significant contributions to the New Orleans Saints organization through their dedication, service and commitment to the franchise. Ingram was selected by the New Orleans Saints in the first round (28th overall) of the 2011 NFL Draft. Over 10 seasons in New Orleans (2011–2018 and 2021–2022), Ingram cemented his place in franchise history, becoming the Saints’ all-time leading rusher in 2021. However, his record was surpassed by Alvin Kamara just three years later. A three-time Pro Bowl selection, including two appearances as a Saint, Ingram retired following the 2022 season and currently serves as a college football analyst for FOX Sports. Due to his commitments with FOX Sports, Ingram was unable to attend the luncheon but will be in attendance at tonight’s gala and tomorrow’s game. In a prerecorded message, Ingram expressed his gratitude to his family, former teammates, the Saints organization and the fans for their unwavering support, encouragement and love throughout his career, fittingly closing his message with an enthusiastic “WHO DAT!” Armstead was selected by the Saints in the third round (75th overall) of the 2013 NFL Draft out of Arkansas-Pine Bluff. Over nine seasons in New Orleans (2013–2021), he established himself as one of the NFL’s premier offensive tackles and a cornerstone of the Saints’ offensive line. Armstead earned three consecutive Pro Bowl selections (2018–2020) and Associated Press second-team All-Pro honors in 2018. He played a key role in protecting quarterback Drew Brees and helping anchor one of the league’s most productive offenses during his tenure with the franchise. During his acceptance speech, Armstead expressed his gratitude to his family, who were in attendance, as well as Saints owner Gayle Benson, who was also present, and the entire Saints organization for their support throughout his career. He also shared that his only regret from his playing days was that he and his teammates were unable to bring another Super Bowl championship to the city of New Orleans. Sal La Rock has been a valued member of the Caesars Superdome staff since 1998, beginning his career in event services for public safety before being promoted to Press Box Supervisor just two years later. For nearly three decades, affectionately known as “Mr. Sal,” he has been a familiar face and a warm, welcoming presence for media members covering Saints games. His kindness, dedication and genuine hospitality have made him a beloved fixture in the press box, and game days at the Superdome simply wouldn’t be the same without him. All three honorees will be recognized by the Saints Hall of Fame during halftime of tomorrow’s game against the Cleveland Browns.
author: Tina Howell

title: Saints vs. Browns: Key Matchups
summary: The New Orleans Saints are attempting to get back in the win column and step up in a weak NFC South with a win over the Cleveland Browns on Sunday. But it won’t be easy. The Browns are 5-3 on the season and have found ways to win the tough ones. If New Orleans comes […]
full_text: The New Orleans Saints are attempting to get back in the win column and step up in a weak NFC South with a win over the Cleveland Browns on Sunday. But it won’t be easy. The Browns are 5-3 on the season and have found ways to win the tough ones. If New Orleans comes out with a win, it will be due to taking advantage of these key matchups. Saints RBs vs. Browns run defense The Saints are coming off one of the worst rushing performances of all time. They rushed the ball 17 times against the Pittsburgh Steelers for a total of 18 yards. In the loss, Saints running backs ran 14 times for 11 yards, averaging 0.8 yards per carry. Fortunately for the Saints, they’ll be facing a Browns defense that has struggled against the run. Over the last two weeks, Cleveland is allowing an average of 170.5 rushing yards and three touchdowns per game. Although unlikely, reinforcements may be on the way for the Saints, with left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. returning to practice. The run game is the biggest problem in New Orleans, and frankly, Kellen Moore’s career depends on correcting it. With a favorable matchup, the Saints should find success. Saints pass rush vs. QB Shedeur Sanders Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has been placed in the concussion protocol and is unlikely to play. With it becoming more probable that second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders will be starting, the Saints defense has a favorable matchup. Chase Young has been dominant to start the season, and despite an early bye, he remains top three in sacks. Alongside Young is Carl Granderson, who has logged 5.5 sacks himself. The Saints have been one of the better pass-rushing teams in the league in terms of sacks, and their standout tandem is looking to have a big game against a young, inexperienced quarterback. WR Jordyn Tyson vs. the Browns secondary Sunday will be a big game for the Saints. They are returning from the bye to a home crowd, still within a game’s reach of the top of the NFC South. Despite all the implications, the biggest headline for New Orleans against the Browns will be the return of eighth-overall pick Jordyn Tyson. Tyson will likely see his first NFL action on Sunday, and the Saints will be looking to get him started early. Tyson offers the catch-and-run ability the New Orleans offense has been missing, and he could be an immediate game changer. But if I know the Saints want to get Tyson the ball early, you could bet Cleveland knows it too. Getting Tyson back is big for the Saints, and he could be the difference in a win or a loss, but the Browns will zone in on the momentum New Orleans will be looking to gain out of the bye, and it starts with the rookie.

title: New Orleans Saints News: Should the Saints buy or sell at the trade deadline?

title: 3 ‘things I think’ before Giants-Eagles: Critical 5-day stretch has arrived
summary: The division-leading New York Giants begin a season-defining five-day stretch on Sunday when they face the Philadelphia Eagles. NFC East games against the Eagles and Washington Commanders book-ending that stretch, with an intriguing NFL trade deadline sandwiched in the middle. After the Giants defeated the Houston Texans in overtime in Week 7, head coach John […]
full_text: Devin Singletary | Getty Images The division-leading New York Giants begin a season-defining five-day stretch on Sunday when they face the Philadelphia Eagles. NFC East games against the Eagles and Washington Commanders book-ending that stretch, with an intriguing NFL trade deadline sandwiched in the middle. After the Giants defeated the Houston Texans in overtime in Week 7, head coach John Harbaugh said these post-bye division contests would be “The two most important games of the season” because they “will set the direction for the rest of the season.” NFC East standings Giants 4-2-1 Dallas Cowboys 3-5 Commanders 2-4-1 Eagles 2-6 Two victories in the next five days would get the Giants to 6-2-1, and build the Giants a cushion they might need with the schedule getting tougher over the season’s last eight weeks. It is a fair criticism of the Giants that they have played only one team thus far with a .500 record, and were blown out by the Los Angeles Rams in that game. Over their last eight games, the Giants face the Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2), San Francisco 49ers (6-1), Seattle Seahawks (4-4), Cleveland Browns (5-3), and Detroit Lions (5-2), along with the Cowboys, Eagles, and Indianapolis Colts. Strip away all the chatter about the Giants’ losing streak in Philadelphia, Joe Milton making his first career start at quarterback for the Eagles, Cam Skattebo’s availability, and everything else and the truth is this is a game the Giants should win. They are the better team, and they have much more to play for. “It’s just a really important game for our team,” Harbaugh said. “Division game, man. Division game. We’re trying to win the division first. That’s our first goal here. This game will go a long way toward that. That’s why it’s so important. Division games are big. Division games on the road are really big. Those are big wins if you can get them. They’re tough to get. It’s a big challenge. We’re excited about the opportunity, but we understand it’s a daunting challenge.” If the Commanders can defeat the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, it is possible Washington emerges as the biggest threat to the Giants in the division. A split of the Eagles and Commanders games wouldn’t be devastating, but it would make the path to the playoffs more treacherous for the Giants. Losing both games would bring serious questions regarding whether the Giants are actually ready to capitalize on the opportunity they have. In-between, of course, is the trade deadline. Will the Giants get Jonathan Taylor? A lesser back to supplement what they have? Help at defensive tackle? How much will they be willing to give up to get any of that? Buckle up, Giants fans. It is going to be a fascinating five days. Devin Singletary … then what? If Cam Skattebo is out due to his hamstring injury, as seems likely, the Giants know they will get a solid professional effort from Devin Singletary. What they will get from Gregory Desrosiers in his NFL debut or practice squad elevation Phil Mafah, with one game of NFL experience, is anybody’s guess. If you’re the Giants, all you can do is cross your fingers and hope the game doesn’t turn on a mistake by one of the new, young running backs. Return game questions It is never good when your primary kickoff and punt returner shows up on the injury report with a hand injury. That is what happened to Charlie Jones of the Giants this week. When and how the injury occurred I don’t know, but it was clear throughout the week that it was a concern. On Thursday, Jones was practicing with a wrap on his hand. He is listed as questionable. “He’s managing it,” Harbaugh said. “He was out today catching and everything like that. Just want to make sure he could catch. I haven’t talked to him yet. We’ll see how he felt.” Starting safety Jevon Holland could return punts if Jones can’t. “Not ideal. If we have to do it, we will. But not ideal,” Harbaugh said. Jones and Tyrone Tracy have been the kickoff returners. Tracy is now on IR with a hamstring injury. Who’s next on the depth chart? Good question. Deonte Banks is an outstanding kickoff returner, but he is also the Giants’ best cornerback. Desrosiers returned some kickoffs in college. Jalin Hyatt, just signed to the 53-man roster on Saturday, could be used on kickoff returns. There aren’t a lot of other options.

title: NY Giants add former third-round pick to 53-man roster
summary: The New York Giants on Saturday signed wide receiver Jalin Hyatt off their practice squad to the 53-man roster, filling the spot vacated when they released quarterback Jake Haener earlier in the week. The Giants traded up in the 2023 NFL Draft to select Hyatt in the third round, and he has had a disappointing […]
full_text: Jalin Hyatt | Getty Images The New York Giants on Saturday signed wide receiver Jalin Hyatt off their practice squad to the 53-man roster, filling the spot vacated when they released quarterback Jake Haener earlier in the week. The Giants traded up in the 2023 NFL Draft to select Hyatt in the third round, and he has had a disappointing career to this point. In three seasons, Hyatt has caught only 36 passes. Over the past two seasons, that total is just 13. New head coach John Harbaugh gave Hyatt an opportunity, however, similar to the one he gave to Deonte Banks and other previously disappointing Giants draft picks. Hyatt, despite an injury that cost him time during training camp, was impressive enough in the summer to earn a spot on the practice squad. Hyatt has played in just one game for the Giants this season, and has no catches. With wide receiver/kick returner Charlie Jones ailing with a hand injury, Hyatt provides depth at receiver and could fill in as a kickoff returner. Hyatt averaged 27.8 yards on four kickoff returns last season. With Hyatt moving to the 53-man roster, the Giants re-signed Haener to their practice squad. Practice squad elevations The Giants elevated two players from their practice squad for Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles — running back Phil Mafah and defensive end Dawuane Smoot . With Tyrone Tracy on IR and Cam Skattebo doubtful with a hamstring injury, the Giants have only Devin Singletary and Gregory Desrosiers as healthy backs on their active roster. Mafah, 6-foot-1, 232 pounds, was a seventh-round selection by the Dallas Cowboys in the 2025 NFL Draft. He played in just one game, getting five carries for 18 yards and a touchdown. Mafah signed to the practice squad in mid-September after being waived by Dallas. Smoot, 31, is in his 10th NFL season. The 6-foot-3, 264-pound 31-year-old was signed to the practice squad in mid-October.

title: NFL betting advice: Giants-Eagles picks and props
summary: Welcome to the New York Giants betting angle, Week 9 edition! Each week, I’m giving you my three favorite wagers for that week’s New York Giants game. My one rule: I won’t ever give you wagers that go beyond -120. No gimmes! The Giants are coming off their Bye week and heading into what has been a […]
full_text: Next Man Up! | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to the New York Giants betting angle, Week 9 edition! Each week, I’m giving you my three favorite wagers for that week’s New York Giants game. My one rule: I won’t ever give you wagers that go beyond -120. No gimmes! The Giants are coming off their Bye week and heading into what has been a personal house of horrors. Big Blue hasn’t won a game in Philadelphia since 2013, but for the first time since 2009, they’re favored at the Linc. That tells you a lot about how this season has gone for Philadelphia, losers of six straight. The first NY-PHI game of this season looks a lot different than it did when the schedule came out. The starting quarterbacks for this game aren’t Jaxson Dart and Jalen Hurts. Oh, no. They’re not even Jameis Winston and Tanner McKee, who opened the season as the respective backups. No, the starters in Week 9 for these NFC East rivals are J.J. McCarthy and Joe Milton III, each of whom wasn’t even on his current team a few short weeks ago. McCarthy has played just five quarters on the Giants and Milton has yet to take a snap for the Eagles. He’s also making the first start of his NFL career after appearing in five games across two seasons. On top of that, there are injury concerns with both starting running backs. Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is listed as doubtful and Saquon Barkley continues to battle through hamstring and back soreness. He’ll play, but how much? What does this all mean? It means I’m flying a little blind this week with my bets. Be careful out there. My picks were 1-2 in Week 7 and I’m 12-9 on the season. I’m looking to get back in the win column this week. Let’s get to this week’s picks. All lines and odds are from Fanduel and are as of Saturday, November 7. The line for the game is Giants -3, with a total of 38.5. Game Total OVER 38.5 (-115). This game scares me and while I think the Giants will win, I don’t want to lay the points or take the moneyline, given all the bad history of their visits to this building. I do like the over, even though Philly’s offense has been atrocious and hasn’t topped 13 points in three straight. Milton and more Barkley should give them a spark. Philly’s defense has a lot of talent and might give McCarthy some problems, but New York has been scoring and should put up points. This is also a make-or-break game for the Eagles’ chances to stay in the race in a weak NFC East, and I think they’ll compete. Weather won’t be a factor. This game offers the lowest total on the board this week — grab the over. Devin Singletary OVER 55.5 rushing yards (-114). This is a volume play, and my favorite prop on the board for the entire slate. The Giants are going to want to run the ball, and with Tyrone Tracy, Jr. on IR and Cam Skattebo doubtful, Singletary should get a major workload. They don’t have any other backs on the roster with a rushing attempt this season. The Eagles are allowing 131 rushing yards per game which is the fifth-most in the NFL. A lot of that is game script, but this is a favorable matchup regardless. Singletary is competent enough to hit this prop by the end of the third quarter at the latest. Joe Milton III UNDER 189.5 passing yards (-114). Saquon Barkley played just 19 snaps each of the last two weeks while dealing with injuries. I’m guessing he’ll get a bigger workload this week, to help take pressure off Milton in his first start. DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are out for the third straight game, so Philadelphia is once again going to need to rely on tight end Dallas Goedert plus a bunch of unproven and inexperienced pass catchers. Milton has a big arm but struggles with accuracy, and the Giants’ pass defense has been playing really well. They held C.J. Stroud to just 153 yards in a game that went to overtime in Week 7. Tyler Shough only threw for 144 yards against them the week before. Take the under. Those are the picks for Week 9. Good luck with your wagers! And if you play fantasy football, be sure to check out my Week 9 fantasy preview, with start/sit advice and more, right here .

title: Giants-Eagles ‘5 questions’: Even Bleeding Green Nation has given up
summary: The New York Giants are visiting Lincoln Financial Field, their own personal house of horrors, this Sunday when they face the Philadelphia Eagles. Things are upside-down in the NFC East, though, with the Giants on top and the wounded Eagles at the bottom. Let’s discuss that in our ‘5 questions’ segment with Brandon Lee Gowton […]
full_text: NIck Sirianni (left) and Howie Roseman. | Getty Images The New York Giants are visiting Lincoln Financial Field, their own personal house of horrors, this Sunday when they face the Philadelphia Eagles. Things are upside-down in the NFC East, though, with the Giants on top and the wounded Eagles at the bottom. Let’s discuss that in our ‘5 questions’ segment with Brandon Lee Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation. Ed: How are Eagles fans processing what has happened to the team this year? It has been a shocking fall. Is there any light at the end of the tunnel? BLG: Back in the offseason, I talked about feeling less optimistic about the Eagles’ short-term outlook than their long-term outlook. Stand by what I said back in April. Optimistic about the Eagles in the long-term, less so in the short-term: pic.twitter.com/58vNJfo9M5 — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) October 12, 2026 There’s no denying that this season is a stinker. The Eagles are arguably the worst team in the NFL. There isn’t just one reason why that’s the case. When you’re this bad, it truly takes a team effort. The offense is bad and injured. New offensive coordinator Sean Mannion and new offensive line coach Chris Kuper (who replaced legendary two-time Super Bowl champion Jeff Stoutland) seem to be in over their heads. Nick Sirianni has no answers to help them. Jalen Hurts was a big reason why the Eagles won their first two games but he didn’t play as well after that and is now out for the season. Vic Fangio’s defense has way underperformed expectations. The veteran defensive coordinator is not having a good season. The Eagles paid big money to homegrown interior defensive linemen Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis … in addition to veteran edge rusher Jonathan Greenard … but the defensive line is getting pushed around. Howie Roseman didn’t have a very good offseason. You can’t point to many moves that are currently helping the team. (The A.J. Brown trade is looking pretty good, though. But the first-round pick they got for him doesn’t arrive until 2028.) Despite the current struggles, there is reason to be optimistic about this team’s future. Things previously looked bleak for the Eagles after they fired their head coach in 2012, 2015, and 2020. But Jeffrey Lurie and Roseman quickly righted the ship after each of those debacles. This isn’t to suggest that there’s a guarantee that the Eagles will get back on track as soon as next season. But there’s reason to give that duo some benefit of the doubt. I certainly won’t be surprised if they use this bad season to reset the franchise and focus on building a new championship contender. The Eagles probably won’t stay bad for very long. And even if they do … we’ve been able to witness two Super Bowl wins within the past nine years. It could be way worse! Ed: What are your thoughts on the Jalen Hurts situation? In my view, it is a really bad look for the Eagles. Does it look and feel as bad from where you sit? BLG: It certainly doesn’t look or feel great. And I know some people around him were not happy with how the situation was handled. Understandably so. Without knowing all the details, it’s difficult to speak definitively on the matter. I’ll just say that I hope the team truly did operate with Hurts’ health and safety in mind and this was just an unfortunate scenario. I also hope Hurts is getting better and can be cleared to play football again in the future. For many reasons, his standing with the team moving forward isn’t clear. But there’s plenty of time to figure that out down the road. Ed: If you could take one player off the Giants’ roster and put him in Philadelphia’s lineup, who would it be? Why? BLG: ’m not super interested in trying to salvage this season, which already seems lost. So, I’m not thinking about a short-term, win-now addition. Malik Nabers is tempting; he’s been good and the Eagles could use another stud receiver with Makai Lemon’s outlook uncertain. I’m interested in fortifying the Eagles’ offensive line with Lane Johnson retiring … maybe take Andrew Thomas and either move him or Jordan Mailata to right tackle? The Eagles could use help at tight end and I like Isaiah Likely. But he also got paid a lot of money. I’ve been hearing good things about Arvell Reese, though I haven’t had a ton of time to key in on him yet. But I’m ultimately going to go with Philly native Abdul Carter. I noticed he ranks top 20 in pressures generated. He seems to be having a better season than his sack numbers would indicate. The Eagles need edge rusher help in long term and it would be fun to have him return home to help his favorite NFL team. The Giants’ first-round pick. pic.twitter.com/31Tris2MVo — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) April 25, 2025 Ed: How would you expect Howie Roseman to react to this? A seller in the short-term? What about the long-term? BLG: It seems like a no-brainer for Roseman to sell players who won’t be around next season. The likes of Riq Woolen (one-year contract), Hollywood Brown (one-year contract), and Moro Ojomo (playing on last year of his deal and the Eagles already paid Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis) should pretty much be gone for whatever the Eagles can fetch for them. The Eagles should be willing to take offers for more premium players, such as Saquon Barkley. It’s already been reported that they’re NOT going to deal him. And my guess is that report came to light because Roseman already sensed the market for him isn’t as lucrative as it would take for the Eagles to move him. That’s fine. But, again, they should be willing to sell almost every player on their roster as long as the price is right. Just like it was in the case of the Cam Jurgens trade. Absolutely no one in Philly thought the Eagles could get a second-round pick for a player who really struggled last season and wasn’t off to a great start this year. If there’s great value to be had, Roseman should take it. I doubt Roseman is of the mind the Eagles need to be in a multi-year rebuild. He’s built contenders in much shorter time-frames. Ed: How weird is it for you to look at the betting line and see the Giants as FAVORITES at the Linc? What do the Giants have to do to win this game? What, if anything, makes you think the Eagles can pull an upset? (And, yes, that sounds weird to me, too) BLG: It’s certainly not hard to believe given the current state of the Eagles. But it is wild in the historical context that they haven’t been in this home underdog position since 2009. The Eagles have mostly owned the Giants for a long time now; they are 21-6 in 27 meetings against the G-Men since I started covering the Birds for BGN in 2013. What do the Giants have to do to win? Pretty much just show up. The Eagles’ offense is abysmal. Their defense has had some moments but they’re bad, too. It doesn’t seem like this team stands much of a chance. I refuse to believe otherwise until they actually give us something to think otherwise. I think John Harbaugh will have his team ready and fired up to get a win in Philly. The Giants should also be well-rested coming off a bye while the Eagles are banged up and coming off a Sunday night road game. Eagles 7, Giants 28.
author: Ed Valentine

title: College football 2026: Draft Prospects for the Giants in a monster Week 10
summary: Good Morning New York Giants fans! Happy Saturday and welcome to Week 10 of the 2026 College Football season! I’m not going to beat around the bush today: We’re being treated to an absolutely monstrous slate of games that features seven matchups between ranked opponents. I’m not sure I’ve ever seen one day with this […]
full_text: Miami defensive tackle Ahmad Moten Sr. celebrates a fumble recovery﻿ | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Good Morning New York Giants fans! Happy Saturday and welcome to Week 10 of the 2026 College Football season! I’m not going to beat around the bush today: We’re being treated to an absolutely monstrous slate of games that features seven matchups between ranked opponents. I’m not sure I’ve ever seen one day with this many “good against good” match-ups, and not only will today’s action have a profound effect on the upcoming Draft Process, it will also have a seismic impact on the College Football Playoffs. With that in mind, we’re going about things a bit differently today, and I’ll be spotlighting a player who could appeal to the Giants, or fit their needs as we currently perceive them, on each team in these games. So grab your snacks of choice, buckle in, and let’s get to it. (3) Utah vs. (9) BYU ABC – noon (3) Utah player to watch – Wayshawn Parker (RB) Parker has solid, but unspectacular, size for an NFL back at 5-foot-10, 205 pounds. He might not be a big back, but he’s a physical runner who has great vision and patience running downhill and true home run speed when he sees daylight. Parker has averaged over 6.5 yards per carry in each of the last two seasons and is also a dangerous pass catcher out of the backfield. (9) BYU player to watch – Faletu Satuala (S) The Giants were reportedly very interested in Ohio State safety Caleb Downs, and the “Ravens” style defense loves to use versatile box safeties as pivot players to help dictate terms to the offense. Satuala is has a massive frame for a safety at 6-foot-4, 215 pounds, but is a versatile and dynamic athlete. He was a basketball and lacrosse star in high school, as well as a wide receiver, safety, and kick returner as a high school football player. He’s a comfortable zone defender with a nose for the ball, and knows how to use his rare length to close receiving windows. He also has the physical mentality to be a pseudo-linebacker and enforcer in the box. (18) Missouri vs. (7) Texas ESPN – noon (18) Missouri player to watch – Jamal Roberts (RB) Roberts stepped into the gaping hole left by the devastating injury to Ahmad Hardy and has absolutely thrived. Roberts has good size at 6-foot, 215 pounds, and a good balance of play strength, vision, and quickness. He had a dominant 211-yard, 3-touchdown performance against Florida and a 222-yard game against Texas A&M the next week. He currently leads the SEC in both rushing attempts and yards, and is a capable pass catcher as well as a true workhorse back. Roberts could be a fantastic value on the third day of the draft. (7) Texas player to watch – Maraad Watson (iDL) Watson has been below the national radar, but the New Jersey native is a massive young man at 6-foot-3, 333 pounds and has been quietly productive. He only has 19 tackles on the year, but also has 3.0 tackles for a loss, 3.0 sacks and a forced fumble. Watson is a projected 6th round pick at the moment, so he could be a hidden gem with long term upside for the Giants on the third day. (14) LSU vs. (5) Alabama ABC – 3:30 p.m. (14) LSU Player to watch – Princewill Umanmielen (EDGE) EDGE/OLB could be a sneaky need for the Giants in 2027. Fans might not want to see it, but the Giants would only have two starting caliber pass rushers on their team if they allow Kayvon Thibodeaux to leave in free agency. And while Thibodeaux’s stats haven’t been up to expectations, he’s emerged as a “Leonard Williams” style facilitator for the rest of the defensive front. Umanmielen is a long and fluid rusher with a great first step and the kind of motor that’ll brin a smile to Dennard Wilson’s face. He’s also fifth in all of college football for sacks at 8.5. (5) Alabama player to watch – Bray Hubbard (S) Hubbard is another industrial-sized safety who can play box safety or the STAR hybrid defender at the next level. He has great size at 6-foot-2, 215 pounds and isn’t afraid to be physical near the line of scrimmage. He’s a tone-setter coming downhill while also having the athleticism to be a real factor dropping into underneath coverage. Hubbard has 9 interceptions, 10 passes defensed, and 5 forced fumbles over the last three years while starting in Alabama’s sophisticated defense. (12) Ohio State vs. (23) Oregon CBS – 3:30 p.m. (12) Ohio State player to watch – Kenyatta Jackson (DE/EDGE) Jackson was supposed to be the next Ohio State defensive lineman. However, the fifth-year senior has yet to consistently play up to his athletic potential for the Buckeyes. He has an NFL-ready frame at 6-foot-6, 265 pounds, and Giants’ fans who want a return to a 4-3 front with “classic” 7-technique defensive ends will be intrigued. He does have the play strength to reduce inside to a 4i or 3-technique alignment, and that versatility could make him an intriguing option for Dennard Wilson’s defense as it’s being run today. He could be an option anywhere from the end of Round 1 into Day 2. (23) Oregon player to watch – A’Mauri Washington (iDL) Washington has been on our radar since the summer. Unfortunately, he’s been one of the (many) Oregon players who haven’t been able to consistently play up to their potential. However, if the Giants want to replace Dexter Lawrence, Washington might be worth a long look. He has a similar build at 6-foot-3, 330 pounds, with simply absurd lower-body power — he has a 35-inch vertical leap and a 765-pound squat. He’s also surprisingly fast for a big man and has topped 20 miles per hour in a sprint. He has the potential to be a game-wrecker if he can fully unlock his potential at the next level. (13) Tennessee vs. (6) Kentucky ESPN – 6:15 p.m. (13) Tennessee player to watch – Xavier Gilliam (iDL) We looked at Gilliam very recently, but he has been one of the biggest risers in all of college football. And if the Giants are as serious about adding to their defensive line as they seem to be, Gilliam has to be in consideration for their first round pick (if they have one, and he’s there). He has stormed onto the national stage after transferring from Penn State to the Tennessee and has been the best defensive tackle in the country. His leverage, power, and explosiveness has made him an absolute terror for interior offensive linemen. The 6-foot-2, 305-pound tackle currently has 6.0 sacks, 11.5 tackles for a loss, 2 forced fumbles, and 2 passes defensed. (4) Kentucky player to watch – Colton Price (OC) Bryan Hudson has played well at center over the last few weeks. However, the Giants may want to bring in some competition or depth for their pivot. Price has a good build for an NFL center at 6-foot-3, 308 pounds and is highly regarded for his football IQ as well as his competitive toughness. He transferred from Baylor to Kentucky after earning his degree at Baylor and is not only an excellent pass protector, but is proving to be a capable run blocker on Kentucky’s physical line. He might not have the athletic traits to be drafted early, but he could prove to be an excellent option as a Day 3 pick to battle for a starting center job. (11) Notre Dame vs. (1) Miami NBC – 7:30 p.m. (11) Notre Dame player to watch – Adon Shuler (S) Another New Jersey native, Shuler is a versatile piece in a very good Notre Dame secondary. He’ll likely be a strong safety or STAR nickel defender at the next level, with the ability to be a factor playing in space or coming downhill. He has solid size at 6-foot, 205 pounds, and has a reputation for toughness and intensity. He’s a two-time team captain (2025 and 2026) who’s well regarded for his football IQ as well as his propensity for making clutch plays. (1) Miami player to watch – Ahmad Moten Sr. (iDL) This is the third time around putting the spotlight on the Miami defensive line. The duo of Ahmad Moten Sr. and Justin Scott is among the best in the nation, and spotlighting one usually means spotlighting both. The Hurricanes will need both to play at their absolute…

title: NY Giants trade rumors: Ravens say Derrick Henry won’t be dealt
summary: Plan A for the New York Giants to upgrade at running back remains a mega-deal for Jonathan Taylor. Plan B, if there is a real Plan B, won’t be Derrick Henry of the Baltimore Ravens. Per Adam Schefter, the Ravens have “informed Henry that they have no intention of trading him” to his former coach […]
full_text: Derrick Henry | Getty Images Plan A for the New York Giants to upgrade at running back remains a mega-deal for Jonathan Taylor . Plan B, if there is a real Plan B, won’t be Derrick Henry of the Baltimore Ravens. Per Adam Schefter, the Ravens have “informed Henry that they have no intention of trading him” to his former coach John Harbaugh and the Giants, or anywhere else. The understandable logic behind that, from a Ravens point of view, is that the Ravens are not a) giving up on this season, or b) giving up on the idea that they can retain star quarterback Lamar Jackson long term. Peter Schrager of ESPN added this on ‘GetUp’ , per Pro Football and Sports Network : “I don’t see it,” said Schrager. “My sense is this, talking to Baltimore’s sources: they have 12 draft picks in the upcoming draft, so draft capital doesn’t really do anything right now. They also play the Chargers, Panthers, Texans, Bucs the next four weeks. Those are winnable games. And they just traded for a quarterback; they traded for Cam Jurgens.” “They’re not already in this selloff, fire sale mode. They are not Tennessee, they are not Indianapolis. That said, if there are calls about some other players they would probably be listening to some. I’m talking about guys who might’ve put themselves as veterans on the trade market themselves by the way that they’ve been performing in recent weeks.” Justice Hill? Schefter mentioned in his report that the Giants had asked the Ravens about the availability of veteran running back Justice Hill . Hill was a 2019 fourth-round draft pick by the Ravens and has spent his entire career with Baltimore, so Harbaugh knows him well. The confusing thing about interest in the 28-year-old Hill is that in seven seasons he has never carried the ball more than 84 times, and has just 301 carries for his career. There is nothing on his resume to suggest he is better than Tyrone Tracy or Devin Singletary. Unless the Giants are concerned about the hamstring injuries Tryone Tracy (currently on IR) and Cam Skattebo (doubtful vs. the Eagles) are dealing with and see Hill as an emergency fill-in, I’m not sure what he adds to the backfield. Latest on Jonathan Taylor The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones believes that the Giants and Minnesota Vikings are the favorites to convince the Indianapolis Colts to trade their star running back. Jones said he was told the Colts have already rejected an offer of a second- and fifth-round pick. NFL.com also listed the Giants as one of the most likely landing spots for Taylor, and I believe the reasoning they offered is spot on: A splash move at the deadline could go a long way to ensuring the Giants keep their division lead into January — and provide them a chance to pull off a postseason upset. I believe that the Giants, with the investment they made in Harbaugh, would love to justify it with an NFC East title in Harbaugh’s first season. I also think they believe it would help set them up for the future, a future they believe Taylor can be part of for a couple of seasons. In regards’ to Jones’ reporting that the Colts rejected a second- and fifth-round pick, what if the Giants made this offer: A 2027 second-round pick, a 2028 fifth-round pick, and Tracy. If you are bringing in Taylor, and you have Skattebo, you don’t really have carries for Tracy. Why not include him in your offer in an effort to hold on to some of your draft capital? Vita Vea too pricey? We wrote Friday that Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ defensive tackle Vita Vea was reportedly on the Giants’ radar . Jones writes: Vea signed a one-year, $30 million contract extension in August after protracted negotiations. It would be unusual for the team to deal him less than three months later, even if he has a low base salary in 2026 that can fit under anyone’s cap. In the NFC South, furthermore, you’re always in it. The Bucs are a half-game behind Carolina for the division lead, and they hold the early tiebreakers over Carolina and Atlanta. A 3-5 record in Tampa looks radically different from a 3-5 record in Arizona. I don’t think Tampa Bay would turn down a first-round pick for Vea, but I also don’t think any team is going to offer one for a 31-year-old with one season left on his deal. Vea would help the Giants, but he also appears to be in decline: Giving up a first-round pick would seem like a massive overpayment.
