title: New York Giants mailbag: Trade deadline, McCarthy vs. Dart, more questions
summary: Isaac L. Scharf asks: Hello, do you really believe that the Giants are contenders, or are they pretenders? We may be seeing a little bit of last year’s Patriots given the fact that we haven’t played a single team over .500. So do you think the Giants are contenders or pretenders? Ed says: Isaac, the […]
full_text: Isaac L. Scharf asks: Hello, do you really believe that the Giants are contenders, or are they pretenders? We may be seeing a little bit of last year’s Patriots given the fact that we haven’t played a single team over .500. So do you think the Giants are contenders or pretenders? Ed says: Isaac, the standings say they are contenders. The oddsmakers say they are the favorites to win the NFC East . The way everyone else in the division has played absolutely tells us that the Giants should be in the race for the division down to the wire. Pretenders? Well, yes, if you think of them as a team that will or should be a legitimate Super Bowl contender. I say just take the ride, enjoy it, and don’t try to label the Giants as anything. Chris Holland asks: I am wondering if the NFL has made any statements regarding the rampant use of the “peanut punch”. From a safety perspective this is an accident waiting to happen. Ball carriers are going to start suffering injuries to their hands and lower arm as the result of having very large and strong defenders throw full force punches at the ball. I have already seen a player get accidentally punched in the head by one of these “peanut punches”. I get the feeling that the league will continue to allow this practice despite obvious safety concerns because the punches can result in turnovers and looks good on Sportscenter. I also think it’s basically impossible for the ball carriers to truly secure the ball against these punches. Thoughts? Ed says: Chris, no, there have not been any statements about the Peanut Punch that I am aware of. The league did fine Dre Greenlaw for striking the helmet of Atlanta Falcons wide receiver on a missed punch. Maybe it comes up during the offseason when new rules are discussed. Until then, I don’t think anything changes. Darren Silver asks: Supposing JJ McCarthy continues to play well and the Giants make the playoffs as a result, does it really make sense to then trade him for draft picks? Since he’s on a manageable contract, I think having a starting caliber QB back-up is much more valuable than any extra draft picks he might attract. We know Dart (or any starting QB) can go down in a heartbeat. Why not have QB insurance to save us from losing a season due to another Dart injury? I don’t think even a first round pick is as valuable as that would be. Ed says: Darren, there is a line between having a good backup quarterback and having a full-blown quarterback controversy over who should be the starter. That can divide a locker room, a coaching staff, a fan base, and the media that pumps out content about the team every day. Nobody wants “who is playing quarterback this week?” to be a question that gets asked consistently. Or, for fans to start chanting the backup’s name the first time the starter plays poorly. If McCarthy plays well enough, that is is the risk you run. If he plays well enough the rest of the season to deserve to be a starting quarterback, you automatically set up a “who’s team is it?” situation if they are both on the 2027 roster. Those never work out well. Jameis Winston is the quarterback insurance, and he is fine for a few games. A lot of teams would love to have him. The only way I see McCarthy and Dart both being on the team next season is if McCarthy plays OK, but the overall body of work makes it clear that the ceiling is higher with Dart and there is zero question about who is No. 1. I still believe the ideal scenario is that McCarthy plays well enough to create a robust market for him this offseason, and that the Giants are able to turn that fifth-round pick they used to acquire him into multiple draft picks of higher value. Could McCarthy play so well that the Giants actually decide to put Dart on the market in the offseason? Sure. But, we are nowhere close to that yet. It has been five quarters of football. Tom Donlan asks: What is the biggest roster weakness that you think could prevent the Giants from winning the division, and how realistic can it (they) be upgraded via trade this year, and which parts of the Giants success look sustainable beyond this season so they challenge for the division with regularity? Also, when you look back at this deadline two years from now, what decision – or decision to stand pat – would tell us the Giants evaluated themselves correctly? Ed says: Tom, I think the biggest roster weakness the Giants need to address is defensive tackle. D.J. Reader is the only good, reliable interior defensive lineman they have. The run defense has been good at times, porous at other times. You can’t consistently defend the run if you can’t consistently hole the line of scrimmage. The sustainable part of the Giants is that they will have John Harbaugh for the next few years. Rosters change, and there are a lot of unforeseen things. I think we have to see what decisions ultimately get made before speculating on the last part of the question. The generic answer would simply be the tell-tale sign of whether or not the Giants did the right thing would be how much success they have beyond this year. Ronald Buchheim asks: Ed, have you talked with trainers or doctors about groin injuries in general or the one that Andrew Thomas has? Do you know whether it is wise to play through these injuries rather than resting completely? And whether playing through risks the injury becoming chronic and hampering the player’s subsequent career? Ed says: Ronald, I have not asked anyone. Players play through injuries all the time. I’m sure there is some risk of making the injury worse, but the Giants wouldn’t put him out there if he wasn’t capable of playing or was risking damaging his career. Michael Buscemi asks: Trying to understand the Colts philosophy — there’s four or five teams interested in Taylor. I don’t understand at this point the Colts demands if they want a number one and no one stepping up to the plate to pay a number one they have two choices — the first don’t do a trade, keep Taylor. By playing him this week they risked the factor of injury which removes any trade ability why take a chance if you really want to trade him trade him or do nothing? Again the risk of injury playing him could remove any possible trade. Ed says: Michael, the Colts, it seems, are going to play this out all the way to the trade deadline on Tuesday and see if anyone will get desperate and up their offer. There is risk, but if they hold him out and then don’t trade him that is not a good look for Indianapolis. Brennan Lyons asks: I was wondering if you guys have heard any solid rumors about us pursuing Brian Thomas of Jacksonville? I really liked him coming out of LSU, along with Nabers, a few years ago. I would love to see them paired up again on the Giants. I have seen reports that the Jaguars are looking for depth at Edge and are apparently intent on getting rid of Thomas. Do you think there would be any chance of trading Thibs for him? I doubt we will resign him after this year but I’m not so sure we would be willing to let him go now that we are in the midst of a legitimate playoff run. Do you think we can effectively replace Thibs for the rest of the season? Long term, we would have control of Thomas for two more years than Thibs. Do you think the Giants would make that move? Ed says: Brennan, I have not. The Giants, by all accounts, are focused on adding at defensive tackle or taking a big swing at a star running back. I understand the idea of trading Kayvon Thibodeaux. The issue with that is that the Giants have already lost Brian Burns, Tremaine Edmunds, and Chauncey Golston to injury. Thibodeaux is important to the defense right now. If the Giants were not in prime position to make a playoff run trading Thibodeaux would be an obvious move. Now? Love him or not, he is an important piece of the defense. Joseph LoBue asks: I found the Compensatory Free Agent chart that you put together last week quite informative (from a CFA process perspective) but even more interesting…

full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to as the first place Giants get ready to face off tomorrow against the Philadelphia Eagles. New York Giants ’ playoff fate will be heavily influenced by Eagles game | USAToday.com Based on the analytics and percentages, a Giants win would put them in prime position for a playoff spot. A loss would drop them back deep into the pack. A Giants win would give them a 68 percent chance to win the NFC East and a 71 percent shot at making the playoffs. A loss would lessen their division odds to 41 percent and their postseason odds to 43 percent. So, this is kind of a “must-win” for Big Blue (4-2-1) as their schedule gets dicey in the second half of the season. Coach Harbaugh breaking down Texans film Coach Harbaugh analyzes the last play of the game against Houston — New York Giants (@Giants) November 6, 2026 Harbs Weekly: Earn the right to play in memorable games | Giants.com Q: Getting into November football, is there a new skill that your team has to unlock? Harbaugh: Everything is new. Every step of the way is going to be new this year. I think it’s kind of what first years are a lot of times. Like we told them, this is November football. You’ve earned the right to play meaningful games in November. What does that mean? What are you playing for? I asked them, “What do they say about December football? Have you heard the old saying?” And someone got it. [Fullback Patrick] Ricard got it. “They remember what you do in December.” That’s right. I said that’s what they remember. I said they won’t really remember November too much. But without November you can’t get to the point where you’re playing games that are going to be memorable. That’s what we’re playing for right now. We’re playing for the opportunity to play in memorable games, and that’s why November is so important and we’ve earned the right to be to be playing in these games. So, it’s just another notch up of value and then I just talked to them a little bit about as the season goes along, it’s still one game but each game becomes worth more. It’s one game, that’s what this is about, but each game becomes even more valuable because there’s more payoff. Later, that’s why they remember what you do in December. There’s more payoff. So, that’s kind of cool. Giants not looking past Saquon Barkley and struggling Eagles | New York Post “Before Lane Johnson had a name, before Jason Kelce had a name, before Cam Jurgens had a name, they had to go earn it,” defensive tackle Shelby Harris said. “You can’t put down anybody just because they haven’t established themselves in the league. The idea is you don’t want them to establish themselves against you. They’re still physical, they’re humungous size-wise across the board, so it’s just go out there and don’t let them be the determining factor of the game.” “I’m expecting [Barkley] to be healthier than he has been so far,” Harris said. “They’ve done a good job trying to manage him on his way back from injury. If he’s going to play, I expect to get the best out of him — full-on star Saquon Barkley. And we’ll have to stop him in order to be successful.” NFL Week 9 preview: Picks, predictions, schedule, betting odds, fantasy tips | ESPN.com What we’re hearing on the Giants: The Giants believe the bye week should’ve helped QB J.J. McCarthy. He’s now fully caught up after being traded to New York in late September. McCarthy, who is making his second start for the Giants, expects Eagles DC Vic Fangio to make him “earn it.” It will be the latest test of whether the young QB can succeed while facing simulated pressures and getting through his progressions. How Skatt and the Giants are fed Dr. Matt Frakes is the head of nutrition for the New York Giants. Part of his job is to help the players understand the impact of their food choices. @charlottecrrll spoke with Cam Skattebo and Frakes on how nutrition has impacted the team's recent success, particularly with… pic.twitter.com/8elG7zg7gh — The Athletic (@TheAthletic) November 6, 2026 Ravens’ Derrick Henry is frustrated. Will Giants’ John Harbaugh try to trade for him? | NJ.com “I mean, we’ve lost four times [in a row],” Henry said. “It’s frustrating. I don’t have the magical answer. We’ve got to go back to work.” When asked about a potential trade, Henry said, “I have not mentioned me going anywhere else. I’m saying let’s go back to work.” Henry turns 33 in January. He is under contract through next season. Harbaugh doesn’t want a one-year rental, and Henry technically would not be that. His salary next year is $11 million — all of which is non-guaranteed. He has a $1 million roster bonus due in March. So the Ravens (or Giants) have a team option on him for 2027. The 10 best NFL player matchups to watch in Week 9 | PFF New York Giants WR Malik Nabers vs. Philadelphia Eagles CB Quinyon Mitchell. The Giants seek to widen their NFC East lead when they face the Eagles, losers of six in a row. While a battle of backup quarterbacks may be the top storyline, Nabers vs. Mitchell will be must-see television. Nabers has returned from his torn ACL with a vengeance. He’s earned an 82.8 PFF receiving grade with 2.54 yards per route run, numbers that have culminated despite a slower first three games. On top of that, the former sixth overall pick has dropped only two catchable targets all year. Philadelphia’s defense has regressed in 2026, but not because of Mitchell. He’s generated a 67.2 PFF coverage grade, letting up a 69.2 passer rating into his coverage while enabling just a 54.3% opponent completion percentage. Mitchell has had the advantage when these former 2024 first-round picks have squared off. Across 11 prior matchups, Nabers has gained just one catch for nine yards on two targets, being charted as open only three times. Giants look to snap losing streak in Philadelphia. If not now, when? | The Athletic The Giants have had heartbreakers at Lincoln Financial Field, but a loss Sunday would be the worst of the streak because they’re the better team with a far more promising outlook. The Giants are 3.5-point favorites Sunday and winning in Philadelphia would be another step in Harbaugh’s process of rebuilding the franchise. Harbaugh’s track record suggests the Giants are in a strong position to end the streak. His Ravens teams went 15-3 after the bye during his 18 seasons in Baltimore. “We’ve got everything to gain and we know how big this game is,” Harbaugh said. “We know who we’re going against. title: Jets vs Chiefs: Five Questions with Arrowhead Pride
summary: The New York Jets are on the road in Kansas City, Missouri on Sunday for the 9th game of their 2026 campaign. They will be facing the Kansas City Chiefs. The Chiefs have lost two straight games after starting the season 5-0. Previewing this matchup, Maurice Elston, a writer at Arrowhead Pride, was kind enough […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 01: (NEW YORK DAILIES OUT) Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs in action against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on October 01, 2023 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Chiefs defeated the Jets 23-20. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets are on the road in Kansas City, Missouri on Sunday for the 9th game of their 2026 campaign. They will be facing the Kansas City Chiefs. The Chiefs have lost two straight games after starting the season 5-0. Previewing this matchup, Maurice Elston, a writer at Arrowhead Pride, was kind enough to answer a few questions regarding the 2026 Kansas City Chiefs. The Chiefs limited their opponents to 10 points or fewer in three of their first five games, but they have allowed a combined 48 points in the last two games. Are the recent struggles on defense just a quality of opponent issue, or are there bigger problems involved? I think there are some bigger issues involved, particularly the Chiefs’ inability to consistently pressure the quarterback and finish possessions on critical downs. Seattle converted 11 of 16 third downs and controlled the ball for nearly 36 minutes. Denver only converted 2 of 11 third downs, so the defense improved in that area, but the Broncos went 2-for-2 on fourth down. That continued a trend we have seen against the Chiefs: opposing coaches are willing to be aggressive on fourth down because they understand the importance of extending possessions and keeping Patrick Mahomes off the field. The lack of a pass rush ties everything together. The Chiefs failed to record a sack against Seattle and produced only one against Denver. They have only nine sacks through seven games, with one of the NFL’s lowest pressure and sack rates. When you cannot consistently pressure the quarterback, offenses have more time to find favorable matchups. When you combine that with an inability to finish possessions on third or fourth down, it eventually leads to more plays, more yards and more points. The quality of the opposition certainly played a role, but the pass rush is a legitimate concern that must be corrected. The Chiefs’ offense had fallen into an average-ish range over the past few years, but this year they are back to being one of the better offenses in the NFL. Is this just the Kenneth Walker effect? What has gone right this year that wasn’t necessarily working in recent years for the Chiefs? The Kenneth Walker effect is certainly one of the biggest reasons for the improvement. The Chiefs had not possessed a truly dynamic running game or a home-run threat at running back in recent years. Walker has 770 rushing yards through seven games, which has already surpassed the season total of Kansas City’s leading rusher in each of the previous two years. Kareem Hunt led the Chiefs with 728 yards in 2024 and only 611 in 2025. Walker’s presence has changed how defenses must prepare for Kansas City. They can no longer play light boxes, sit back in coverage and assume the Chiefs will eventually abandon the running game. Andy Reid has also used more under-center formations and play-action concepts, which have created better opportunities for Mahomes. During the first five games, before Tyquan Thornton’s injury, the combination worked especially well. Defenses had to respect Walker in the backfield while also accounting for Thornton’s ability to stretch the field. When opponents played zero coverage or crowded the line of scrimmage, the Chiefs had somebody capable of beating them deep. Walker is not the only reason the offense has improved, but his presence has made every other element more effective. The running game, play-action passing and vertical threat were complementing one another in a way we had not seen from this offense in several years. Can you give us a synopsis of what the Chiefs’ draft class has looked like so far, and what you expect from them as the year goes on? The first name that stands out is Mansoor Delane. The Chiefs traded up to select him sixth overall, and when healthy, he has looked worthy of that investment. The shoulder injury that has followed him since the offseason has caused him to miss time, but his coverage has been excellent. Even on some of the receptions he allowed against Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Delane was in good position. Sometimes a great throw and catch simply beat great coverage. R Mason Thomas has also flashed as a pass rusher. His sack total does not reflect it yet, but you can see his natural ability to turn the corner and defeat offensive tackles. His next step is learning how to finish those pressures and turn them into sacks. Emmett Johnson has contributed in several different roles. He has returned kicks, played on special teams and shown value as a receiving and pass-protecting back. His breakout performance against Denver—143 yards from scrimmage, including 128 receiving yards and a touchdown—demonstrated the type of weapon he can become. Peter Woods, the Chiefs’ second first-round pick, has shown flashes but has lacked consistency and is now dealing with a neck injury. Cyrus Allen has not received many offensive opportunities, but he has displayed an intriguing ceiling when he has gotten on the field. Fourth-round cornerback Jadon Canady was inactive or used sparingly early in the season, but injuries in the secondary have created opportunities for him. Seventh-round quarterback Garrett Nussmeier is more of a developmental player and has not factored into the offense. Overall, I would describe the class as solid with a high ceiling. Delane already looks like a potential cornerstone, while Thomas and Johnson have shown they can become significant contributors. As injuries create more opportunities, I expect several members of this class to take on larger roles during the second half of the season. Every team has a player or two who may be somewhat unfamiliar to other teams’ fans but is known as an unsung hero by fans of his own team. Who are the Chiefs’ unsung heroes? If possible, give us one player on each side of the ball. On offense, I would go with Emmett Johnson. Jets fans may be a little more familiar with him after his performance against Denver, but he still is not a household name. Johnson gives the Chiefs another weapon in the passing game and has also contributed as a runner, blocker and returner. He does not need 15 touches to affect a game because he can create a big play whenever the ball finds him. Defensively, I would choose Christian Roland-Wallace. With L’Jarius Sneed now on injured reserve, Roland-Wallace becomes an important part of the secondary rotation. He has been one of the Chiefs’ most improved defensive players and offers the versatility to contribute outside or in the slot. He may not receive much national attention, but he could play a significant role while Kansas City works through its injuries at cornerback. If you were an opposing head coach, how would you attack this Chiefs team on offense and on defense? When defending the Chiefs, my approach would be straightforward until Kansas City proves it can consistently beat it without Tyquan Thornton. I would crowd the line of scrimmage to slow down Kenneth Walker, challenge the Chiefs’ wide receivers with physical man coverage and trust my front four to win against Kansas City’s offensive tackles. Thornton provided the vertical threat that punished defenses for stacking the box. Without him, teams have been much more aggressive about taking away the running game and forcing the remaining receivers to win one-on-one. When attacking the Chiefs’ defense, I would target the linebackers in coverage. If an offense has a dynamic receiving back or tight end, it should look for ways to isolate that player against Kansas City’s linebackers in space. I would also remain aggressive on fourth down, because opponents have shown that extending drives can wear this defense down. The formula is to force Kansas City’s receivers…

title: Three things I’m looking at in the Jets vs. Chiefs Game
summary: We’re back ready to watch our New York Jets play against the Kansas City Chiefs. For the third straight week, the Jets are facing a team that’s coming off consecutive losses and looking to “get right” against Gang Green. Miami and Las Vegas were able to accomplish that feat and it seems like Kansas City […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 1: Braelon Allen #0 of the New York Jets runs the ball against the Las Vegas Raiders at MetLife Stadium on November 1, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Raiders defeated the Jets 38-33. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re back ready to watch our New York Jets play against the Kansas City Chiefs. For the third straight week, the Jets are facing a team that’s coming off consecutive losses and looking to “get right” against Gang Green. Miami and Las Vegas were able to accomplish that feat and it seems like Kansas City should theoretically have no problem doing the same. The Chiefs started the season 5-0 and although they’ve been inconsistent, they are coached by one of the greatest coaches in history, have a great defense and a first ballot hall of famer at QB. It’ll be quite the tall task for the Jets to upset the Chiefs. While the Jets were actually the favorites going into the last two weeks at home, they are a 9.5-point underdog as they enter Arrowhead Stadium. It’s tied with the Raiders-Niners game for the largest spread in the NFL this week so that should help paint the picture of how tough this will be for the Jets to overcome. Still, anything is possible and this year’s Jets have firepower! Let’s take a look: The Split I usually pride myself on discussing the “lesser-talked” items that don’t get mainstream media attention, but the elephant in the Jets’ RB room is too massive to ignore. The entire fanbase and media have completely turned on Breece Hall (again) and have spent the last month hypothetically trading him all over the league. As the sole human being left who still wants him to spend his entire 20’s as a Jet, this game seems like a real pivotal moment for that dream I have. Let’s make no mistake about it: Braelon Allen has been absolutely incredible these last four weeks. He has arguably been the best rusher in the entire NFL during this time, averaging over 100 yards per game and scoring the game-winning touchdown against the Browns. He’s proven to be a valuable rushing asset, which was very much up for debate before he suited up against the Bears this season. The question is, is there enough pie for multiple running backs to eat? Plenty of teams thrive with duos that eat consistently on a weekly basis. The Rams’ Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, the Bears’ D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai, and Broncos’ J.K. Dobbins and R.J. Harvey are some quick examples. Even the Raiders who just beat the Jets last week had Mike Washington take 25 carries and Ashton Jeanty still finish the game with 70+ scrimmage yards. It’s up to Frank Reich to deploy these two Killer Bs in a way that maximizes both players’ talent, and I think it’s easier to do than my colleagues and fellow Jets content creators have claimed. I think there is plenty to go around and wholeheartedly believe it’d be a grave mistake to trade Breece Hall. Of course, conventional wisdom says to keep Braelon running his 17+ carries per game and then utilize Breece’s route running and hands to be a weapon in the pass game. I agree with that general philosophy, but would still value Breece’s rushing ability. His issues have been between the tackles but he’s explosive in space and I’d utilize those young tackles to deploy outside runs to get Breece going. Luckily, this game will be away, so the crowd won’t be a factor – I believe the impatient short-sighted fans have already made their decision so if Hall were to start slow he’d hear his own fans booing him. At Arrowhead, this is a nonfactor, he has the freedom to get himself involved without hearing from the peanut gallery and a chance to prove they can be a duo for years to come. What does success look like? The Chiefs have allowed 100+ scrimmage to opposing RB1s in three of the last four weeks. That one exception is the Chargers, who are still winless and have been horrible all year. I’m looking for 100+ scrimmage yards for RB1 and 50+ scrimmage yards for RB2. Now, who is RB1 and RB2? That’s up for Frank Reich, Breece Hall, and Braelon Allen to decide. Walker On A Dream I think we can all agree that Aaron Glenn’s superpowers of defensive play-calling are the worst ‘powers’ out there and that the Jets defense has been an issue. It looks like things are going to get bad to worse because the Chiefs are looking to get their high-powered offense back on track. They were averaging 28 points and undefeated until this two-game skid hit and they scored 27 points combined in these last two. Now they’re facing a Jets team that has allowed 30.6(!) points per game during this three game losing streak. They’ve especially been leaky to the the running back position, which is horrible news when you consider Kenneth Walker is having a career year. Only Jahmyr Gibbs has more rushing yards per game and only Jaylen Warren has more yards per carry. They also having a rookie running back Emmett Johnson who just caught five passes for 128(!) yards last week and a touchdown last week. Will this running back duo show us what a real duo looks like and run wild on the porous Jets defense this week? What adjustments can Glenn make, what players can step up, or will it just be “Jets beating Jets” like Minkah Fitzpatrick said last week? No Wil(son), No Way? Garrett Wilson is set to miss his first game of the season with a concussion, and while that normally meant complete despair for the offense in the past, there are lots of options to step up this Sunday. Of course Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. seem like the natural choices, but there are cases to be made for Mason Taylor, Kenyon Sadiq and Isaiah Williams. Even the aforementioned Breece Hall can get a lot of looks in the pass game. Wilson had 12 targets last week. You may be thinking “how do we replace all those targets?” but in the weeks prior you may recall that his targets have been an issue. Geno has had no problem spreading the ball around all season so I’d imagine this week will be more of the same. The most interesting thing to me is seeing who garners the most attention from the Chiefs defense. If you were Steve Spagnuolo what would you do? Mitchell is coming off a 142-yard game but Omar Cooper Jr. had consecutive 100 yard games before that. With attention and potential double teams occurring on the outside is this a game for the tight ends to finally feast? Sadiq still only has 5 catches for 43 scoreless yards in the five games since his 100-yard breakout performance against the Lions. Hopefully Frank Reich and Geno Smith can keep the offensive momentum rolling without their best WR on the field. Let’s go Jets!

title: Previewing the Jets’ opposition: Kansas City Chiefs
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs have beaten the New York Jets in four of their five meetings since 2011, with the most recent being a controversial 23-20 win in 2023. That game saw Michael Carter II’s game-clinching interception negated by a phantom penalty on Sauce Gardner and wasted one of the best performances of Zach Wilson’s […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs with the football and looks to pass during the third quarter against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The Broncos defeated the Chiefs 28-24. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs have beaten the New York Jets in four of their five meetings since 2011, with the most recent being a controversial 23-20 win in 2023. That game saw Michael Carter II’s game-clinching interception negated by a phantom penalty on Sauce Gardner and wasted one of the best performances of Zach Wilson’s career. In this matchup, the Chiefs will be heavy favorites despite having lost two in a row following a 5-0 start. Let’s break down the Chiefs’ roster going position by position: Quarterbacks The Jets have Patrick Mahomes to reckon with this week, and he’s having a solid season as he’s posting a quarterback rating of 99.7; his best since 2022. Mahomes has 12 touchdowns and four interceptions and is coming off a good game against the Broncos where he passed for 321 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions. Behind Mahomes is a familiar face: Jets 2025 starter Justin Fields. Seventh round rookie Garrett Nussmeier is the number three. Offensive Line The Chiefs’ interior line is the same as last year led by pro bowlers Creed Humphrey and Trey Smith at center and right guard respectively. Smith has a team-high five offensive penalties. Kingsley Suamataia completes the interior trio at left guard, although he’s already been benched twice this year, including on Sunday where he was suddenly replaced before pre-game warmups by Mike Caliendo. That fuelled rumors that was was being disciplined by the coaching staff but Andy Reid denied this. Caliendo, who also started four games last year, has struggled in pass protection. Suamataia is expected to be back in the starting lineup for Sunday’s game. The tackle positions have seen some changes as last year’s starting right tackle, Jawaan Taylor, was released in March and the starting left tackle – 2025 first round pick Josh Simmons – is on injured reserve. Jaylon Moore, who started a handful of games last year, is currently starting at right tackle, while the left tackle is undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson, who is one of five undrafted rookies on the roster. Moore has given up a team-high three sacks, but Benson – while yet to surrender a sack – has given up the most pressure on the team. Moore missed week seven’s game, so former New York Giant Joshua Ezeudu started at right tackle in that one. The other backups are center Hunter Nourzad and another undrafted rookie; tackle Diego Pounds. Running Backs The Chiefs’ big offseason acquisition on offense was the reigning Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker. The move has been a resounding success as he rushed for 100 yards in four of his first five games as the Chiefs started 5-0. Since then, he’s averaged just three yards per carry, though. Even so, he’s just 10 yards off the league lead with 770 rushing yards. He has also caught 22 passes. There are two rookies backing up Walker – fifth round pick Emmett Johnson and the undrafted Jaydn Ott. Ott hasn’t played yet, though. The Chiefs also have a fullback – Ben VanSumeren – on the roster. However, they will also use defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga in short yardage situations. He has even carried the ball twice. Pass catchers The Chiefs’ top pass catching option has once again been tight end Travis Kelce, who has 410 receiving yards to lead the team. The leading pass catcher among the wide receivers is the speedy Xavier Worthy, who has 27 catches, albeit that he’s only averaging 8.5 yards per catch. Despite some injury concerns and legal issues, Rashee Rice is now back in the lineup for the Chiefs. He has 20 catches in five games this year. Tyquan Thornton was also starting at wide receiver, but he’s now on injured reserve. The backups are Jalen Royals, Andrew Armstrong, Nikko Remigio and fifth round rookie Cyrus Allen. Royals has seen the most action from this group. At tight end, Noah Gray is a solid contributor who gets plenty of playing time. Jake Briningstool and Jared Wiley round out this group. Defensive Line The Chiefs’ defensive line is anchored by pro bowler Chris Jones, although he is having a down year statistically with just half a sack, one tackle for loss and three quarterback hits. He had 7.5, 12 and 25 last year. George Karlaftis, who had six sacks last year, has a team-high two sacks and also leads the team with 16 quarterback hits (just one less than the rest of the team combined) and six tackles for loss. Karlaftis also has a team-high with eight passes defensed. In fact, these all eight of these came in the last five games. Prior to that, he had 17 in his first 67 NFL games. Tonga is the other starter at defensive tackle with Felix Anudike-Uzomah the other starting defensive end. Kansas City has been operating a three-man rotation inside with first round rookie Peter Woods getting plenty of playing time. However, Woods has been ruled out with a neck injury so Bryson Eason may need to step up. Last year’s second round pick Omarr Norman-Lott remains on the PUP list. The backups on the edge are second round rookie R Mason Thomas and Ashton Gillotte. Undrafted rookie Jack Pyburn is also on the roster. Linebackers Nick Bolton remains in a full-time role with Drue Tranquill on the field most of the time. Last year, Bolton had 154 tackles and Tranquill added 103. They’ve been productive this year, too, with Bolton on 68 tackles and Tranquill on 53 tackles, including five tackles for loss. Jack Cochrane gets playing time in three-linebacker sets, while Jeffrey Bassa has seen limited action. Cooper McDonald has yet to play any defensive snaps, though. Defensive Backs The Chiefs suffered a loss a few weeks ago when their top cornerback L’Jairus Sneed was placed on injured reserve. Sneed was also the team’s primary slot corner, so they’ve been using Christian Roland-Wallace in that role for the past few weeks. Nohl Williams and first round rookie Mansoor Delane are the current starters on the outside, although Kristian Fulton started in place of Delane on Sunday. Delane has a shoulder issue which is likely to limit him for the rest of the season but he was expected to return against the Jets. However, he has been ruled out, so Fulton will presumably start again. Melvin Smith and fourth round rookie Jadon Canady are also available to provide depth at cornerback. The starting safeties are Chamarri Conner, who had 117 tackles last season, and offseason signing Alohi Gilman. Jaden Hicks has also been getting playing time in three-safety sets. He also started the first three games with Conner out. Undrafted rookie safety Xavier Nwankpa has played five snaps so far this season. Special Teams Former pro bowl kicker Harrison Butker is having a rough year with six missed field goals already and Justin Tucker waiting in the wings on the practice squad in case he should falter again. Punter Matt Araiza is having his best year statistically in his third season with the Chiefs, though. Remigio is the team’s return specialist, although Johnson ends up sharing the work on kickoff returns. Remigio, who is yet to achieve a 50-yard return as he is halfway through his third season, is officially listed as questionable. Bassa and Nwankpa are the team’s most productive players in kick coverage this season, but last year they were led by McDonald and Cochrane. Canady and Nwankpa have been the primary gunners.

full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Makai Lemon #9 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates a touchdown with teammates during the third quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The ninth weekend of the 2026 NFL season is here! Let’s run through a Philadelphia Eagles-focused rooting guide for all of the Week 9 games. EAGLES GAME NEW YORK GIANTS at PHILADELPHIA EAGLES: The Eagles currently have a 2.4% chance of making the playoffs, according to FTN Fantasy . They have the second-longest odds (+1600 on FanDuel) among NFC teams to qualify for the postseason, only ahead of the Arizona Cardinals (+2000). With this in mind, I don’t think it’s unfair to be interested in the Eagles maximizing their positioning in the 2027 NFL Draft. At the same time, I don’t begrudge any Eagles fans who think that’s loser talk and want to see the team win until they’re officially eliminated (and perhaps even past that point). With a victory, the Eagles will be 3-6 entering their Week 10 bye. With a loss, the Eagles can potentially move as high as No. 2 overall in the draft order. Current 2027 NFL Draft order via Tankathon : NFL DRAFT CONSIDERATIONS JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS defeat BALTIMORE RAVENS: It’s good for the Eagles that the Ravens lost on Thursday night because Philly owns Baltimore’s fifth-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. CINCINNATI BENGALS at ATLANTA FALCONS: The Falcons are the bigger threat to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Root for the Falcons. DALLAS COWBOYS at INDIANAPOLIS COLTS: There are multiple reasons to root for the Colts here. 1) If you still want the Eagles to win the NFC East, you want the Cowboys to lose this game. 2) If you want the Eagles to pick as high as they possibly can, you want the Colts to win so that Philly can move ahead of Indy (actual pick owed the New York Jets) in the draft order. Root for the Colts. NEW YORK JETS at KANSAS CITY CHIEFS: The Eagles want to stay ahead of the Jets’ own selection (currently No. 6) in the draft order. Root for the Jets. DETROIT LIONS at MIAMI DOLPHINS: The Eagles want to move ahead of the Dolphins (currently No. 3) in the draft order. Root for the Dolphins. CLEVELAND BROWNS at NEW ORLEANS SAINTS: The Eagles want to stay ahead of the Saints in the draft order. Root for the Saints. LOS ANGELES RAMS at WASHINGTON COMMANDERS: If you want to see the Eagles win the NFC East, you want to see the Commanders lose. But Washington winning helps to ensure Philly stays ahead of them in the draft order. Root for the Commanders. DENVER BRONCOS at CAROLINA PANTHERS: The Panthers are the bigger threat to move ahead of Philly in the draft order. Root for the Panthers. HOUSTON TEXANS at LOS ANGELES CHARGERS: In order for the Eagles to have a chance at the No. 1 overall pick, the Bolts need to win some games. Root for the Chargers. GREEN BAY PACKERS at NEW ENGLAND PATRIOTS: The Eagles own the more favorable of either New England’s or Chicago’s 2027 fifth-round pick due to the A.J. Brown trade. Might as well root for the Pats to lose. Root for the Packers. LAS VEGAS RAIDERS at SAN FRANCISCO 49ERS: The Raiders are the bigger threat to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Also, would be enjoyable to see the Niners lose. Root for the Raiders. ARIZONA CARDINALS at SEATTLE SEAHAWKS: The Cardinals are the bigger threat to move ahead of Philly in the draft order. Root for the Cardinals. TAMPA BAY BUCCANEERS at CHICAGO BEARS: The Bucs are the bigger threat to move ahead of Philly in the draft order. Root for the Buccaneers. BUFFALO BILLS at MINNESOTA VIKINGS: The Eagles don’t want the Patriots to make the playoffs since Philly could own New England’s fifth-round pick. More preferable to see the Bills win the AFC East. title: Eagles News: Cooper DeJean among notable players surprisingly struggling
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! It’s been a weird season for Cooper DeJean, who was pretty awesome in his first two seasons for the Birds. The All-Pro defensive back is missing more tackles than ever (seven missed tackles in eight games this year, one away from […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 26: Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean #33 warms up during the game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Philadelphia Eagles on October 26, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA.(Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! It’s been a weird season for Cooper DeJean, who was pretty awesome in his first two seasons for the Birds. The All-Pro defensive back is missing more tackles than ever (seven missed tackles in eight games this year, one away from tying his single-season career-high for missed tackles) and he’s been vulnerable in coverage (96.2 passer rating allowed after it was just 78.0 over his first two seasons). Seems like the struggles could be a combination of him being more injured than we know … plus his new role splitting time between nickel cornerback and safety. The feeling here is that DeJean will rebound next season. It’s silly to get too down on him. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Struggling players at midseason: Is Justin Herbert broken beyond repair? Can DK Metcalf get right? – NFL.com COOPER DEJEAN — What’s the problem? A first-team All-Pro selection in 2025, DeJean has struggled in his transition from nickel to safety this season. The Eagles have used the third-year pro as a starting safety in their base defense to leverage his athleticism, range and ball skills in the deep half. While DeJean has continued to make plays in coverage, particularly in the slot, he has struggled with his tackling in the hole from the safety spot. With a missed-tackle percentage of 21.3%, per Next Gen Stats, DeJean’s struggles with angles and wrapping up have contributed to the Eagles’ surprising defensive woes. Will he bounce back in 2026? DeJean is too talented to let his slump drag on through the end of the season. The athletic defender will eventually adjust to the different angles and figure out the contact balance needed to knock running backs off their pins in the hole. Whether he spends more time on the practice field hitting the tackling dummy or taking the “banana” route (an inside-out angle to the ball-carrier), DeJean will find a way to reduce his missed tackles with more experience and better technique. Given how quickly he became an NFL star as a slot defender, it is too soon to write off the 23-year-old as a failed safety. Nick Sirianni explains decision for Eagles QB change – BGN “Every second that goes by in a situation like that, that you can hold onto information as long as you possibly can, is a little less time for the opponent to get ready for the game. I know there’s a lot of interest in everything that you all want to hear, the fans want to hear. My job is to win football games, do everything we can do to help win football games, protect the guys here on this football team, and handle everything that I can inside.” Fantasy football start/sit advice for Week 9 at QB, RB, WR, TE – SB Nation Malachi Fields, Giants at Eagles. Will JJ McCarthy continue his strong play this week in Philadelphia? Maybe, but I do think he’s going to give his receivers chances to make explosive plays either way. And the Eagles pass defense has been bad this season. Philly has allowed the third-most receptions, second-most yards, third-most touchdowns, and the most fantasy points to wide receivers through eight games. Malik Nabers says he will play, but he is dealing with a knee injury that has kept him out of practice. Isaiah Likely is high on the pecking order as well, but the Eagles have been tougher on tight ends, allowing the sixth-fewest fantasy points to the position. Eagles’ Tanner McKee: Expected to suit up Sunday – CBS Sports McKee is listed as questionable for Week 9 due to what the report notes is “a cracked rib sustained on the first drive” in Week 8, but it appears he is feeling good enough to suit up. Joe Milton is set to start for the Eagles, so even if McKee is in uniform as anticipated, McKee will open the contest in a reserve role. Game Preview – NYG at PHI – Iggles Blitz Milton is a good athlete so the Eagles could mix in designed runs or just go with RPOs. He has a big time arm so they could try to dial up more deep shots. None of this will mean much unless the Eagles OL does their part. They were not good enough last week. That has to change. The Giants run defense hasn’t been good this season. They don’t have good DTs. Saquon Barkley isn’t 100 percent, but he should play. He’ll have a chance to be productive if the guys up front do their jobs. A good run game would be a huge help for Milton. This really is a can’t lose situation if you think about it. If Milton plays okay and the Eagles win, you get to enjoy a W. If he stinks and the Eagles lose, you move closer to a Top 5 pick. The Eagles haven’t lost a home game to the Giants since 2013. We’ll see if that streak continues. Win or lose, let’s hope the Eagles entertain us for three hours. Eagles vs. Giants score predictions: Why our beat writers like New York in NFC East clash – The Athletic At 2-6, the Eagles are teetering on a lost season. Sunday’s game might be their final chance to convince anyone they still have a chance in the NFC East. What has Fangio made of Mukuba’s season so far? “Overall good,” Fangio said. “Again, some plays that he’d like to have back, but I think he’s a good young player that’s going to be a good player in this league for a long time.” For Fangio, that’s high praise. Mukuba is a second-year safety who has struggled at times this season. But Fangio’s saying he’s going to be a good player in the league for a long time didn’t go unnoticed. Especially not by Mukuba. “It just means that he has a lot of confidence and belief in me,” Mukuba said. “I’ve got to just feed off of that and keep building.” Game Preview vs. Giants: Six storylines to follow Sunday – PhiladelphiaEagles.com This game is big in the NFC East. This is the final game for the Eagles before the bye week and it’s crucial. It is the third straight game within the division, one the Giants lead with a 4-2-1 record. The Eagles are looking to get back in the win column and establish themselves in the division heading into the second half of the season. Any other storylines? There are always the numbers that matter – turnover battle, red zone, penalties, special teams hidden yardage – and don’t change week to week. Philadelphia has won 13 straight games (including playoffs) against the Giants dating back to the 2014 campaign. Former Eagles Special Teams Coordinator and Secondary Coach John Harbaugh has had early success with the Giants, as expected. New York is physical, fired up, and confident. The Eagles need to play 60 minutes of good football to win this game. 3 ‘things I think’ before Giants-Eagles: Critical 5-day stretch has arrived – Big Blue View If the Commanders can defeat the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, it is possible Washington emerges as the biggest threat to the Giants in the division. A split of the Eagles and Commanders games wouldn’t be devastating, but it would make the path to the playoffs more treacherous for the Giants. Losing both games would bring serious questions regarding whether the Giants are actually ready to capitalize on the opportunity they have. In-between, of course, is the trade deadline. Will the Giants get Jonathan Taylor? A lesser back to supplement what they have? Help at defensive tackle? How much will they be willing to give up to get any of that? Buckle up, Giants fans. title: Nick Sirianni explains decision for Eagles QB change
summary: The Eagles added Joe Milton to the roster just a few weeks ago, but he’s already getting an opportunity to turn things around for a struggling Philadelphia offense. Head coach Nick Sirianni spoke to reporters on Friday and explained their decision to promote Milton and demote Tanner McKee in the process. “Obviously, that’s always a […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The Eagles added Joe Milton to the roster just a few weeks ago, but he’s already getting an opportunity to turn things around for a struggling Philadelphia offense. Head coach Nick Sirianni spoke to reporters on Friday and explained their decision to promote Milton and demote Tanner McKee in the process. “Obviously, that’s always a difficult thing to think through because it isn’t ever just on one person. Matter of fact, I think Tanner [McKee] played solid, but this is just what I felt like we needed to do right at this particular moment to give ourselves the best chance to win this weekend.” Sirianni went on to say that Milton is talented and has been in Philly for a couple weeks, they’ve seen that he has a talented arm and is a talented athlete that can process and make decisions. “Just a lot of good qualities that [Joe Milton] has. I like his confidence and everything that he brings, and it’s been fun getting to know him and working with him.” The head coach also explained that they felt it was best to make the move now instead of waiting for the bye week, because they are doing everything they can to win each and every game. “At the end of the day, I have to make the decision based off of that. But every decision that we make, we talk through in great, great detail. Obviously, Howie [Roseman] and I talk in great detail, the offensive staff and I, Parks [Frazier] and Sean [Mannion] and everybody. We just talk through it. At the end of the day, my job as the head coach is to make these decisions that I think is best for the football team, but you discuss everything with everybody.” Sirianni was asked about comments on Monday in support of Tanner McKee keeping his job. He revealed that they were fresh off the Sunday night game, and that was the initial plan, but after looking through the film and planning for the next game, they went in another direction. He also confirmed that while they made a change at quarterback, they did not make any changes to coaches roles. The head coach talked about how they look at everything when evaluating players, including that McKee was leading an offense decimated by injuries. Still, he noted that everyone still has to the best with whatever their circumstances may be, but they evaluate everyone fairly. Sirianni also threw his support to the entire QB room, saying he has always believed in the players they have at the position. He also defended his decision to withhold the information that they were making a change at quarterback, saying that he only tells the media what he wants, and that kind of decision is something he’ll want to hold onto for as long as possible. “Every second that goes by in a situation like that, that you can hold onto information as long as you possibly can, is a little less time for the opponent to get ready for the game. I know there’s a lot of interest in everything that you all want to hear, the fans want to hear. My job is to win football games, do everything we can do to help win football games, protect the guys here on this football team, and handle everything that I can inside.” Not that it would be a competitive advantage, but Sirianni also hedged to confirm that McKee will relegate to the backup position, saying they’ll see how it goes — the other QB on the roster is rookie Cole Payton, so it seems silly to suggest McKee won’t be QB2.

title: Eagles News: Joe Milton has “a f***ing cannon” of an arm
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Hope to see the Eagles try to put Joe Milton’s arm strength to use by having him take some deep shots. Also, a more general thought on Milton: I wonder if him playing well could actually reflect poorly on the coaching […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 18: Joe Milton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks to pass against the Carolina Panthers prior to an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on October 18, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Hope to see the Eagles try to put Joe Milton’s arm strength to use by having him take some deep shots. Also, a more general thought on Milton: I wonder if him playing well could actually reflect poorly on the coaching staff if it’s like Nick Foles said about it being a good thing that he doesn’t know the scheme well. Will be interesting to see what he can do in terms of making plays out of structure vs. what he’s asked to do within the scheme. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles notebook: Meet Joe Milton, the cannon-armed, rabbit-chasing quarterback tasked with resetting a lost season – PHLY Eagles “He’s a confident dude,” Steen said. “He’ll let you know. I like that. Everybody can tell you that he’s extremely gifted, so his confidence is cool to see. Especially for a dude that just got here, it’s pretty cool to see.” Jordan Mailata added, “Have you seen his arm? It is a fucking cannon — pardon my language. You see it on TV, you hear about it when he was going through the draft, but when you see it, it’s a work of art. … He’s really a team guy, he’s very open, talks to everyone. It’s a welcome sight because, with everything going on, he brings a good light to it.” In his limited playing time, that confidence has often manifested in him doing back flips in full pads to celebrate touchdowns in games, during the Senior Bowl in 2024, or, frankly, just to show off to his teammates. “I haven’t seen that yet,” Steen said. “Hopefully we can see it on Sunday.” Eagles Film Review: Joe Milton is an easy player to get excited about – BGN I am not pretending Milton is a polished answer at quarterback. Obviously. The accuracy can be wildly inconsistent, and the bad plays are pretty rough. But there is legitimate talent here. He has a quick release, rare velocity, real downfield ability, and enough mobility to add a different dimension to the offense. The Eagles have spent too much of this season making the offense hard to watch. Milton gives them a chance to run more boot action, take vertical shots, and use the quarterback in the run game. Will it be messy? Almost certainly. It could completely suck, let’s be honest. This is a poorly schemed offense with a lot of talent issues right now. If they allow loads of unblocked pressure again, he probably won’t have a chance to succeed. Milton’s mobility may help him escape some of that pressure. But the protection and the play design still have to give him a chance to operate. Eagles-Giants preview: 5 things to watch – PhillyVoice 2) It appears that the Eagles are going to keep putting an injured Saquon Barkley on the field. It was reported last week that the Eagles are not trading Saquon Barkley at the trade deadline. Obviously, one of the takeaways from that stance is that Barkley is in the team’s long-term plans. Barkley has made clear that his body is not where it needs to be, but he has toughed it out and played anyway. He has hamstring and back injuries, and has clearly been in pain during games each of the last two weeks. In my opinion, in this lost season, it is malpractice not to protect Barkley, and the Eagles are playing with fire by continuing to put this star player in harm’s way. The risk is far higher than the reward. Barkley did not practice on Wednesday, but he was limited on Thursday and appears to be gearing up to give it another go on Sunday. Game Review – WAS 27, PHI 10 – Iggles Blitz DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks were out again. Makai Lemon went 6-57. He does a good job on short routes. He’s able to get open and catch the ball in traffic. Lemon had a gain of 20 on an intermediate catch and run. He had a chance for a downfield play along the sideline, but wasn’t able to make the grab. He got open. Just couldn’t finish it. That part of his game will need work. Darius Cooper went 2-19. Hollywood Brown went 2-17. Roob’s Eagles Observations: Life without Jalen Hurts just isn’t any fun – NBCSP THIS REALLY OUGHT TO BE IMPOSSIBLE: Maybe the most damning stat regarding the 2026 Eagles is that they’ve been outgained by an average of over 100 yards per game. How is that even possible? Through Week 8, the Eagles have allowed 2,938 yards and netted 2,122 yards for a difference of 816 yards – or 102 yards per game. That’s what happens when you’re ranked 32nd in the NFL in yards per game and 27th in yards allowed. This is the first time since 1971 – that was 55 years ago – the Eagles have been outgained by at least 100 yards per game through eight games. Also happened in 1937, 1938 and 1957. The 1930s were not good years for the Eagles. Neither is 2026. The Eagles have been outgained by at least 71 yards in each game during the six-game losing streak. They’ve been outgained by an average of 148 yards during these last six games, the most yards they’ve been outgained by in any six-game span since 1976. This is only the second time in franchise history they’ve been outgained by 70 or more yards in six games in a row. It also happened during the 2023 late-season collapse. Fun season. 2026 NFL trade deadline: Proposing deals for Tony Pollard, Riq Woolen, others – ESPN Chicago Bears get: CB Riq Woolen. Philadelphia Eagles get: 2027 fifth-round pick. Why this deal makes sense for both sides: The Bears already made an aggressive trade for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons — a game changer in the front — but they still need more top-end speed in the back end. Woolen brings the physical traits and boundary speed to play man coverage with his 6-foot-4 frame, plus he fits in coordinator Dennis Allen’s split-safety schemes as a ball disruptor (12 interceptions and 59 pass breakups in his career). For the Eagles, they get a Day 3 return on Woolen, who is set to be a free agent in 2027 after signing a one-year deal with Philly. What I’m hearing about Derrick Henry, Jonathan Taylor, Garrett Wilson rumors at the NFL trade deadline – The Athletic Why the Eagles made a QB change. The Eagles felt shortly after the loss to the Commanders that a change at quarterback was needed. Tanner McKee is 0-3 as a starter this season, and Philly needs something different from the position. This will technically be Joe Milton III’s first start, though he played all but three snaps of the Jerod Mayo finale in 2024 for the Patriots (more on that at the end of this column). Known for his rocket arm and physical attributes, Milton will certainly offer something different for the Eagles. “All I know is I see a guy back there where something is happening,” one team source says. Nick Sirianni admits that he misled reporters about quarterback situation – PFT That’s the most important thing to remember. Coaches lie whenever they feel like they have to. Despite that fact, reporters and fans routinely take their words at face value, swallowing the bullshit while saying, “Thank you, sir, may I have another?” So thank you, Nick, for making my job a little easier. In my first week of law school, one of the professors said, “The most important thing I can do for you is to give you a good crap filter.” Because crap is everywhere. Usually, the people spewing it don’t admit it. When they do, it provides a tangible reminder as to whatever they say in the future. For Sirianni, that’s the most problematic aspect of his decision to tell the truth about lying. There’s now an “Exhibit A” to which anyone and everyone can point as to anything and everything he says when assessing whether he’s being straight with reporters and, in turn, with fans. Meet Jalen Cyrus, the artist behind the viral Go Birds T-shirt – PhiladelphiaEagles.com Gameday drip is a huge deal.…

summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are 6-2 through their first eight games of their 2026 season and could be a very active team before the NFL’s November 10th trade deadline. While it might make more sense for the Steelers to add talent rather than sell, the Steelers are shopping around at least one of their veterans. Sports […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are 6-2 through their first eight games of their 2026 season and could be a very active team before the NFL’s November 10th trade deadline. While it might make more sense for the Steelers to add talent rather than sell, the Steelers are shopping around at least one of their veterans. Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer named Steelers veteran linebacker Cole Holcomb as a name that could be on the move before Tuesday’s deadline. “Then there’s the Steelers, who, again, are sniffing around at receiver, and could deal veteran LB Cole Holcomb,” Breer wrote. This season, the linebacker has played a very minimal role for Pittsburgh, recording just one tackle with four assisted. Holcomb has been with the Steelers since 2023. He suffered a knee injury that kept him out for the entire 2024 season. Although Holcomb just plays a backup role for the Steelers, it’s hard to imagine a team with a 42-year-old quarterback in position to make a playoff push and win their division for the second year in a row being willing to deal anyone who could potentially help them down the line. Pittsburgh’s inside linebacker play has exceeded expectations this season, with Payton Wilson and Patrick Queen both putting forth arguably their best seasons with the team. Beyond Wilson and Queen, the depth is lacking at the position overall. As the deadline draws near, it would not be shocking at all to see Pittsburgh make at least one move to improve their team. Despite their strong start to the season, at least one NFL insider suggests that the Steelers could sell one of their defensive veterans. Let us know what you think in the comments . full_text: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Pittsburgh Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker was fined $17,911 for his hit on Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson. Brisker was flagged for roughing the passer due to a blow to the head and neck area. Brisker was adamant that the call was an incorrect one after the game, and poked fun at Watson for complaining to the officials. “I think it’s just babying the quarterback. He’s laying there and crying or whatever he’s doing.,” Brisker said . “It is what it is… “He had his binky today.“ What is a bit surprising is that Steelers guard Mason McCormick was not fined for body slamming Browns edge rusher Jared Verse, at least not at the time of writing. summary: Is it too early to talk about the NFL Draft? full_text: Photo by Soobum Im/Getty Images | Getty Images Is it too early to talk about the NFL Draft? There are always those that say “never,” but for many, draft season doesn’t start until the Steelers have played their last snap of the season in the early months of the new year. However, Pittsburgh’s bye week always presents a good time to take a step back from the storylines of the current season and evaluate the bigger picture. Just how good are the Steelers ? What are their biggest roster needs? And who are some early targets in the upcoming 2027 draft? With no game this weekend to distract from, here are six recent national NFL mock drafts and the Steelers’ projected first-round selection in each. You can click on each pick’s heading to read the full draft and see who was available when Pittsburgh was “on the clock.” Let’s dive in: Pick 27: Dante Moore, QB, Oregon Fox Sports’ Rob Rang: Given the investment made in Drew Allar last spring, I don’t believe the Steelers are planning to draft a quarterback in the first round of the 2027 draft. However, should an abbreviated 2026 season push Dante Moore — the most talented passer in this class — far enough down the board, it would make sense for Pittsburgh to adjust its plan. Pick 27: Ellis Robinson IV, CB, Georgia A to Z Sports’ Kyle Crabbs and Rob Gregson: While Jamel Dean, Asante Samuel Jr. and Daylen Everette have done a nice job this season, Ellis Robinson IV would transform that secondary. He’s one of the most complete corners in this class, and he plays with a physicality and tenacity that scream Pittsburgh. Pick 28: Trinidad Chambliss, QB, Ole Miss CBS Sports’ Ryan Wilson: The Steelers need a QB. This is not up for debate. But do they roll with ’26 third-rounder Drew Allar? Would, say, 6-foot-4 Austin Simmons make more sense here? Or does Mike McCarthy roll the dice on Chambliss, who is not 6-foot but has played a lot of high-level SEC football and is a proven winner? Pick 22: Kelley Jones, CB, Mississippi State USA Today’s Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Grappling with the likes of Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins is never fun for opponents. That’s the Steelers’ reality for the foreseeable future, however, and sending off Joey Porter Jr. only complicates that task. At 6-4 and 205 pounds, Jones combines the size to pester both well-built receivers and the speed to stick close by each one. Pick 28: Jadan Baugh, RB, Florida Sports Illustrated’s Justin Melo: The Pittsburgh Steelers will probably transition to Will Howard or Drew Allar at quarterback next season. They should explore their potential post-Aaron Rodgers before spending another pick at quarterback. They could help their young starter by adding a workhorse running back like Florida’s Jadan Baugh. Pick 28: Tae Johnson, S, Notre Dame NFL Stock Exchange’s Connor Rogers: “I think (the Steelers) offensive line has a lot of young talent, and it feels like they’re probably pretty excited about Drew Allar after Aaron Rodgers — I’m not really thinking quarterback here yet. … I literally looked up DK (Metcalf’s) contract wondering about (drafting Texas’ Cam Coleman), but it’s not pretty, so it’s not happening here. … But when you watch Tae Johnson’s 2025 tape, it’s game-changing safety-level stuff. If he’s healthy and comes back this year and returns to the form he had last year, this is well worth this selection. The Steelers are currently on track to pick in the late-20s of the first round. Currently, the team has nine picks in 2027: one each in Rounds 1 and 2, two in Round 3, none in Round 4, one in Round 5 and two each in Rounds 6 and 7. The Steelers are not projected to earn any compensatory picks in 2027 according to Over the Cap. Which of the above players caught your eye the most? Which position do you think the Steelers will target in the first round? Want to make any way-too-early predictions yourself? Join the BTSC community and let us know in the comments.

title: Seahawks sign Deven Eastern, will only have 2 quarterbacks active vs. Cardinals
summary: The Seattle Seahawks had an open roster spot entering Saturday due to the release of running back Velus Jones Jr, who subsequently signed to the practice squad. Seattle opted to go into the defensive trenches to fill that vacant 53-man roster spot, signing rookie defensive tackle Deven Eastern. With Leonard Williams and Brandon Pili both […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks had an open roster spot entering Saturday due to the release of running back Velus Jones Jr, who subsequently signed to the practice squad. Seattle opted to go into the defensive trenches to fill that vacant 53-man roster spot, signing rookie defensive tackle Deven Eastern . With Leonard Williams and Brandon Pili both out with injury, Seattle’s defensive interior is significantly compromised. Eastern had an up-and-down and injured preseason, but at this stage the Seahawks need any bodies to get through the next couple of games before their Week 11 bye. Seattle also elevated swing tackle Bobby Hart and wide receiver Montorie Foster Jr from the practice squad for a second consecutive week. With Charles Cross and Rashid Shaheed both out, Hart and Foster get the call-ups again, leaving them each with one PS elevation left. What is the most notable aspect of Saturday’s roster transactions is the fact that quarterback Adrian Martinez was not signed to the active roster as an emergency third-stringer. By NFL rule, only players on the active roster can be an emergency third QB, so Martinez would’ve needed to be signed to the 53 from the practice squad to be eligible. Instead, he’s not going to be available on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, so Drew Lock and Jalen Milroe are it for the Seahawks. If they both get hurt, your guess is as good as mine as to who the third QB is.

full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 20: Jaxon Smith-Njigba #11 of the Seattle Seahawks celebrates with Drew Lock #2 after scoring a touchdown during the third quarter of the game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks return to Lumen Field on Sunday to face the Arizona Cardinals in a divisional matchup with plenty of betting opportunities. Seattle enters as an 8.5-point favorite, with the game total set at 39.5 points, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The Seahawks have had an inconsistent season, but Arizona’s defensive struggles create some interesting opportunities on both sides of the ball. The Cardinals have allowed 29 touchdowns through eight games, the most in the NFL. That could open the door for Seattle’s offense, particularly in the red zone. Here are four bets/game picks worth considering ahead of Sunday’s game. 1. Jadarian Price Anytime Touchdown Scorer (+180) Jadarian Price is an interesting option to find the end zone against Arizona. The rookie has shown the potential to turn an ordinary running lane into a big play, and Seattle’s recent investment in its offensive line could help him find more opportunities to showcase that ability. Against a defense that has struggled throughout the season, those opportunities could translate into a touchdown. There is one important caveat, though: Price needs to take better care of the football. His fumbles have been a concern, and another mistake could limit his opportunities. If he can protect the ball, his explosiveness gives him a legitimate chance to make an impact on the scoreboard. 2. Trey McBride Over 59.5 receiving yards Trey McBride is one of the most reliable pass-catching tight ends in the NFL, and Seattle has historically struggled to contain him. The coverage behind Seattle’s linebackers has been a recurring issue, particularly when opponents attack the intermediate areas of the field. McBride is exactly the type of player who can take advantage of that weakness. He’s a dependable target, consistently finds space in coverage and gives his quarterback a reliable option when the pocket gets uncomfortable. Arizona should have plenty of reasons to involve him throughout the game, especially if Seattle prioritizes preventing explosive plays elsewhere. 3. Jaxon Smith-Njigba Anytime Touchdown Scorer (-125) Jaxon Smith-Njigba should be one of Drew Lock’s most important weapons on Sunday. The two have shown good chemistry, and that connection could become particularly valuable against an Arizona defense that has struggled to consistently defend the passing game. Smith-Njigba can help Seattle address one of its biggest offensive concerns: finishing drives in the red zone. He was an important part of the solution in the first meeting between these teams, and the Seahawks should look to get him involved again when the field becomes shorter. His value isn’t limited to the red zone, either. Smith-Njigba has also been a dangerous deep threat throughout the season, capable of creating separation and turning downfield opportunities into explosive plays. That versatility makes him an especially valuable target for Lock, who will need reliable options to keep the offense moving. With their established chemistry and JSN’s ability to contribute at every level of the field, there’s a good case for backing him to find the end zone. 4. Seahawks -8.5 (-110) This might be the most difficult bet to evaluate, largely because of the uncertainty surrounding Drew Lock. However, I don’t see much of a middle ground in this matchup. If Lock struggles, Seattle could have a difficult afternoon. Turnovers, particularly interceptions, could give Arizona short fields and keep the Cardinals in a game where they might otherwise struggle to keep pace offensively. On the other hand, Lock could deliver another performance similar to his first meeting against Arizona. If he protects the football, establishes a rhythm with Smith-Njigba and takes advantage of Seattle’s improved offensive line, the Seahawks have enough talent to win comfortably and cover the spread. The Cardinals’ defensive struggles make the second scenario entirely possible. Seattle has the weapons to create separation on the scoreboard, but everything depends on which version of Lock shows up. I’m willing to take the risk because I believe Seattle has a significant advantage if its quarterback plays a clean game. Drew Lock will make his second start this season, taking on the Arizona Cardinals once again. But the mystery of the elbow injury has now been solved, per Tom Pelissero. More in The Sweep: https://t.co/2WjDotsn76 pic.twitter.com/shgYQc9NTO — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 7, 2026 Lock’s availability was also somewhat in question this week, due to the tendinitis issue, but he apparently looked good enough in limited practice appearances to lead Seattle into a Week 9 divisional matchup. Lock made two appearances to start the season, posting a 127.3 passer rating (would lead the NFL if he had enough throws to qualify), 73% completion rate, 422 yards, 4 touchdowns and 0 interceptions. The hot start, coupled with turnover struggles from Sam Darnold, have had some fans clamoring to leave the backup inserted as the starter. A strained quad for Darnold will cause this idea to come to fruition for one week. The Arizona Cardinals defense has allowed the 2nd-most fantasy points to the QB position, so it will be interesting to see if big Lock lights it up again. Will the Seattle decision makers choose to ride the hot hand if the offense looks effective again, against a low-end opponent? Those are questions for another day.
