title: NFL Week 9 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines, TD scorers, more
summary: QB controversy in Minnesota? Browns upsetting the Saints? Touchdowns for two rookie RBs? Let's predict 15 things for Week 9.
full_text:
Week 9 of the  2026 NFL season is underway after the Jaguars easily handled the Ravens on  Thursday night . But what will happen in the remaining 14 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

 First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

 Can the Browns bounce back with an upset win over the Saints? Will rookie running backs Jonah Coleman  (Broncos) and  Kaelon Black  (49ers) score touchdowns this weekend? Does Colts WR Keenan Allen have fantasy potential against the Cowboys? And could  Carson Wentz cause some QB controversy in Minnesota?

 Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Upset picks | Projected stat lines 
 Fantasy sleepers, surprises 
 TD scorers | Other predictions 

 
 

 Maldonado predicts two upsets 
 

 Green Bay Packers +3 (+140 moneyline) at New England Patriots 

 Green Bay's defense can take away the throws driving New England quarterback  Drake Maye 's hot streak in Sunday's game . On passes traveling 10-plus yards, the Packers have allowed just two touchdowns and snagged seven interceptions.

 Maye could still hurt the Packers with his legs, but his receiving group is banged up -- the Patriots are again without  A.J. Brown , who has played just 26% of their offensive plays this season. On the other end, Green Bay quarterback  Jordan Love  can create enough big plays throwing to  Christian Watson and Matthew Golden  to win outright.

 
 

 

 Cleveland Browns +3 (135 moneyline) at New Orleans Saints 

 Quarterback Tyler Shough has cooled off after leading the NFL in passing yards through the first two weeks. His early production depended heavily on passing volume while trailing, and that volume has dropped substantially.

 Cleveland's strong pass defense and top-10 pressure rate make this a difficult spot for Shough to rebound Sunday . The Saints are much easier to attack on the ground, giving Browns RB Quinshon Judkins a chance to keep QB Shedeur Sanders and the offense more balanced. Cleveland's protection is a concern, but its defense can keep this ugly.

 

 

 Walder predicts three stat lines 
 

 Alim McNeill , DT, Detroit Lions : 1.5 sacks, 5 pressures, 25% pass rush win rate

 McNeill, who has 4.5 sacks on the season, leads all defensive tackles in pass rush win rate. And he has an excellent chance to convert that into sacks Sunday because Miami quarterback  Malik Willis has been sacked on 9.3% of his dropbacks this season -- third highest among qualifying quarterbacks. Plus, even if guard Kadyn Proctor returns from a concussion this week, all three members of the Dolphins' interior line are either average or below average in pass block win rate.

 
 

 Jonah Coleman , RB, Denver Broncos : 15 carries, 79 rushing yards, 4 receptions, 29 receiving yards, 1 touchdown

 Coleman looks well positioned to follow up his productive game against the Chiefs with another strong performance against the Panthers . Carolina's run defense isn't good, ranking 26th in EPA allowed per designed carry, 28th in yards allowed per carry, 24th in yards before contact allowed per carry and 28th in yards after contact allowed per carry.

 But it's more than that. The Panthers also have a run-inducing defense, with the sixth-lowest pass rate over expected against them, per NFL Next Gen Stats. That means Coleman's rushing attempts should go up.

 
 

 Sauce Gardner , CB, Indianapolis Colts : 34 coverage snaps, 4 targets, 2 receptions allowed, 17 receiving yards allowed

 Gardner had a rough start to the season, though NFL Next Gen Stats' metrics and player-tracking work I've done suggest he played sticky coverage and simply gave up a couple more catches than expected. Regardless, he has played better recently, allowing a tiny 0.3 yards per coverage snap over the past three games and almost getting an interception last week .

 Gardner should mostly face off against Cowboys WR  George Pickens , who is coming off a two-reception performance against the Cardinals . Sunday's game  could mark another strong performance for the fifth-year cornerback.

 

 

 Moody predicts three fantasy sleepers 
 

 Keenan Allen , WR, Indianapolis Colts (43.6% rostered in ESPN leagues) 

 Allen caught seven passes for a team-high 67 yards  last week in Jacksonville and leads the Colts with 34 receptions this season. On Sunday , he'll face a Cowboys defense that has allowed the seventh-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers.

 Allen has scored just one touchdown this season, but his reception volume (at least six catches in four games) makes him a viable flex option in deeper leagues. He has scored at least nine fantasy points in three of his past four games, including one with 16.2 points.

 

 
 

 Malik Willis , QB, Miami Dolphins (16.0%) 

 Despite Miami's struggles on offense, Willis has scored at least 18 fantasy points in two of his past three games. His rushing ability has helped, with 225 yards and three touchdowns on the ground this season. All of that makes him one of my favorite Week 9 streamers, especially against a Lions defense that has allowed the most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks. Willis is worth holding on to even after this week, as Miami will face weak defenses in the Colts, Bills and Jets.

 
 

 Devin Singletary , RB, New York Giants (9.9%) 

 Courtesy of a 2-yard touchdown run  against the Texans in Week 7 , Singletary turned eight touches into 14.5 fantasy points. He could see more work this Sunday against the Eagles , as  Tyrone Tracy Jr . is on IR ( hamstring ) and  Cam Skattebo  -- who has had fumbling issues -- is doubtful to play ( hamstring ).

 The matchup against Philadelphia is also encouraging. The Eagles have allowed the fifth-most rushing yards per game and 10 rushing touchdowns this season. Singletary should be on the flex radar for fantasy managers in deeper leagues.

 

 

 Bowen predicts three touchdown scorers 
 

 Tee Higgins , WR, Cincinnati Bengals 

 Higgins has caught at least one touchdown in back-to-back games, and he has seen a total of 18 targets during that stretch. In a Cincinnati offense that must be more pass-heavy due to a lack of rushing efficiency, Higgins will get opportunities versus a Falcons defense that plays man-free coverage (man coverage with a safety in the middle) on 41.8% of opponent dropbacks, the second-highest rate in the league. Look for quarterback Joe Burrow  to target Higgins on those one-on-one matchups.

 
 

 Malachi Fields , WR, New York Giants 

 Fields has just one touchdown reception on the season ( Week 4 against the Cardinals ), but he caught four of five targets for 83 yards from quarterback J.J. McCarthy in Week 7 . With his physical profile, Fields can create favorable matchups for himself on the boundary. And he did see an end zone target from McCarthy in their last game before the bye. Let's take Fields to score on a fade route against the Eagles.

 
 

 Kaelon Black , RB, San Francisco 49ers 

 Black scored his first NFL touchdown in a Week 7 loss to the Falcons , and he has seen his role expand as a change-of-pace runner behind  Christian McCaffrey . Black has at least nine touches in each of his past two games, and the Week 9 matchup is perfect for him to find the end zone again. The Raiders are allowing 146.4 rushing yards per game, the second most in the league.

 

 

 

 Solak makes four more predictions 
 

 Vikings' Carson Wentz will create QB controversy 

 Expectations were high for quarterback Kyler Murray against a bad Lions secondary last week ... but the Lions' pass defense showed up despite a rough start to the season. With Murray laid up by a hamstring injury , backup Wentz gets an actually…

title: Weekly Patriots notes: What New England could do at the trade deadline, intel
summary: The Patriots will upgrade if they can before Tuesday's deadline, but it might be quiet. In fact, New England could even trade away someone like Christian Barmore.
full_text:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Quick-hit thoughts and notes around the New England Patriots and NFL:

 1. Deadline chatter: The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET, and fireworks aren't expected with the Patriots.

 There are multiple reasons, according to sources familiar with the team's thinking, and near the top of the list is the unwillingness to sacrifice significant assets from future Patriots teams. The club already did that in the offseason by trading a 2028 first-round pick and 2027 fifth-rounder for receiver A.J. Brown in June, which was part of an overall aggressive offseason.

 That doesn't mean avenues to bolster the injury-ravaged 2026 Patriots haven't and won't be explored, per sources, but any potential trade is more likely to mirror some of the modest moves from the Bill Belichick era. For example, acquiring outside linebacker Kyle Van Noy and a seventh-round pick at the 2016 deadline in exchange for a sixth-round pick is the type of move that could fit the team's approach, targeting depth at one of the current positions of need. It didn't generate big headlines at the time, but in retrospect, it might be the franchise's best deadline deal this century.

 

 The Patriots have about $5 million in salary cap space, some of which they'll need to account for standard in-season movement of players elevated from the practice squad and coming on and off injured reserve. Thus, they aren't positioned to take on a higher-salaried player without creating more cap space first. The Patriots are 12th in the NFL in cash spending this season, according to OverTheCap.

 They are also scheduled to depart for Munich on Wednesday in advance of next Sunday's game against the Detroit Lions , which adds a wrinkle to onboarding any potential acquisition by Tuesday's deadline.

 Another question that has lingered over the past week is the possibility of the 5-3 Patriots moving players. Sports Illustrated national NFL reporter Albert Breer said they have "listened and talked to other teams" about trading defensive tackle Christian Barmore , who is No. 3 on the depth chart and due to earn non-guaranteed salaries of $18 million in 2027 and $19 million in 2028, while counting for $23.6 million against the salary cap in 2027 and $24.6 million in 2028.

 Due to those higher salary and cap figures, and Barmore now playing behind starters Milton Williams and Cory Durden , his spot on the team could be in jeopardy after this season.

 The approaching trade deadline was noted in the locker room this past week by Patriots players, who said their primary focus is Sunday's home game against the Green Bay Packers (4:25 p.m. ET, Fox).

 "We see the reports. We see everything. Everybody has their phone. Once somebody posts something, it's on every app you can go to, or somebody will send it to you," said Williams, the sixth-year defensive tackle. "That's the NFL, the business that we're in. It's tough seeing guys you're going to war with mentioned in talks like that, but that just lets you know that nobody is safe in this business.

 "It will have different effects on different people. Some people take it better than others. I'm going to tell our guys, 'Use it as fuel, use it as motivation,' because I don't know where this information comes from. You just try to put your best foot forward every day, and when there are opportunities to make plays, make them, and I feel like the rest will take care of itself."

 

 2. Davis' rebound: Starting Patriots cornerback Carlton Davis III (neck) didn't finish last week's win over the Dolphins and appeared to be in pain en route to the locker room, but by the end of this week he felt ready to go against the Packers despite being listed as questionable. How did it happen?

 "There can be some truth to what was seen [in Miami], especially that being my first game back [after missing three weeks]. It was a physical game for me," Davis explained. "I had still kind of been dealing with the injury, but in this league you have to be able to roll with the punches. When you take off 3-4 weeks from football and it's your first time hitting/contact, it can be a little rough. You have to build that callous back up.

 "So I was a little hurt after the game, but it was more soreness than actually hurt. We have a great recovery team here. Getting in every day with the [athletic] trainers, and staying on top of it, has been huge in me being able to be out there with the team. And also for me mentally feeling ready to go."

 3. Flex timing: The NFL has until Nov. 17 at the latest to decide if the Patriots' Week 12 road game against the Chargers gets flexed out of Sunday night. The Chargers (0-7) host the Texans (2-5) this Sunday and then visit the Ravens (4-5) on "Monday Night Football" on Nov. 16.

 Would the league keep a winless team in primetime? One reason Patriots-Chargers might stay is because it is being played the week of Thanksgiving and there are fewer choices to move to Sunday night -- with a game Wednesday, three on Thursday, one on Friday and another Monday.

 4. Maye impression: Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon highlighted one of the main challenges in facing Patriots quarterback Drake Maye , noting Maye's ability to "get out of pressure, extend plays to throw and extend plays to run." He said he first saw glimpses of it during Maye's rookie season in 2024 when he started a late-season game against Gannon's Cardinals team, and described the most recent work of Maye -- who was named AFC Offensive Player of the Month -- as "lights out."

 To Gannon's point, Maye has five straight games with at least three passing or rushing touchdowns, the longest streak by any quarterback since the start of last season and the second-longest streak in Patriots history behind Tom Brady's 10 straight in 2007.

 

 5. IR designations: The Patriots have used four IR designations to return -- on offensive tackle Marcus Bryant , receivers A.J. Brown and Mack Hollins , and center/guard Greg Van Roten -- which means they have just four remaining for the regular season. They would get an additional two in the playoffs should they qualify. Who gets them?

 Starting left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and starting receiver Romeo Doubs (shoulder) project as locks. Meanwhile, fullback Reggie Gilliam (knee/ankle), safety Dell Pettus (ankle), linebacker Khalil Jacobs (undisclosed) and outside linebacker Quintayvious Hutchins (knee) are others on IR who have been present in the locker room during media-access periods.

 6. Elite Elliss: When Patriots defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr was asked last week about blue-chip players on his unit, and whether there was a player who might be overlooked in the media, he said he could pick a lot of them but mentioned starting linebacker Christian Elliss  specifically. "That's really the type of guy we love to coach here," he said of Elliss, who leads the team in tackles (60) and worked his way up from core special teamer to defensive stalwart.

 7. Packers WRs: The Packers lead the NFL with 33 completions of 20 or more yards, and Patriots practice squad receivers Kyle Dixon and Chandler Brayboy felt that this past week. Dixon played the role of Christian Watson (42 catches, 708 yards, 16.9 avg.) in practice, while Brayboy was Matthew Golden (43 catches, 619 yards, 14.4 avg.). "Tiring week," Dixon said with a smile. "All those downfield routes."

 8. Brady's presence: Rob Gronkowski was inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame on Saturday, and one of the notable parts of the weekend was having Brady in attendance, with the schedule working out because Brady was in town to call the Packers-Patriots game for Fox the next day. This was the first Patriots Hall of Fame ceremony Brady has attended since leaving the franchise in 2020, other than his own.

 9. They said it: "Now I call New England home. It really is a home for me and always will be for the rest of my life." -- Gronkowski, who still has a residence in…

title: The New York Giants 'don't care' that they're NFC East favorites
summary: It's an unfamiliar role for a franchise that hasn't claimed the NFC East crown since 2011.
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- The tides have turned in an upside-down NFC East. The New York Giants , once massive underdogs to win the division, are now the favorites. 
 
 It's an unfamiliar role for a franchise that hasn't claimed the NFC East crown since 2011. 
 
 "Yeah, I don't know. To me, it's all kind of meaningless," coach John Harbaugh said. "I mean, if you're betting, it's important, but it doesn't matter to us because there's still 10 games left to play. And I'm quite sure every one of the teams in the division believes that in those 10 games, they can make up ground. I've had experience with that in my coaching career. Players know that it's what you do; it's not what anybody says about you or where you get ranked or anything like that. It's just about what you do. You've got to go win games." 
 
 The Giants (4-2-1) still have to beat the Eagles in Philadelphia on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, Fox) for the first time in 13 years, but if they do, it will be the latest step in regaining legitimacy against their once-dominant rival. The Eagles have won the past two NFC East titles and five division championships since the Giants' last.   
 
 But with Philadelphia (2-6) decimated by injury and the surprising Giants off to a strong start in Harbaugh's first season, there is an unfamiliar pecking order in the division. Almost at the midway point of the season, New York has officially evolved into the favorite to win the NFC East. Perhaps even several weeks late with the Cowboys and Eagles struggling so badly. 
 
 "It doesn't mean anything," Giants right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor said. "All that stuff is for Vegas. Obviously, it was annoying that they kept saying other teams were favorites. But I think at this point, we just don't care. If you handle your business, you're going to win. The oddsmakers don't go out there on Sunday. If we continue winning, like I said, it handles itself." 
 
 
 
 The Giants are currently the only team in the NFC East with a winning record. The Cowboys (3-5) and Commanders (2-4-1) are struggling, much like the Eagles. It's not out of the realm of possibility that if the Giants go 4-6 in their final 10 games, they still manage to win the division. A record of 8-8-1 might get it done this season. 
 
 As a result, the Giants are currently -150 to win the NFC East, according to DraftKings sportsbook. The Cowboys are second at +245, while the Eagles are massive long shots at +3300, creating a true role reversal from recent years. 
 
 New York came into the season +600 and had a 12% chance to win the NFC East, according to ESPN Analytics. The Eagles were +120 and had a 44% chance to win the division. 
 
 The Giants were dealt the underdog card, but they didn't seem to agree. 
 
 "In my mind, I feel like every time we play, we should be the favorite," tight end Isaiah Likely said. "And that's just the mentality I have." 
 
 Likely came from Baltimore with Harbaugh where they won the division two of the past four seasons. The Giants, meanwhile, had become regular basement dwellers before Harbaugh's arrival. They finished last in the NFC East in five of the past nine seasons. 
 
 This four-day stretch when they play Sunday against the Eagles and Thursday night against the Commanders could signal a changing of the guard. It's an opportunity for the Giants to show they should be taken seriously, even with their third quarterback of the season, J.J. McCarthy , starting games. 
 
 "I think you can use these games to put the entire league on notice," Eluemunor said. 
 
 The Giants are also expected to add some sort of reinforcements prior to the trade deadline Tuesday. Among the players they've made an offer for is Colts running back Jonathan Taylor , sources told ESPN. 
 
 The rest of the division's struggles have certainly opened the door for the Giants to be aggressive. So far, they've taken advantage. New York already thrashed the Cowboys in the opener at MetLife Stadium. It was just their third win in 19 matchups with Dallas. 
 
 This is their chance to end the skid in Philadelphia and grab command of the division in a down year for the NFC East. 
 
 "Definitely," outside linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux said. "I think it's definitely when you get on a roll in football, you got to keep going. You don't want anything to stop your momentum because it's hard to get it back once you lose it." 
 
 Nobody knows for sure if this will stick with the Giants or it's a one-year hiatus for the Eagles. Just about everything has gone wrong this season in Philadelphia, including starting quarterback Jalen Hurts being out indefinitely because of blood clots in his lungs. 
 
 At least for now, the Eagles appear to be a team on the decline. The Giants, with a new coach and some exciting young talent, look like a team on the rise. Winning the division would be an accomplishment. NFC East titles matter to the executive level of the New York Football Giants organization.

title: Geno Smith has been upgrade from Justin Fields for Jets -- except in win column
summary: Smith statistically has outperformed Fields in New York, but they both only have two wins.
full_text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- A look at what's happening around the New York Jets :

 1. QB comp: The Jets can look at the Kansas City Chiefs ' sideline Sunday to remind themselves how much they've improved at quarterback. They will see Justin Fields , their former starter turned  Patrick Mahomes understudy.

 In 2024, the Jets brought in Fields in hopes to turn their fortunes around at quarterback, but they traded him to the Chiefs in March. 

 The Geno Smith -for-Fields decision has worked out nicely for the Jets, who found a competent "bridge" quarterback in the 36-year-old Smith.

 By every objective measure, not to mention the eye test, Smith has outperformed the 2025 Fields. But there's one caveat; more on that in a bit.

 This is a good time for a comparison because Smith already has played virtually the same number of snaps (494) as Fields did last season (501). Smith is far superior in QBR (59.7 to 39.2), completion percentage (69.0 to 62.7), passing yards (1,913 to 1,259) and touchdown passes (12 to 7).

 Fields had only one interception (Smith has three), but he wasn't nearly as aggressive as Smith, who's averaging 7.7 air yards per attempt -- a yard more than Fields. Fields had more rushing yards (383 to 46) but also more sacks (27 to 23). After some historically poor performances, Fields' mid-November benching surprised no one.

 As for Smith, coach Aaron Glenn loves the way he's pushing the ball downfield, especially on play-action.

 "[He's] really just finding his rhythm on who he is and what he does best," Glenn said of Smith, whose arrival via trade was a precursor to the Jets dealing Fields for a 2027 sixth-round pick.

 The QB swap looks even better when viewed through a financial lens. The Jets acquired Smith for a late-round pick swap and are paying him only $3.3 million for one year (the Las Vegas Raiders are on the hook for $16.2 million). Fields made $20 million last season, and he's costing the Jets another $8 million this year (the Chiefs are paying $3 million).

 An overpay for Fields. An underpay for Smith.

 All things considered, the Jets are getting bang for their current buck.

 "Geno is a better passer and better processor [than Fields], but sometimes you question his decision-making because he's so confident with his arm and his ability but less of an athlete," an AFC scout said. "Geno is a better quarterback; Justin is a better athlete."

 Ultimately, the quarterback's job is to get his team in the end zone (an old Bill Parcells-ism) and win games. This is where the Smith-Fields gap narrows considerably.

 The Smith-led Jets are 2-6, averaging 21.3 points per game. They were 2-7 in Fields' starts, with a 20.2 average. Pretty close. Too close.

 Simply put, they should be better than 2-6, but they haven't made enough winning plays in high-leverage situations. The Jets have five one-score losses (tied for the league lead), including four games in which Smith had a chance to take the lead or tie the game in the fourth quarter.

 Not all of those missed opportunities fall on Smith -- coaching is a factor, too -- but winning those games is part of the job description.

 

 2. Bro hug: After last week's loss, Smith and rookie Cade Klubnik shared a long embrace in the locker room -- a moment of consolation between quarterbacks.

 "It's a tough environment, and it's a very hard position to play and only so many can really do it," Klubnik said, explaining the motivation behind the hug. "There's not very many that can do it at the level he's doing it right now. The result of every game isn't just based off how the quarterback plays; it's a team effort. I just try to support him and always just be the best teammate and leader that I can for him."

 Klubnik, who has yet to play a snap, said he's learning a lot from Smith, noting his "fine-tuned" study schedule and preparation habits. The former Clemson star said he'll be ready if called upon.

 3. History on the horizon? With help from the Indianapolis Colts and Dallas Cowboys , the Jets could make draft history in April.

 No team in the common draft era (since 1967) has made three top-10 selections in a single draft. Right now, the Jets are holding the fourth (Colts), sixth (their own) and 10th (Cowboys) picks.

 That would cost owner Woody Johnson a pretty penny -- $144 million for those three guaranteed contracts, based on Spotrac projections.

 4. Muddled backfield: One of the big storylines Sunday will be the carry split between the red-hot Braelon Allen and the returning Breece Hall . There will be a plan, the Jets say.

 The "framework" is created by Glenn, according to offensive coordinator Frank Reich, who then huddles with running backs coach Nic McKissic to hammer out the details -- best plays for each player, down-and-distance, etc. They also will consider game flow -- hot hand, that sort of stuff.

 Look for something close to a 50-50 split.

 

 5. Tick, tick, tick: The trade deadline is 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday. Word is the Jets don't expect to be very active. Positions to watch -- they have a surplus of safeties, especially with the anticipated return of rookie  VJ Payne  coming perhaps next week. Conversely, they could use help for the injury-ravaged defensive line.

 One thing to remember, at 2-6, it's all about next season. They're not going to trade an asset that could help in the future.

 6. Green Ponds: On the surface, the lack of playing time for rookie cornerback D'Angelo Ponds is perplexing -- 61 defensive snaps, most of which came in Week 7 when starting nickelback Jarvis Brownlee Jr . was benched for disciplinary reasons.

 Ponds was drafted in the second round (50th). Glenn said it's not unusual for high picks to sit on the bench, mentioning Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (No. 1). That's an entirely different situation, of course.

 Know this, of the 34 defensive players selected in the first two rounds, the only one with fewer snaps than Ponds is Minnesota Vikings linebacker Jake Golday (18), who was drafted one spot after Ponds.

 Ponds got off to a slow start because he missed training camp with a calf injury. He's also learning a new position -- slot corner. At Indiana, he played outside corner. There are stark contrasts.

 "It's different, playing outside and going inside," Ponds said, "but I feel like I've got all the tools to do that."

 Glenn downplayed the playing-time issue, saying, "Guys, we can only play so many people." He preached patience, insisting Ponds will get his shot. That should come soon, especially since the Jets are falling out of contention.

 

 7. Red alert: Glenn said they're devoting more practice time to the red zone. Good idea, considering their touchdown efficiency inside the 20-yard line (42.3%) is the league's worst since the 2023 Jets (32.4%).

 8. Don't look now, but ...: Yes, the Jets have another interception drought -- four straight games without a pick. This comes after a historic 20-game drought was snapped in Week 4 by Minkah Fitzpatrick .

 In 25 games under Glenn, they have only one interception in 754 pass attempts. They only need 32 picks to catch up to the league-leading Jacksonville Jaguars  since Glenn's arrival.

 9. Not special anymore: The once-formidable special teams have slipped significantly, hitting rock bottom last week by allowing a 95-yard touchdown on a kickoff return -- the NFL's first of the season. The Jets are ranked 26th in kickoff coverage, 30th in punt coverage coming into Week 9.

 What gives? Start with personnel. 

 Two of their snap leaders from 2025, Isaiah Oliver and Mykal Walker , are gone. Kiko Mauigoa , Marcelino McCrary-Ball and Arian Smith -- core teamers -- are on injured reserve. Three of the players in coverage on the 95-yard touchdown are former starters who haven't played a lot of special teams -- Andre Cisco , Will McDonald IV and Trevin Wallace .
